title.zh-Hant: 普林斯頓建築本科作品集怎麼準備？錄取解析：要證明的不是「會做圖」，而是「會立論」
title.en: How to Prepare a Princeton Undergraduate Architecture Portfolio? An Admissions Reading: What You Have to Prove Is That You Can Make an Argument, Not That You Can Draw

summary.zh-Hant: 普林斯頓建築本科（A.B.）怎麼申請、作品集怎麼準備？整理官方 Arts Supplement 要求（最少 3 件、每件 100 字內說明、截止日），並以一份真實錄取作品集解析「立論」。
summary.en: How do you apply to Princeton's undergraduate architecture degree (A.B.), and how do you prepare the portfolio? This post gathers the official Arts Supplement requirements—a minimum of 3 works, a statement of no more than 100 words each, and the deadlines—and reads one real admitted portfolio for how it makes an argument.

tldr.zh-Hant: 普林斯頓建築本科（A.B. in Architecture）是預備專業學位，不直接對應執照，重視思考與研究。作品集要從問題出發、呈現研究過程，並回應功能、基地環境、社會意涵、技術與歷史理論五個面向——要證明你「會立論」，而不只是「會做圖」。
tldr.en: Princeton's undergraduate architecture degree (A.B. in Architecture) is pre-professional. It does not correspond directly to licensure, and it values thinking and research. A portfolio should start from a question, show the research process, and respond to five concerns—function, site and environment, social meaning, technology, and history and theory—so that it proves you can make an argument, and not only that you can draw.

body.zh-Hant:
今年我指導的一位學生拿到了普林斯頓大學建築系 A.B. in Architecture（建築學文學士）的錄取。很多家長第一個問題是：「作品集是不是要畫得很漂亮？」我的答案是：普林斯頓要你證明的不是「會做圖」，而是「會立論」——你能不能提出一個問題、用研究和設計把它論證清楚。

普林斯頓的建築本科（A.B. in Architecture）到底是什麼學位？

根據普林斯頓建築學院（School of Architecture）的官方說明，A.B. in Architecture 設在博雅教育（liberal arts）課程架構之中，屬於預備專業（pre-professional）學位：它不直接滿足建築師執照要求，而是為之後攻讀專業建築碩士（M.Arch）打基礎。

這一點決定了它看人的方式：它要的不是「已經很會畫施工圖」的學生，而是具備思考深度、能在人文、社會與技術之間建立連結的學生。

普林斯頓建築系的設計課（Studio）在訓練什麼？

官方把設計課定位為「a primary pedagogical framework to rehearse modes of architectural thought and research」——演練建築思考與研究方式的主要教學框架。也就是說，Studio 不是畫圖課，是思考與研究的排練場。

官方要求學生的 Studio 作品能展現對以下五個面向的理解：

  • 功能與使用（program）
  • 基地與環境（site / environment）
  • 社會政治意涵（sociopolitical implications）
  • 技術系統（technical systems）
  • 歷史與理論（history / theory）

課程內容涵蓋建築分析、建築表現、運算與建造技術；使用的媒材包括手繪草圖、數位製圖、實體與數位模型、列印輸出，以及線上與印刷媒體。

為什麼說普林斯頓要的是「會立論」？

看它的獨立研究要求就很清楚：

  • 大三獨立研究（Junior independent work）：一篇約 30 頁的論文。
  • 大四畢業論文（Senior thesis）：一整年、針對一個明確建築主題、論證充分的研究；可以用圖紙、模型、影片、攝影或電腦圖像來呈現，最後以公開口頭答辯收尾。

一個大學部建築學位，從大三開始就要求寫 30 頁論文、做一整年的論證型研究並公開答辯——這說明它從申請階段起，就在找能提出問題、組織論點、用設計去證明觀點的人。作品集裡只有漂亮的效果圖，是不夠的。

除了設計，普林斯頓還在意哪些能力？

官方說明裡反覆出現幾個關鍵詞：

  • 環境正義（environmental justice）：從社會、種族、政治、技術與科學等面向理解建築的影響。
  • 協作與清晰的口頭、書面表達。
  • 獨立研究、參與學術辯論與領導力。

換句話說，你的作品集和文書要能讓招生官看到：你關心建築背後的人與社會，你能寫、能說、能和別人一起做事。

普林斯頓建築本科怎麼申請？官方 Arts Supplement 要求一次看

以下為我在 2026-10-20 查核普林斯頓官方頁面整理的重點（申請前請再次以官網為準）：

  • 學位是 A.B.，不是 B.Arch：普林斯頓建築學院的大學部是四年制、以 liberal arts 為框架的預備專業教育，畢業取得 A.B. with a concentration in architecture，為研究所階段的建築或相關領域做準備（SoA 大學部說明）。
  • 先申請大學，再補交作品：建築作品是透過選填的 Optional Arts Supplement 提交；必須先向普林斯頓大學送出申請，才能在 Applicant Status Portal 上傳（官方 Arts Supplement 頁面）。主修建築須先修 ARC 203、ARC 204 兩門入門課。
  • 最少 3 件作品，不設上限：媒材不限（建築、設計、繪畫、陶藝、雕塑、版畫、攝影、木作等），不必每種都有；鼓勵提交作品集，也接受單張上傳。
  • 每件作品附：不超過 100 字的說明、完成日期；若為課堂作業，再加 1–3 句的作業說明。
  • 原創與誠信：合作作品須說明合作方式並標註所有參與者；任何 AI 的使用都須揭露並簡述。
  • 截止日：Single-Choice Early Action 為 11 月 6 日、Regular Decision 為 1 月 8 日、轉學為 3 月 9 日（皆為申請者當地時間 23:59）。

普林斯頓建築本科錄取作品集實例解析

下面是我指導的一位學生、獲普林斯頓建築本科錄取的作品集。它最值得學的不是技巧，而是每個項目都先有一個問題，再用分析、模型和圖去論證。每件作品都可以點進作品牆看完整頁面。

1. 從場地問題出發：把「沒人停留的街」變成論點

暑期項目從一條夾在建築背立面之間的街道開始：作品集先用分析指出問題——東西兩端高差達 3.5 公尺、午後大半被陰影遮蔽、沒有店面、街道更像服務通道而不是連結，人只是經過、很少停留。設計再分成三層回應：高架步道、以行人與綠化為優先的地面層，以及地下車道。

2. 立場先於造型：「不做新地標，而做調解者」

競賽項目分析了舊金山 UN Plaza：位置關鍵、卻是通道而非目的地。作品集用視線分析劃分空間，並明確寫出立場——在已有市政廳、歌劇院等地標的街區，這個設計不要成為新地標，而是讓不同來由的人相遇的「調解者」。這就是我說的「立論」：先回答「為什麼這樣做」，造型才有依據。

3. 把研究轉成空間：從繪畫、電影到科學資料

其餘作品示範了「研究 → 轉譯 → 模型」的完整路徑：

  • 線與色之屋：追蹤分析 Mondrian《Broadway Boogie Woogie》系列，提取比例、實虛、線與流動的關係，再轉成住宅的平面與剖面，最後做成實體模型。
  • 月球樞紐：以 NASA 關於月球熔岩管與坑洞的研究為起點，探討用月壤製成建材，構想含居住、實驗室、能源與種植的模組化社區。
  • 穿越第五維度：從電影《星際效應》的五維空間出發，先做 2D 抽象練習，再用木棒格架表現「時間的網格」、以鏡面表現無限維度。
  • 無限迴圈：記憶路徑：每段樓梯代表一個「選擇的節點」，外部規整的木框代表完整的自我，內部則是分岔而仍相連的路徑。
  • 生命孔洞：共生棲地：以珊瑚骨骼與神經網絡為參照，用 Voronoi 演算生成空間網絡，再以 3D 列印呈現。
  • 祥雲：從童年記憶中的窗花、雕花屏風出發，把光影與孔洞變成可以被個人辨認的空間。
  • 滑雪道：從自己參加滑雪比賽的經驗提出問題——非雪季如何維持訓練？——進而設計城市滑雪訓練基地，用螺旋結構讓教練與家長可以從各角度觀看。

另一件作品：看完整作品：祥雲 →。作品集最後還附了鋼筆、水彩、麥克筆繪畫與國畫作品，補足手繪與觀察能力。

總結這份作品集的共同結構：個人經驗或研究 → 明確問題 → 分析圖 → 空間轉譯 → 模型驗證。這正好對應官方要求的「每件作品不超過 100 字說明」——每個項目都說得出一句清楚的立論。

申請普林斯頓建築本科，作品集該怎麼準備？

把上面的官方要求翻譯成作品集策略，我的建議是：

  • 每個項目都從一個問題出發：不是「我做了一個房子」，而是「我想回答什麼問題」。
  • 把研究過程放進來：調研、分析、草圖、推演，讓評審看見你的思考路徑，而不只是結果。
  • 回應五個面向：功能、基地與環境、社會意涵、技術、歷史理論——不必每個項目都面面俱到，但整本作品集要看得出你理解建築不只是造型。
  • 媒材多元：手繪、模型、數位工具都可以，重點是媒材服務於論點。
  • 文字要清楚：簡短、精準地說明你的立論，這本身就是官方重視的書面表達能力。

普林斯頓的建築本科，適合的是想把建築當成一種思考方式的人。如果你的作品集能證明你「會立論」，你就已經站在對的起跑點上。
body.en:
This year, a student I mentored was admitted to the A.B. in Architecture (Bachelor of Arts in Architecture) at Princeton University. The first question many parents ask is: "Does the portfolio have to be beautifully drawn?" My answer is that what Princeton wants you to prove is that you can make an argument, not that you can produce drawings—whether you can pose a question and argue it clearly through research and design.

What degree is Princeton's undergraduate architecture (A.B. in Architecture), exactly?

According to the official description from Princeton's School of Architecture, the A.B. in Architecture sits within a liberal arts curriculum and is a pre-professional degree: it does not directly meet architect licensing requirements. It lays the foundation for later study toward a professional Master of Architecture (M.Arch).

That sets the kind of student it is looking for: someone with depth of thought who can connect the humanities, society, and technology, and not someone who is already highly skilled at construction drawings.

What does Princeton Architecture's design course (Studio) train?

The school defines the design course as "a primary pedagogical framework to rehearse modes of architectural thought and research"—a framework for rehearsing architectural thinking and research. Studio is not a drawing class. It is a rehearsal room for thinking and research.

Official guidance asks that a student's Studio work show an understanding of these five concerns:

  • Function and use (program)
  • Site and environment (site / environment)
  • Sociopolitical implications (sociopolitical implications)
  • Technical systems (technical systems)
  • History and theory (history / theory)

The curriculum covers architectural analysis, architectural representation, computation, and construction technology. The media used include hand sketches, digital drawings, physical and digital models, printed output, and online and print media.

Why say that what Princeton wants is the ability to make an argument?

The independent-research requirements make it plain:

  • Junior independent work: a paper of about 30 pages.
  • Senior thesis: a full year of well-argued research on a clearly defined architectural topic. It may be presented through drawings, models, film, photography, or computer images, and it closes with a public oral defense.

An undergraduate architecture degree that, from junior year, requires a 30-page paper, a full year of argument-driven research, and a public defense is, from the application stage onward, looking for people who can pose a question, organize an argument, and use design to prove a point. Beautiful renderings alone are not enough in a portfolio.

Beyond design, what other abilities does Princeton care about?

A few keywords come up again and again in the official description:

  • Environmental justice: understanding architecture's effects through social, racial, political, technical, and scientific lenses.
  • Collaboration and clear oral and written expression.
  • Independent research, taking part in academic debate, and leadership.

In other words, your portfolio and essays need to show an admissions officer that you care about the people and the society behind architecture, and that you can write, speak, and work with other people.

How do you apply to Princeton undergraduate architecture? The official Arts Supplement requirements at a glance

The points below are what I compiled from Princeton's official pages, checked on 2026-10-20 (please confirm again on the official site before you apply):

  • The degree is an A.B., not a B.Arch: undergraduate study at Princeton's School of Architecture is a four-year pre-professional education framed by the liberal arts. Graduates receive an A.B. with a concentration in architecture, in preparation for graduate study in architecture or a related field (SoA undergraduate overview).
  • Apply to the university first, then submit the work: architecture work is submitted through the optional Optional Arts Supplement. You must send an application to Princeton University before you can upload in the Applicant Status Portal (official Arts Supplement page). To concentrate in architecture, you must first take the two introductory courses ARC 203 and ARC 204.
  • A minimum of 3 works, with no maximum: any medium is allowed (architecture, design, painting, ceramics, sculpture, printmaking, photography, woodworking, and so on), and you do not need one of each. A portfolio is encouraged, and single-image uploads are also accepted.
  • With each work: a statement of no more than 100 words, and a completion date; if it is a class assignment, add 1–3 sentences describing the assignment.
  • Originality and integrity: collaborative work must explain how the collaboration was done and credit every participant. Any use of AI must be disclosed and briefly described.
  • Deadlines: Single-Choice Early Action is November 6, Regular Decision is January 8, and transfer is March 9 (all at 23:59 in the applicant's local time).

A reading of an admitted portfolio for Princeton undergraduate architecture

Below is the portfolio of a student I mentored who was admitted to Princeton undergraduate architecture. What is worth learning from it is not the technique. It is that every project starts with a question, then argues it through analysis, models, and drawings. Each work can be opened on the board for the full page.

1. Start from a site problem: turn "a street where no one stays" into an argument

The summer project begins with a street squeezed between the back elevations of buildings. The portfolio uses analysis to name the problem—the height difference between the east and west ends reaches 3.5 metres, most of the street is in shadow through the afternoon, there are no shopfronts, and the street feels more like a service passage than a connection. People only pass through, and they rarely stay. The design then answers in three layers: an elevated walkway, a ground level that puts pedestrians and planting first, and an underground roadway.

2. A position before the form: "not a new landmark, but a mediator"

The competition project analyzes San Francisco's UN Plaza: the location is critical, yet it is a route through rather than a destination. The portfolio uses sightline analysis to divide the space, and it states a position outright—on a block that already has landmarks such as City Hall and the opera house, this design should not become a new landmark. It should be a "mediator" where people who arrive for different reasons can meet. That is what I mean by making an argument: answer "why do it this way" first, and the form then has a basis.

3. Turn research into space: from painting and film to scientific data

The remaining works show the full path of "research → translation → model":

  • House of Lines and Colour: a close reading of Mondrian's Broadway Boogie Woogie series, drawing out the relationships of proportion, solid and void, line, and flow, then translating them into the plan and section of a house, and finally into a physical model.
  • Lunar Nexus: starting from NASA research on lunar lava tubes and pits, it explores making building materials from lunar soil and proposes a modular community with housing, a laboratory, energy, and planting.
  • Traversing the Fifth Dimension: starting from the five-dimensional space in the film Interstellar, it begins with a 2D abstract exercise, then uses a wooden-stick grid to represent "the grid of time" and mirrors to represent infinite dimensions.
  • Infinite Loop: Memory Paths: each flight of stairs stands for a "node of choice". The regular wooden frame on the outside stands for a complete self, and the inside is a set of paths that branch and stay connected.
  • Living Cavities: Symbiotic Habitat: taking coral skeletons and neural networks as references, it generates a spatial network with a Voronoi computation and presents it through 3D printing.
  • Auspicious Clouds: starting from the paper window patterns and carved screens of childhood memory, it turns light, shadow, and openings into a space a person can recognize as their own.
  • Ski Trail: drawing on the student's own experience competing in ski races, it asks a question—how do you keep training outside the snow season?—and then designs an urban ski-training base whose spiral structure lets coaches and parents watch from every angle.

Another project: See the full project: Auspicious Clouds →. The portfolio also ends with pen, watercolor, and marker drawings and traditional Chinese painting, which fill out the hand drawing and the ability to observe.

The shared structure of this portfolio is: personal experience or research → a clear question → analytical drawings → spatial translation → verification in the model. That lines up with the official requirement of "no more than 100 words of description per work"—every project can state its argument in one clear sentence.

When you apply to Princeton undergraduate architecture, how should you prepare the portfolio?

Turning the official requirements above into a portfolio strategy, my advice is:

  • Start every project from a question: not "I made a house", but "what question do I want to answer?"
  • Bring the research process in: investigation, analysis, sketches, and the steps of working the idea out, so reviewers see the path of your thinking and not only the result.
  • Respond to the five concerns: function, site and environment, social meaning, technology, and history and theory. No single project has to cover every one, but the portfolio as a whole should show that you understand architecture is more than form.
  • Use more than one medium: hand drawing, models, and digital tools all belong. The medium should serve the argument.
  • Write clearly: state your argument briefly and precisely. That is itself the written expression the school values.

Princeton undergraduate architecture suits people who want to treat architecture as a way of thinking. If your portfolio can prove that you can make an argument, you are already on the right starting line.

title.zh-Hant: 康乃爾建築本科為什麼地位這麼穩？AAP 五年制 B.Arch. 優勢、和萊斯比較與申請門檻
title.en: Why Has Cornell Undergraduate Architecture Held Its Standing So Steadily? The AAP Five-Year B.Arch. Advantages, a Comparison with Rice, and the Admissions Bar

summary.zh-Hant: 康乃爾 AAP 建築本科強在哪？整理五年制 B.Arch.、NAAB 與 STEM 認證、羅馬與紐約學期、和萊斯的差別、2026 年最新申請門檻（SAT/ACT 必交、4 年數學），並以錄取作品對照 AAP 重視的七種特質。
summary.en: What makes Cornell AAP undergraduate architecture strong? This post gathers the five-year B.Arch., NAAB accreditation and STEM designation, the Rome and New York semesters, the differences from Rice, and the latest 2026 admissions requirements (SAT or ACT required, 4 years of mathematics), and sets admitted work against the seven qualities AAP values.

tldr.zh-Hant: 康乃爾 AAP 建築本科是五年制、NAAB 認證、STEM 認證的專業學位 B.Arch.：前三年核心課、後四學期跨領域深化，約 1/4 課程可跨院修讀，可到羅馬或紐約讀一學期。申請需 4 年數學（建議微積分、物理）、SAT/ACT（2026 秋起必交）、1 份輔導＋2 份老師推薦，以及經 SlideRoom 提交的作品集與 3 分鐘影片（ED 11/1、RD 1/2）。作品集要讓評審看出你屬於 AAP 列出的七種特質中的哪一種。
tldr.en: Cornell AAP's undergraduate architecture degree is a five-year, NAAB-accredited, STEM-designated professional B.Arch.: three years of core courses, then four semesters of cross-disciplinary depth, with about 1/4 of the courses open to other colleges, and the option of a semester in Rome or New York. Applicants need 4 years of mathematics (calculus and physics recommended), the SAT or ACT (required from fall 2026), 1 counselor recommendation plus 2 teacher recommendations, and a portfolio and a 3-minute video submitted through SlideRoom (ED 11/1, RD 1/2). The portfolio should let reviewers see which of the seven qualities AAP lists you belong to.

body.zh-Hant:
每年談到美國建築本科，康乃爾大學建築、藝術與規劃學院（AAP）幾乎都會被放進第一梯隊。它的地位為什麼一直這麼穩？我把這幾年帶學生申請康乃爾的經驗，加上 2026 年 10 月重新查核的官方資料，整理成這篇：康乃爾建築到底強在哪、和萊斯（Rice）差在哪、申請門檻有多高，以及錄取學生的作品長什麼樣子。

康乃爾建築本科是什麼學位？

康乃爾 AAP 的建築本科是五年制專業學位 Bachelor of Architecture（B.Arch.），在綺色佳（Ithaca）主校區就讀。依 AAP 的 NAAB 認證頁，B.Arch. 目前的 NAAB 認證期為 2025–2033 年，需修滿 154 學分。和普林斯頓那種四年制、偏通識的預備專業學位不同（我在普林斯頓建築本科錄取解析裡有詳細比較），康乃爾畢業時拿的就是可以銜接建築師執照路徑的專業學位。

康乃爾建築的地位，穩在哪四件事？

1. 專業學院的強度，綜合大學的廣度。AAP 官方 B.Arch. 頁寫得很清楚：這個學位把五年專業教育的強度，和一所研究型大學的資源結合在一起。雖然大部分課程都和建築直接相關，學生仍有約四分之一的課會在康乃爾其他學院或 AAP 其他系修讀——從工程、商學到人文，都能成為你的「建築＋X」。

2. 先打底、再深化的課程結構。所有學生前三年走同一套核心課程，涵蓋設計、理論、歷史、技術、表現法與結構；最後四個學期鼓勵跨領域、偏研究與思辨的學習。官方列出的專長方向有五個：建築、文化與社會；建築科學與技術；建築史；建築理論；建築視覺表現。

3. 羅馬與紐約的一學期。B.Arch. 學生有機會到 Cornell in Rome 或紐約的 Gensler Family AAP NYC Center 各待一學期——一邊是兩千年的城市教科書，一邊是當代建築實務的現場。

4. STEM 認證與 NAAB 認證。官方說明 B.Arch. 被認定為 STEM 學程（Architectural and Building Sciences/Technology），國際生畢業後可延長 F-1 身分、在美國工作最長三年（OPT 加上 STEM 延長）。加上 NAAB 認證，對想在美國累積實務經驗的國際生很實際。官網也自述這個學位「consistently ranked one of the top programs in the country」——排名每年會變，但它長期在前段，這是事實。

康乃爾 vs. 萊斯：兩所頂尖建築本科怎麼選？

常有家長問我：康乃爾和萊斯都很強，差在哪？我用官方資料整理成一張表：

比較項目康乃爾大學（Cornell AAP）萊斯大學（Rice Architecture）
學位結構五年制 B.Arch.，一個專業學位四年 B.A. in Architecture，再申請兩年 B.Arch.（共六年、兩個學位）
招牌經驗羅馬學期、紐約 AAP NYC CenterPreceptorship：在知名事務所支薪實習 9–12 個月
大學環境大型綜合研究型大學，約 1/4 課程可跨院修讀規模較小的研究型大學，B.Arch. 階段須再以作品集申請
適合誰目標明確、想五年拿到專業學位、善用綜合大學資源想先廣泛探索、重視長時間實務歷練

資料來源：Cornell AAP、Rice School of Architecture（2026-10-21 查核）。兩條路沒有高下，重點是哪一種節奏適合你。

申請康乃爾建築本科需要什麼條件？

依 康乃爾招生處的學院別要求與 新生申請頁（2026-10-21 查核）：

  • 高中課程：AAP 要求 4 年英文、3 年數學、3 年科學；建築系要求 4 年數學，並建議修微積分與物理。
  • 標準化考試：自 2026 秋季入學起，所有新生申請者必須提交 SAT 或 ACT（可先自報分數）。康乃爾表明沒有 GPA 或分數門檻，採整體審查。
  • 推薦信：1 份升學輔導（counselor）推薦＋ 2 份老師推薦。
  • 文書：Common App 加上康乃爾補充文書（依所申請學院作答）。
  • 作品集＋影片面試（必交）：只能透過 Cornell AAP SlideRoom 提交，ED 11 月 1 日、RD 1 月 2 日截止，逾期不收。另外，AAP 已公告 2027 秋季不接受外校轉學申請。

作品集的格式細節（15–20 張、每個項目最多 2 張、每張說明建議 50 字內、禁止 AI 生成圖、3 分鐘不剪輯影片回答三題），我在康乃爾建築本科作品集怎麼做一文已逐條拆解，這裡不重複。

康乃爾 AAP 在找什麼樣的人？

這是我覺得最值得細讀的部分。AAP 建築招生頁列出七種它重視的特質，申請者具備其中「一項或多項」即可：

  • Expressive Designers：能綜合多種資訊，清楚表達設計意圖。
  • Creative Thinkers：能把創新的想法說清楚、做出形式。
  • Spatial Changemakers：對建築與城市的現狀提出批判與挑戰。
  • Cultural Innovators：尋找個人或集體設計的新形式。
  • Rigorous Makers：主動精進技術與創作能力。
  • Empathic Individuals：在乎共同打造公平、永續、有韌性的環境。
  • Broad Thinkers：興趣橫跨科學到人文。

換句話說，作品集不必面面俱到，但要讓評審一眼看出「你是哪一種人」。下面用我指導、獲康乃爾錄取學生的作品，對照這幾種特質。

康乃爾建築錄取作品實例：對照 AAP 的特質

這四件作品的共同點是：每件都有一個清楚的出發點（一群使用者、一種文化、一朵花的結構、一只絲瓜），而不是「我會做模型」而已。這也是我帶學生時最常說的一句話：先決定你想讓評審記住你是誰，再決定放哪些作品。另一個從聲音分析走到實體模型的例子，可以看小提琴聲波的立體呈現：把自己演奏的小提琴曲聲波描成草圖，再用木棒與 PVC 三角板做成立體結構。

我的建議：怎麼為康乃爾做準備？

1. 學術成績不能鬆。4 年數學（最好含微積分）、物理，加上 SAT/ACT 已恢復必交——康乃爾建築不是「作品好就好」的學校。

2. 從七種特質裡挑一到兩種，當成作品集的主軸。官方說「一項或多項」，與其每種都沾一點，不如把一兩種講深。

3. 讓作品集和影片說同一個故事。影片第二題要你講一個項目的設計過程與影響，最好就是作品集裡最有分量的那一件。

4. ED 要提早一年規劃。作品集 11 月 1 日就要交，比多數學校早；真正能動手做作品的時間，通常是高二升高三的暑假前後。

本文依 2026 年 10 月官方資料更新。
body.en:
Every year, when the conversation turns to undergraduate architecture in the United States, Cornell University's College of Architecture, Art, and Planning (AAP) is almost always placed in the top tier. Why has its standing stayed so steady? I have put this piece together from several years of guiding students through Cornell applications, plus official material I checked again in October 2026: where Cornell Architecture is actually strong, how it differs from Rice, how high the admissions bar is, and what admitted students' work looks like.

What degree is Cornell undergraduate architecture?

Cornell AAP's undergraduate architecture degree is a five-year professional degree, the Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch.), taught on the main campus in Ithaca. According to AAP's NAAB accreditation page, the B.Arch. is currently NAAB-accredited for 2025–2033, and 154 credits are required. Unlike Princeton's four-year pre-professional degree, which leans toward general education (I compare the two in detail in a reading of Princeton undergraduate architecture admissions), what Cornell awards at graduation is a professional degree that connects to the path toward an architect's license.

What four things keep Cornell Architecture's standing so steady?

1. The intensity of a professional school, the breadth of a comprehensive university. AAP's official B.Arch. page states it clearly: the degree joins the intensity of a five-year professional education with the resources of a research university. Although most of the courses relate directly to architecture, students still take about a quarter of their courses in Cornell's other colleges or in other departments of AAP—from engineering and business to the humanities, any of them can become your "architecture + X".

2. A curriculum that builds a base, then goes deeper. For the first three years, every student follows the same core curriculum, covering design, theory, history, technology, representation, and structures. The final four semesters encourage study that is cross-disciplinary and leans toward research and critical thinking. The school lists five areas of focus: architecture, culture, and society; architectural science and technology; history of architecture; architectural theory; and architectural visual representation.

3. One semester in Rome and one in New York. B.Arch. students have the chance to spend one semester at Cornell in Rome or one semester at the Gensler Family AAP NYC Center in New York—one a 2,000-year urban textbook, the other the site of contemporary architectural practice.

4. STEM designation and NAAB accreditation. The official description states that the B.Arch. is designated a STEM programme (Architectural and Building Sciences/Technology). After graduation, international students may extend F-1 status and work in the United States for up to three years (OPT plus the STEM extension). Together with NAAB accreditation, that is practical for international students who want to build professional experience in the United States. The site also describes the degree, in its own words, as "consistently ranked one of the top programs in the country"—rankings change every year, but it has stayed near the front for a long time, and that is a fact.

Cornell vs. Rice: how do you choose between two top undergraduate architecture degrees?

Parents often ask me: Cornell and Rice are both strong, so where do they differ? I have turned the official information into a table:

ComparisonCornell University (Cornell AAP)Rice University (Rice Architecture)
Degree structureFive-year B.Arch., one professional degreeA four-year B.A. in Architecture, then an application for a two-year B.Arch. (six years and two degrees in total)
Signature experienceA Rome semester, and the AAP NYC Center in New YorkPreceptorship: a paid internship of 9–12 months in a well-known firm
University settingA large comprehensive research university, with about 1/4 of courses available across collegesA smaller research university; the B.Arch. stage requires a further application by portfolio
Who it suitsStudents with a clear aim, who want a professional degree in five years and will use a comprehensive university's resourcesStudents who want to explore widely first and who value a long stretch of practical training

Sources: Cornell AAP, Rice School of Architecture (checked 2026-10-21). The two paths do not rank one above the other. What matters is which pace suits you.

What does an application to Cornell undergraduate architecture require?

According to Cornell Admissions' requirements by college and the first-year applicants page (checked 2026-10-21):

  • High school curriculum: AAP requires 4 years of English, 3 years of mathematics, and 3 years of science. The architecture department requires 4 years of mathematics, and it recommends calculus and physics.
  • Standardized tests: beginning with entry in fall 2026, every first-year applicant must submit the SAT or ACT (scores may be self-reported first). Cornell states that it has no GPA or score cutoff and that review is holistic.
  • Recommendations: 1 counselor recommendation + 2 teacher recommendations.
  • Essays: the Common App, plus Cornell's supplemental essays (answered according to the college you apply to).
  • Portfolio + video interview (required): these can be submitted only through Cornell AAP SlideRoom, with deadlines of ED November 1 and RD January 2. Late work is not accepted. AAP has also announced that it will not accept transfer applications from other institutions for fall 2027.

The format details of the portfolio (15–20 images, at most 2 images per project, a suggested note of no more than 50 words on each, no AI-generated images, and an unedited 3-minute video answering three questions) are already unpacked point by point in How do you make a Cornell undergraduate architecture portfolio. I will not repeat them here.

What kind of person is Cornell AAP looking for?

This is the part I find most worth reading closely. AAP's architecture admissions page lists seven qualities it values. An applicant needs "one or more" of them:

  • Expressive Designers: can bring several kinds of information together and state a design intention clearly.
  • Creative Thinkers: can state an inventive idea clearly and give it form.
  • Spatial Changemakers: offer a critique and a challenge to the current state of architecture and the city.
  • Cultural Innovators: look for new forms of individual or collective design.
  • Rigorous Makers: take the initiative to sharpen technical skill and the ability to make.
  • Empathic Individuals: care about building, together, environments that are equitable, sustainable, and resilient.
  • Broad Thinkers: interests that run from the sciences to the humanities.

In other words, the portfolio does not have to cover every aspect, but it should let reviewers see at a glance what kind of person you are. Below, I set work by students I mentored who were admitted to Cornell against these qualities.

Admitted Cornell architecture work, set against AAP's qualities

What these four projects share is a clear point of departure in each one (a group of users, a culture, the structure of a flower, a loofah), rather than merely "I can make a model". This is also the line I say most often when I work with students: first decide who you want the reviewers to remember you as, then decide which projects to include. For another example that moves from sound analysis to a physical model, see Three-Dimensional Violin Sound Waves: the sound waves of a violin piece the student performed are drawn as sketches, then built into a spatial structure with wooden sticks and triangular PVC panels.

My advice: how do you prepare for Cornell?

1. The academic record cannot slip. 4 years of mathematics (preferably including calculus), physics, and the SAT or ACT, which is required again—at Cornell Architecture, strong work on its own is not enough.

2. Pick one or two of the seven qualities and make them the spine of the portfolio. The official line is "one or more". Develop one or two in depth, which goes further than a light touch on every one.

3. Let the portfolio and the video tell the same story. The video's second question asks you to talk through one project's design process and its impact. That should be the project with the most weight in the portfolio.

4. Plan ED a year ahead. The portfolio is due on November 1, earlier than at most schools. The time when you can actually make the work usually falls around the summer between 11th and 12th grade.

This article was updated from official material in October 2026.

keywords: 康乃爾 vs 萊斯 建築

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾建築本科要讀幾年？畢業拿什麼學位？
q.en: How many years is Cornell undergraduate architecture, and what degree do you graduate with?

a.zh-Hant: 五年，畢業取得 NAAB 認證的專業學位 Bachelor of Architecture（B.Arch.），共 154 學分；目前認證期為 2025–2033 年。
a.en: Five years. Graduates receive the NAAB-accredited professional degree Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch.), for 154 credits in total. The current accreditation term is 2025–2033.

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾建築本科是 STEM 學位嗎？
q.en: Is Cornell undergraduate architecture a STEM degree?

a.zh-Hant: 是。官方說明 B.Arch. 被認定為 STEM 學程（Architectural and Building Sciences/Technology），國際生畢業後可延長 F-1 身分在美國工作最長三年。
a.en: Yes. The official description states that the B.Arch. is designated a STEM programme (Architectural and Building Sciences/Technology). After graduation, international students may extend F-1 status and work in the United States for up to three years.

q.zh-Hant: 申請康乃爾建築需要考 SAT 或 ACT 嗎？
q.en: Do you need to take the SAT or ACT to apply to Cornell Architecture?

a.zh-Hant: 需要。自 2026 秋季入學起，康乃爾所有新生申請者都必須提交 SAT 或 ACT，可先在申請中自報分數；學校沒有 GPA 或分數門檻。
a.en: Yes. Beginning with entry in fall 2026, every first-year applicant to Cornell must submit the SAT or ACT, and scores may be self-reported on the application first. The university has no GPA or score cutoff.

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾建築和萊斯建築有什麼不同？
q.en: How do Cornell Architecture and Rice Architecture differ?

a.zh-Hant: 康乃爾是五年一個 B.Arch. 學位，有羅馬與紐約學期；萊斯是四年 B.A. 再加兩年 B.Arch.（共六年），其中包含在事務所支薪實習 9–12 個月的 Preceptorship。
a.en: Cornell is one five-year B.Arch. degree, with semesters in Rome and New York. Rice is a four-year B.A. plus a two-year B.Arch. (six years in total), which includes a Preceptorship of 9–12 months of paid internship in a firm.

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾建築的作品集和影片什麼時候截止？
q.en: When are the deadlines for Cornell Architecture's portfolio and video?

a.zh-Hant: 須透過 Cornell AAP SlideRoom 提交，ED 為 11 月 1 日、RD 為 1 月 2 日，逾期不收（2026-10-21 查核）。
a.en: They must be submitted through Cornell AAP SlideRoom. ED is November 1 and RD is January 2, and late submissions are not accepted (checked 2026-10-21).

Compared with Rice (four-year B.A. plus a two-year B.Arch. including a 9–12-month paid Preceptorship), Cornell is a single five-year degree. title.zh-Hant: 康乃爾建築本科作品集怎麼做？AAP 官方要求、3 分鐘影片與 4 個高分策略
title.en: How do you make a Cornell undergraduate architecture portfolio? Official AAP requirements, the 3-minute video, and 4 high-scoring strategies

summary.zh-Hant: 康乃爾 AAP 建築本科看重創造力、設計過程、媒材多元與項目化思維。整理官方作品集內容建議、3 分鐘影片三題、SlideRoom 格式與截止日，以及 4 個實戰策略。
summary.en: Cornell AAP undergraduate architecture values creativity, design process, a range of media, and project-based thinking. This post gathers the official suggestions for portfolio content, the three prompts in the 3-minute video, the SlideRoom format and deadlines, and 4 practical strategies.

tldr.zh-Hant: 康乃爾建築本科作品集：15–20 張投影片（每項目最多 2 張）＋ 1 段不剪輯、3 分鐘內的影片，經 SlideRoom 提交，ED 11/1、RD 1/2。手繪必備，禁止代做與 AI 生成圖。策略：2–3 件作品組成一個主題項目、每頁加資訊欄、展示 2D→3D、連結個人興趣。
tldr.en: A Cornell undergraduate architecture portfolio is 15–20 slides (at most 2 per project) plus one unedited video of no more than 3 minutes, submitted through SlideRoom, with deadlines of ED 11/1 and RD 1/2. Freehand drawing is required; work made by someone else and AI-generated images are not allowed. The strategies are to group 2–3 works into one thematic project, add an information field on every page, show 2D→3D, and connect the work to a personal interest.

body.zh-Hant:
康乃爾大學建築、藝術與規劃學院（AAP）的建築本科，被許多人視為美國最頂尖的建築本科項目之一。我指導的學生也曾獲得錄取。這篇把我整理的官方要求與作品集策略一次說清楚：康乃爾到底想在作品集裡看到什麼？

康乃爾建築本科在找什麼樣的學生？

AAP 官方說明它在申請者身上尋找三件事：創造力（creative ability）、對建築的投入（commitment to architecture），以及扎實的學術背景（strong academic background）。作品集主要負責證明前兩項。

康乃爾建築作品集最看重哪四件事？

  • 創造力與熱情：作品要看得出你真的在乎、真的有想法。
  • 設計過程：從靈感、草圖到成品的推演，比單一張完成圖更重要。
  • 媒材多元：展現你能用不同方式表達。
  • 項目化思維（project-based mindset）：作品不是零散的單張，而是有主題、有脈絡的項目。

康乃爾建築作品集可以放哪些作品？

官方建議的內容包括：手繪（freehand drawing，必備）、繪畫、雕塑、攝影、木作、其他手工藝、過程作品，以及獨立項目。

同時有兩條紅線：不能找人代做作品集，也不能使用 AI 生成的圖像。

康乃爾的 3 分鐘影片要回答哪些問題？

除了作品集，康乃爾要求一段不經剪輯、不超過 3 分鐘的影片，回答三個問題：

  1. 你如何表達你的創造力？（How do you express your creativity?）
  2. 描述一個創意項目的設計過程與它帶來的影響。（Describe the design process and impact of one creative project.）
  3. 你為什麼想學建築？（Why do you want to study Architecture?）

這三題其實和作品集是同一件事的兩面：影片是你親口講出作品集背後的思考。所以作品集裡至少要有一個項目，是你能完整講出「從哪來、怎麼做、帶來什麼」的。

康乃爾建築本科錄取作品集實例解析

以下是我指導、獲康乃爾建築本科錄取學生的作品。注意它們如何對應官方要求的「手繪＋多元媒材＋過程」。

這個項目先用古畫與手繪研究「織」的過程（官方列為必備的 freehand drawing），再用模型轉成空間——同一主題串起 2D 研究與 3D 成果，正是官方說的 project-based mindset。

怎麼讓作品集更有說服力？4 個實戰策略

1. 把 2–3 件作品組成一個項目。與其放很多單張，不如用一個主題串起來，例如「光與影」或「城市的記憶」，讓評審看到你在一個問題上持續深入。

2. 每頁加上資訊欄。標註作品名稱、媒材、尺寸、日期，以及是獨立創作還是課堂作業。文字說明保持精簡。

3. 展示從 2D 到 3D 的轉換。例如一位學生先畫出空間構想，再把它做成實體模型——這正是康乃爾在意的設計過程。

4. 把項目和個人興趣連起來。例如另一位學生透過親手製作，研究日式建築的構造方式。真實的興趣，會讓作品集有辨識度。

康乃爾 AAP 官方作品集要求（截至 2026-10-20 查核）

依 Cornell AAP 建築本科招生頁：

  • 學位：五年制專業學位 Bachelor of Architecture（B.Arch.）。
  • 必交：作品集＋影片面試，只接受經 Cornell AAP SlideRoom 提交。
  • 15–20 張，每個項目最多 2 張；需展示手繪（草圖與完整作品）與多元媒材。
  • 每張說明建議不超過 50 字，說明意圖、過程與結果；並註明尺寸、媒材、是課堂、作品集工作坊或獨立完成。
  • 圖片保持清楚、除非是作品一部分否則不放文字；團隊作品須標註合作者與自己的角色；不得外包，包括 AI 生成圖像。
  • 影片：連續拍攝、不剪輯、總長不超過 3 分鐘，只回答三個問題。
  • 截止日：ED 11 月 1 日、RD 1 月 2 日；逾期不收；AAP 不接受 2027 秋季的外部轉學申請。
body.en:
Undergraduate architecture at Cornell University’s College of Architecture, Art, and Planning (AAP) is widely regarded as among the strongest in the United States. Students I have mentored have been admitted. This post sets out, in one place, the official requirements I have compiled and the portfolio strategies that go with them: what does Cornell actually want to see in a portfolio?

What kind of student is Cornell undergraduate architecture looking for?

AAP’s official materials say it looks for three things in an applicant: creative ability, commitment to architecture, and a strong academic background. The portfolio is there mainly to demonstrate the first two.

Which four things does a Cornell architecture portfolio value most?

  • Creativity and passion: the work should show that you genuinely care, and that you have ideas of your own.
  • Design process: the development from inspiration and sketches through to a finished piece matters more than any single completed image.
  • A range of media: show that you can express an idea in more than one way.
  • A project-based mindset: the work is not a scatter of single images, but projects with a theme and a through-line.

What work can a Cornell architecture portfolio include?

The content the school suggests includes freehand drawing (required), painting, sculpture, photography, woodwork, other crafts, process work, and independent projects.

There are also two hard lines: you may not have someone else make the portfolio, and you may not use AI-generated images.

Which questions does Cornell’s 3-minute video have to answer?

Alongside the portfolio, Cornell requires a video that is unedited and no longer than 3 minutes, answering three questions:

  1. How do you express your creativity?
  2. Describe the design process and impact of one creative project.
  3. Why do you want to study Architecture?

These three questions and the portfolio are two sides of the same thing: the video is you saying, in your own voice, the thinking behind the portfolio. So the portfolio needs at least one project you can talk through completely — where it came from, how you made it, and what it brought.

A close reading of portfolios admitted to Cornell undergraduate architecture

Below is work by students I mentored who were admitted to Cornell undergraduate architecture. Notice how it answers the official ask for “freehand drawing + a range of media + process.”

This project first uses old paintings and freehand drawing to study the process of “weaving” (freehand drawing, which the school lists as required), then uses a model to turn that into space — one theme tying 2D research to a 3D result, which is exactly the project-based mindset the school describes.

How do you make a portfolio more convincing? 4 practical strategies

1. Group 2–3 works into one project. Rather than showing many single images, thread them with one theme — “light and shadow,” or “the memory of the city” — so reviewers see you staying with one question and going deeper.

2. Add an information field on every page. Note the title, medium, dimensions, and date, and whether the work is independent or a class assignment. Keep the written note short.

3. Show the shift from 2D to 3D. One student, for example, first drew a spatial idea and then built it as a physical model — precisely the design process Cornell cares about.

4. Connect the project to a personal interest. Another student, for example, studied how Japanese architecture is put together by making it by hand. A real interest is what gives a portfolio a recognisable voice.

Official Cornell AAP portfolio requirements (checked 2026-10-20)

From the Cornell AAP undergraduate architecture admissions page:

  • Degree: a five-year professional degree, the Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch.).
  • Required: a portfolio and a video interview, accepted only when submitted through Cornell AAP SlideRoom.
  • 15–20 slides, at most 2 per project; freehand drawing (sketches and finished work) and a range of media must be shown.
  • A note of no more than 50 words on each image is recommended, covering intent, process, and outcome; also note the dimensions, the medium, and whether the work was done in class, in a portfolio workshop, or independently.
  • Keep images clear, and do not add text unless it is part of the work; for team work, name the collaborators and your own role; do not outsource the work, including AI-generated images.
  • Video: filmed continuously, unedited, no longer than 3 minutes in total, answering only the three questions.
  • Deadlines: ED 11/1, RD 1/2; late submissions are not accepted; AAP is not accepting external transfer applications for fall 2027.

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾建築本科作品集需要幾頁？
q.en: How many pages does a Cornell undergraduate architecture portfolio need?

a.zh-Hant: 15–20 張投影片，每個項目最多 2 張，透過 Cornell AAP SlideRoom 提交。
a.en: 15–20 slides, at most 2 per project, submitted through Cornell AAP SlideRoom.

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾建築申請的影片有什麼要求？
q.en: What are the requirements for the video in a Cornell architecture application?

a.zh-Hant: 1 段不經剪輯、不超過 3 分鐘的影片，回答三個問題：你如何表達創造力、描述一個創意項目的設計過程與影響、你為什麼想學建築。
a.en: One unedited video of no more than 3 minutes, answering three questions: how you express your creativity, the design process and impact of one creative project, and why you want to study architecture.

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾建築作品集可以用 AI 生成圖片嗎？
q.en: Can a Cornell architecture portfolio use AI-generated images?

a.zh-Hant: 不可以。官方明確要求不能使用 AI 生成的圖像，也不能找人代做作品集。
a.en: No. The official requirements state clearly that you may not use AI-generated images, and that you may not have someone else make the portfolio.

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾建築作品集的截止日是什麼時候？
q.en: When is the deadline for a Cornell architecture portfolio?

a.zh-Hant: 原文整理的截止日為 ED 11 月 1 日、RD 1 月 2 日，比 Common App 更早；申請前請以 AAP 官網最新公告為準。
a.en: The deadlines compiled here are ED 11/1 and RD 1/2, earlier than the Common App. Before you apply, follow the latest announcement on the AAP website.

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾建築作品集一定要有手繪嗎？
q.en: Does a Cornell architecture portfolio have to include freehand drawing?

a.zh-Hant: 官方建議的內容中，手繪（freehand drawing）被列為必備，其他可包括繪畫、雕塑、攝影、木作、手工藝、過程作品與獨立項目。
a.en: Among the content the school suggests, freehand drawing is listed as required. Other work may include painting, sculpture, photography, woodwork, crafts, process work, and independent projects.

posts.abstract_en: What does Cornell look for in a B.Arch portfolio? Cornell AAP's five-year Bachelor of Architecture requires a portfolio and a video interview submitted only via Cornell AAP SlideRoom: 15–20 slides with no more than two per project, freehand drawings and a range of media, image descriptions of no more than 50 words, and a note on size, medium and whether work was done in class, in a workshop or independently. No outsourcing, including AI-generated images. The unedited video (max. 3 minutes) answers three prompts. Deadlines (checked 2026-10-20): ED Nov. 1, RD Jan. 2. title.zh-Hant: 看完這五個作品，你會明白名校想要的到底是什麼：康乃爾、UCL、雪城等錄取作品集解析
title.en: Look through these five projects and you will see what top schools actually want: admitted portfolios from Cornell, UCL, Syracuse, and others

summary.zh-Hant: 五件獲康乃爾、賓大、UCL、AA、雪城、愛丁堡等校錄取的建築作品集作品逐一解析：崖邊之屋、脊椎博物館、豬場 AR 遊戲、漂浮紅樹林涼亭、X-重力，對照官方作品集要求，說明名校真正想看的是問題意識、轉譯能力與設計過程。
summary.en: Five architecture portfolio projects admitted to Cornell, Penn, UCL, the AA, Syracuse, Edinburgh, and other schools — The Cliffhouse, Spine Museum, a pig-farm AR game, Floating Mangrove Pavilion, and X-Gravity — are read one by one against official portfolio requirements. What top schools really want is a sense of the problem, the ability to translate, and a visible design process.

tldr.zh-Hant: 名校作品集看的不是技巧堆疊，而是三件事：先有一個自己的問題、能把個人關注（身體、自然、動物、構造、重力）轉譯成空間語言、並讓研究與過程被看見。康乃爾 AAP 列出七種重視的特質，UCL Bartlett 看你「從一個想法發展下去」的能力、接受過程與失敗嘗試，雪城 B.Arch. 重視寫生與創造力、不看軟體操作。本文以五件錄取作品示範。
tldr.en: A top-school portfolio is not a stack of technique. It looks for three things: a question of your own, the ability to translate a personal concern (the body, nature, animals, construction, gravity) into spatial language, and research and process that can be seen. Cornell AAP lists seven qualities it values. UCL Bartlett looks for the ability to develop onward from one idea, and it accepts process and failed attempts. Syracuse’s B.Arch. values observational drawing and creativity, and it does not assess software skill. This post demonstrates that with five admitted projects.

body.zh-Hant:
常有家長和學生問我：「名校到底想看什麼樣的作品集？」與其講抽象的原則，不如直接看作品。這篇挑了五件我指導過、拿到頂尖院校錄取的作品——錄取學校包括康乃爾、賓州大學、UCL、AA 建築聯盟學院、雪城大學、愛丁堡大學等。五件作品的題目完全不同：一座崖邊的紙構房子、一座從脊椎動態長出來的博物館、一個讓人扮演豬的 AR 遊戲、一座漂浮在紅樹林上的涼亭、一組掙脫重力的立方體。但它們被錄取的理由，其實是同一件事。

名校在作品集裡到底想看什麼？先看官方怎麼說

我在 2026 年 10 月重新查核了幾所學校的官方說明，用字不同，但方向高度一致：

  • 康乃爾 AAP：建築招生頁列出七種它重視的特質（Expressive Designers、Creative Thinkers、Spatial Changemakers、Cultural Innovators、Rigorous Makers、Empathic Individuals、Broad Thinkers），申請者具備「一項或多項」即可。
  • UCL Bartlett（大學部）：官方作品集 FAQ說，他們想看你「創造性、知性與三維思考」的能力，以及從一個想法出發、把它發展下去的能力；過程、草圖、甚至失敗的嘗試都可以放；作品也不必全是建築。
  • 雪城大學 Syracuse Architecture（B.Arch.）：作品集要求頁寫明以技巧、紀律與創造力評估，建議 12–15 件作品中至少 8 件是寫生觀察；照著照片、雜誌或名作臨摹的作品不算強項，軟體操作也不是評分重點。

翻成白話就是：名校不是在找「最會做模型的人」，而是在找「有自己的問題、而且能把問題做成空間的人」。下面五件作品，正好是五種不同的示範。

五個錄取作品逐一解析

1. 崖邊之屋：把構造問題當成設計主題

這位學生先拆解經典的懸崖住宅案例，再把自己過去做過的牆面圖案研究帶進來，並參考日本榫卯的接合邏輯。最有意思的是材料上的決定：用紙片互相插接取代膠水，靠幾何穿插讓結構自己站穩，正立面的方形單元一層層錯開、探出崖邊，讓一棟靜態的房子看起來在流動。

它成功的原因不是「靈感很多」，而是實地觀察、傳統工藝和過去的練習，全部服務於同一個核心概念：一棟不靠膠水、靠接合站起來的房子。這正對應康乃爾說的 Rigorous Makers。

2. 脊椎博物館：從身體的動態長出空間

這件作品從一個很個人的關注出發——脊椎的健康與姿態。學生先研究脊椎扭轉、彎曲、側傾等動作，把它們整理成空間操作（扭、彎、失衡、傾斜、不對稱），再用參數化工具生成有韻律的樓板與牆面。基地選在澳門，配合旅遊城市的屬性安排展區，讓私密與開放的空間交錯；數位模型和實體模型並行，讓「脊椎線條變成空間」的過程一目了然。

它示範的是跨領域研究如何轉成設計語言：不是畫一個像脊椎的造型，而是把身體的運動邏輯變成空間的生成規則。

3. 豬場：用一個 AR 遊戲讓人站到豬那一邊

這是一件碩士申請作品，題目是人與動物的不平等。學生沒有用理論說教，而是設計了一座莊園和一個 AR 遊戲：訪客扮演一頭豬，靠討好人類賺分數、換取更好的生存空間，卻終究逃不過被吃掉的命運——分數最後還能在莊園餐廳兌換豬肉。實體模型把餐廳、牧場、籠舍和動線串成一條體驗路徑。

它說明了一件事：作品集不一定要是「一棟建築」。只要你能把一個價值問題轉成可體驗的空間與規則，遊戲、裝置、場景都可以是建築思考。UCL Bartlett 的大學部作品集 FAQ 也明說：作品不必全是建築。

4. 漂浮紅樹林涼亭：從《湖濱散記》走到紅樹林

人和自然，是依存還是共生？這位學生的起點是一本書——梭羅的《湖濱散記》（Walden）。他把這個哲學問題帶到紅樹林做實地觀察：鬆軟的泥沙、定期漲退的海水、瀕危鳥類的棲地，都成了設計必須回答的「生態考題」。最後的建築用細鐵絲當柱、像樹林一樣輕輕落地，霧面的曲面屋頂漂浮在紅樹林之上，盡量不打擾底下的生態。

從哲學提問 → 生態調查 → 設計落地，三步環環相扣，這就是名校最認的「設計者思維」，也對應康乃爾的 Empathic Individuals 與 Broad Thinkers。

5. X-重力：一個看展的瞬間，變成一套形式實驗

這件作品的起點很單純：學生幾年前看展時，被一件作品裡「反重力」的動態感打動。他沒有停在「喜歡」，而是開始做實驗——先用迴圈與旋轉的研究找到節奏，再把大小不一的立方體用木條錯位連接、部分覆上紙面，堆疊成一團像是飄浮起來的量體。模型沒有複雜裝飾，卻把「掙脫重力」直接放到你眼前。

它的價值在思考方式：不靠昂貴材料或複雜技術，只靠打破對重力的常規認知，用最簡潔的手段傳遞一個鮮明的主張。

五個作品的共同點：名校想要的三件事

1. 先有問題，才有形式。五件作品各自從一個問題出發：房子能不能不用膠水站起來？身體的動態能不能變成空間？人能不能站在豬的角度？建築能不能不打擾紅樹林？重力能不能被「看起來」打破？問題清楚，作品就有主軸。

2. 把個人的關注「轉譯」成設計語言。一本書、一次看展、對身體或動物的在意——這些看起來「不像設計」的起點，經過研究和轉譯，才是最有辨識度的作品集素材。

3. 讓過程被看見。節點草圖、動作分析、遊戲規則、迴圈研究——評審要看的是你怎麼想、怎麼試、怎麼修正，而不只是一張漂亮的成品照。UCL 甚至明說，失敗的嘗試也可以放。

我怎麼陪學生找到作品集主題？

這幾年帶學生，我最常做的不是「教他們做設計」，而是先聽。很多好題目藏在學生自己都沒當回事的地方：一次觀展的觸動、一本讓他想很久的書、對動物權益的憤憤不平、對家鄉地貌的眷戀。我的工作是比學生更早聽見這些興趣，再提供嚴謹的研究框架和跨領域工具，幫他把個人敘事、哲學思考和情感關懷，轉成只屬於他的設計語言。

我不替學生設計。最好的作品集，是一個「人」的展開——它記錄的不是技巧的堆疊，而是思考如何演進、觀念如何成形。名校最後認可的，也正是這份還沒被馴化的想像力、有深度的思考，以及作品背後那個清晰、有主張的人。

想申請名校，作品集可以從哪裡開始？

  • 列出你真正在意的三件事（不限於建築），挑一件追問到底：它背後的問題是什麼？
  • 先研究、再造型：用觀察、閱讀、實地調查或實驗模型，把問題拆清楚。
  • 保留過程：草圖、失敗的模型、迭代照片都要拍、都要存。
  • 對照目標學校的要求：例如雪城要大量寫生、康乃爾要影片面試、UCL 大學部只收 10 頁 PDF——同一套作品，要依學校重新剪裁。

想看單一學校的細節，可以讀我整理的康乃爾建築本科作品集怎麼做、康乃爾建築本科為什麼地位這麼穩，以及普林斯頓建築本科錄取解析。更多學生作品，請看作品牆。

本文依 2026 年 10 月官方資料更新。
body.en:
Parents and students often ask me, “What kind of portfolio do top schools actually want to see?” Rather than talking through abstract principles, it is better to look at the work. This post takes five projects I mentored that earned offers from leading schools — Cornell, the University of Pennsylvania, UCL, the Architectural Association (AA), Syracuse University, the University of Edinburgh, and others. The five subjects could not be more different: a paper house on a cliff edge, a museum grown from the movement of a spine, an AR game in which you play a pig, a pavilion floating over a mangrove, and a set of cubes that slip free of gravity. The reason they were admitted is, in fact, the same thing.

What do top schools actually want to see in a portfolio? Start with what they say officially

In October 2026 I checked the official guidance from several schools again. The wording differs, but the direction is highly consistent:

  • Cornell AAP: the architecture admissions page lists seven qualities it values (Expressive Designers, Creative Thinkers, Spatial Changemakers, Cultural Innovators, Rigorous Makers, Empathic Individuals, Broad Thinkers). An applicant needs only “one or more” of them.
  • UCL Bartlett (undergraduate): the official portfolio FAQ says they want to see your capacity for “creative, intellectual, and three-dimensional thinking,” and your ability to start from one idea and develop it; process, sketches, and even failed attempts can be included; the work does not all have to be architecture.
  • Syracuse University, Syracuse Architecture (B.Arch.): the portfolio requirements page states that applicants are assessed on skill, discipline, and creativity. Of the suggested 12–15 works, at least 8 should be observational drawings. Work copied from photographs, magazines, or celebrated pieces is not a strength, and software skill is not a focus of the scoring.

In plain words: top schools are not looking for “the person who is best at making models.” They are looking for “someone who has a question of their own, and who can turn that question into space.” The five projects below are five different demonstrations of exactly that.

Five admitted projects, read one by one

1. The Cliffhouse: treating a problem of construction as the design theme

This student first took apart classic cliff-house precedents, then brought in earlier research on wall patterns, and drew on the joining logic of Japanese mortise-and-tenon. The most interesting decision is the material: paper sheets slotted into one another, in place of glue. Interlocking geometry lets the structure stand on its own. Square units on the front elevation offset layer by layer and reach out past the cliff edge, so a static house looks as if it is flowing.

The reason it succeeds is not that there is “a lot of inspiration.” Field observation, traditional craft, and earlier exercises all serve one core concept: a house that stands by its joints, not by glue. That is what Cornell calls Rigorous Makers.

2. Spine Museum: space grown from the movement of the body

This project starts from a deeply personal concern — the health and posture of the spine. The student first studied movements of the spine such as twisting, bending, and leaning to the side, sorted them into spatial operations (twist, bend, imbalance, tilt, asymmetry), and then used parametric tools to generate floor plates and walls with a rhythm. The site is in Macau. The exhibition areas are arranged for a city of tourism, so private and open spaces interleave. Digital models and physical models run side by side, so the process by which “the line of the spine becomes space” is easy to read.

What it demonstrates is how research across fields becomes a design language: not drawing a shape that looks like a spine, but turning the logic of bodily movement into the rules that generate the space.

3. Pig Farm: an AR game that puts you on the pig’s side

This is a project for a master’s application. The subject is inequality between humans and animals. The student does not lecture with theory, and instead designs a manor and an AR game: the visitor plays a pig, earns points by pleasing humans, and trades them for a better space in which to live, yet cannot in the end escape being eaten — and the points can finally be redeemed for pork in the manor’s restaurant. A physical model threads the restaurant, the pasture, the pens, and the circulation into one path of experience.

It makes one thing clear: a portfolio does not have to be “a building.” If you can turn a question of values into space and rules that someone can experience, a game, an installation, or a setting can be architectural thinking. The undergraduate portfolio FAQ at UCL Bartlett says the same thing outright: the work does not all have to be architecture.

4. Floating Mangrove Pavilion: from Walden to the mangrove

Are humans and nature dependent on each other, or do they live in symbiosis? This student’s starting point was a book — Thoreau’s Walden. That philosophical question was taken to a mangrove for field observation: soft silt and sand, seawater that rises and falls on a cycle, and habitat for endangered birds all became “ecological questions” the design had to answer. The final building uses thin wire as columns and meets the ground lightly, like a stand of trees. A frosted curved roof floats above the mangrove, disturbing the ecology underneath as little as possible.

From a philosophical question → an ecological survey → a resolved design, the three steps lock together. This is the “designer’s thinking” that top schools recognise most readily, and it corresponds to Cornell’s Empathic Individuals and Broad Thinkers.

5. X-Gravity: a moment at an exhibition becomes a formal experiment

The starting point is simple. A few years ago, at an exhibition, the student was struck by a sense of “anti-gravity” movement inside one work. The student did not stop at “I like this,” and began to experiment — first finding a rhythm through studies of loops and rotation, then connecting cubes of different sizes with wooden sticks set out of alignment, covering some faces with paper, and stacking them into a mass that seems to float. The model has no elaborate ornament, yet it puts “breaking free of gravity” directly in front of you.

Its value is in the way of thinking: not expensive materials or complicated technique, only a break with the usual understanding of gravity, using the simplest means to carry a sharp claim.

What the five projects share: three things top schools want

1. A question first, and only then a form. Each of the five projects starts from a question. Can a house stand up without glue? Can the movement of a body become space? Can a person take the pig’s point of view? Can a building leave a mangrove undisturbed? Can gravity be broken “in appearance”? When the question is clear, the project has a through-line.

2. “Translate” a personal concern into a design language. A book, a visit to an exhibition, care for the body or for animals — starting points that do not look like “design” — become, after research and translation, the most recognisable material a portfolio can hold.

3. Let the process be seen. Joint sketches, movement analysis, the rules of a game, loop studies — reviewers want to see how you think, how you try, and how you revise, not only a polished photograph of the finished piece. UCL even says outright that failed attempts can be included.

How do I help students find a portfolio theme?

In the years I have spent with students, what I do most often is not “teach them how to design.” It is to listen first. Many good subjects hide in places the students themselves never take seriously: the jolt of seeing an exhibition, a book that kept them thinking for a long time, anger about animal rights, attachment to the landscape of home. My work is to hear those interests sooner than the student does, then offer a rigorous frame for research and tools from other fields, and help turn a personal narrative, philosophical thinking, and emotional concern into a design language that belongs to that student alone.

I do not design for my students. The best portfolio is a “person” unfolding — it records not a stack of technique, but how thinking develops and how an idea takes shape. What a top school recognises in the end is exactly that untamed imagination, thinking with depth, and, behind the work, a person who is clear and has a claim to make.

If you want to apply to a top school, where can a portfolio start?

  • List three things you genuinely care about (not limited to architecture), pick one, and follow it to the end: what is the question behind it?
  • Research first, then give it a form: use observation, reading, site investigation, or experimental models to take the question apart until it is clear.
  • Keep the process: sketches, failed models, and photographs of iterations all need to be shot and all need to be saved.
  • Set the work against the target school’s requirements: Syracuse wants a great deal of observational drawing, Cornell wants a video interview, and UCL undergraduate accepts only a 10-page PDF — the same body of work has to be recut for each school.

For the detail on a single school, you can read what I have put together on how to make a Cornell undergraduate architecture portfolio, why Cornell undergraduate architecture holds its standing so steadily, and a reading of admission to Princeton undergraduate architecture. For more student work, see the work wall.

This article was updated from official sources in October 2026.

keywords: AA 建築聯盟學院 作品集
建築作品集主題怎麼找
what top architecture schools look for in a portfolio

q.zh-Hant: 名校建築作品集最看重什麼？
q.en: What do top architecture schools value most in a portfolio?

a.zh-Hant: 看重的是問題意識、把個人關注轉成空間語言的能力，以及可見的設計過程，而不是技巧或軟體操作。康乃爾 AAP 列出七種重視的特質，UCL Bartlett 看你從一個想法發展下去的能力，雪城則以技巧、紀律與創造力評估。
a.en: They value a sense of the problem, the ability to turn a personal concern into spatial language, and a visible design process, rather than technique or software skill. Cornell AAP lists seven qualities it values. UCL Bartlett looks at your ability to develop onward from one idea. Syracuse assesses skill, discipline, and creativity.

q.zh-Hant: 建築作品集一定要放建築設計嗎？
q.en: Does an architecture portfolio have to include architectural design?

a.zh-Hant: 不一定。UCL Bartlett 官方說明作品不必全是建築，可以是繪畫、模型、攝影、遊戲、裝置等；本文的「豬場」就是以 AR 遊戲加實體模型，在碩士申請中獲 UCL 與 AA 等校錄取。
a.en: Not necessarily. UCL Bartlett’s official guidance says the work does not all have to be architecture; it can be painting, models, photography, games, installations, and so on. “Pig Farm” in this article is an AR game plus a physical model, and in a master’s application it was admitted to UCL, the AA, and other schools.

q.zh-Hant: 作品集可以放過程和失敗的嘗試嗎？
q.en: Can a portfolio include process and failed attempts?

a.zh-Hant: 可以，而且建議放。UCL Bartlett 明確表示歡迎從最初靈感、草圖到失敗嘗試的過程；節點草圖、動作分析、迭代模型都能讓評審看見你的思考方式。
a.en: Yes, and it is worth including them. UCL Bartlett states clearly that the process is welcome, from the first inspiration and sketches through to failed attempts. Joint sketches, movement analysis, and iterative models all let reviewers see how you think.

q.zh-Hant: 雪城大學建築本科作品集要放幾件？
q.en: How many pieces should an undergraduate architecture portfolio for Syracuse University include?

a.zh-Hant: 官方建議 12–15 件近期最好的作品，其中至少 8 件為寫生觀察作品，並附一段對建築興趣的簡短說明；每件標註媒材、課內或自主、原尺寸與一兩句說明（2026-10-21 查核）。
a.en: The official suggestion is 12–15 of the best recent works, at least 8 of them observational drawings, together with a short statement of interest in architecture. Each piece should be labelled with the medium, whether it was made in class or independently, the original dimensions, and one or two sentences of description (checked 2026-10-21).

q.zh-Hant: 作品集主題要怎麼找？
q.en: How do you find a theme for a portfolio?

a.zh-Hant: 從自己真正在意的事開始，例如一本書、一次看展、對身體或動物的關注，追問背後的問題，再用觀察、研究和實驗模型把問題轉成空間。
a.en: Start from something you genuinely care about — a book, a visit to an exhibition, attention to the body or to animals — follow the question behind it, then use observation, research, and experimental models to turn that question into space.

posts.abstract_en: What do top architecture schools really want to see in a portfolio? This post walks through five works by students I mentored that earned offers from Cornell (B.Arch ED), Penn, UCL, the AA, Syracuse, Edinburgh and others: a cliffside house of slotted paper with no glue, a Macau museum generated from the movements of the spine, an AR game in which visitors play a pig, a pavilion floating on wire columns above a mangrove forest, and a cluster of cubes that seems to escape gravity. Checked against official guidance (2026-10-21) — Cornell AAP's seven applicant attributes, UCL Bartlett's emphasis on developing an idea and showing process (including failed attempts), and Syracuse's call for 12–15 works with at least eight observational drawings — the common thread is clear: start from your own question, translate personal concerns into spatial language, and make the process visible.

title.zh-Hant: 歐洲建築留學怎麼選？14 所頂尖院校學費與畢業後工簽全整理（2026 年 10 月官方查核）
title.en: Studying architecture in Europe: tuition and post-study work permits at 14 leading schools (checked October 2026)

summary.zh-Hant: 荷蘭、瑞士、義大利、西班牙、奧地利、比利時、捷克 14 所建築院校的非歐盟學費與畢業後求職居留比較：TU Delft、TU/e、ETH、EPFL、米蘭理工、都靈理工、羅馬大學、IED、UPC、IAAC、因斯布魯克、維也納應用藝術大學、KU Leuven、UMPRUM，2026 年 10 月依官方資料重新查核。
summary.en: A comparison of non-EU tuition and post-study job-seeking residence at 14 architecture schools in the Netherlands, Switzerland, Italy, Spain, Austria, Belgium and the Czech Republic: TU Delft, TU/e, ETH Zurich, EPFL, Politecnico di Milano, Politecnico di Torino, Sapienza, IED, UPC, IAAC, the University of Innsbruck, the University of Applied Arts Vienna (die Angewandte), KU Leuven and UMPRUM, rechecked against official sources in October 2026.

tldr.zh-Hant: 歐洲建築碩士的非歐盟學費差距很大：奧地利每學期約 €730–€750、義大利公立大學每年約 €300–€3,900、ETH／EPFL 每學期 CHF 2,190、KU Leuven 每年 €9,493.92、TU Delft 每年 €25,633。畢業後求職居留：荷蘭 1 年（可自由工作）、比利時 12 個月、西班牙 24 個月（期間不能工作）、義大利與奧地利約 1 年、捷克 9 個月、瑞士 6 個月。授課語言要逐科確認，例如因斯布魯克建築碩士是德語授課。
tldr.en: Non-EU tuition for architecture master’s degrees in Europe varies widely: about €730–€750 per semester in Austria, about €300–€3,900 a year at Italian public universities, CHF 2,190 per semester at ETH Zurich and EPFL, €9,493.92 a year at KU Leuven, and €25,633 a year at TU Delft. Post-study job-seeking residence runs for 1 year in the Netherlands (you may work freely), 12 months in Belgium, 24 months in Spain (you cannot work during that period), about 1 year in Italy and Austria, 9 months in the Czech Republic, and 6 months in Switzerland. Check the language of instruction course by course; the architecture master’s at the University of Innsbruck, for example, is taught in German.

body.zh-Hant:
說到建築留學，多數人第一個想到的是美國和英國。但這幾年我陪學生選校時，越來越常把歐洲大陸放進名單：荷蘭、瑞士、義大利、西班牙、奧地利、比利時、捷克都有很強的建築學院，不少學校的學費只有英美的零頭，而且多數國家都有畢業後讓你留下來找工作的居留許可。我自己在美國唸書、之後在德國柏林工作過幾年，很清楚「學費」和「畢業後能不能留下」這兩件事，往往比排名更影響一個人的職涯。

這篇把 7 個國家、14 所學校的學費和畢業後工簽整理在一起。原文發表於 2026 年 3 月，這次我在 2026 年 10 月逐項回到大學與各國移民機關官方網站重新查核，有幾個數字已經變了（例如台夫特、ETH／EPFL 的學費），也修正了幾個常見誤解（例如西班牙的求職居留是 24 個月、奧地利紅白紅卡需要雇主）。

2026 年 10 月重新查核：以下學費以非歐盟／非歐洲經濟區（non-EU/EEA）學生為準，除另有註明外為 2026/27 學年；每筆都附官方來源。學費每年調整，申請前請以學校當年公告為準。

為什麼建築留學值得考慮歐洲？

  • 學費差距大：義大利、奧地利、西班牙公立大學的非歐盟學費每年多在數百到數千歐元；荷蘭、比利時、私立設計學院較高，但多半仍低於英美。
  • 畢業後有正式的求職居留：荷蘭與比利時 1 年、西班牙 24 個月、義大利與奧地利約 1 年、捷克 9 個月、瑞士 6 個月。
  • 英語授課普遍，但不是每校每科都是：這次查核就發現，因斯布魯克大學的建築碩士是德語授課；巴塞羅那 ETSAB 的 MBArch 也只有部分方向全英語。選校時一定要逐科確認授課語言。

14 所歐洲建築院校學費一覽（2026 年 10 月查核）

幾個重點：台夫特 2026/27 的非歐盟碩士學費已到 €25,633，比原文寫的 €22,290 高；ETH 和 EPFL 從 2025 年秋季起對外國學生收三倍學費，每學期 CHF 2,190，一年約 CHF 4,380，仍是頂尖理工學院裡最便宜的一群。義大利三所公立大學的計算方式都和「國籍或收入申報地」有關，同一所學校，不同國家的學生繳的不一樣。

畢業後能留下來工作嗎？各國求職居留怎麼比？
