和原文相比，這次查核修正了三點：西班牙現行規定是 24 個月、不可延長，而且期間不能工作；奧地利的紅白紅卡不是「免雇主擔保直接申請」，而是先延長 12 個月找工作，拿到雇主的工作合約後才能申請；義大利畢業生適用的是「求職或創業」居留，不是給失業者的「待業居留」。

荷蘭：TU Delft 與 TU/e 適合誰？

文首的封面是台夫特理工大學圖書館的斜坡草坪屋頂。荷蘭的優勢在「畢業後」：在荷蘭完成認證的碩士學位後，可以申請 1 年的求職年居留，期間可以自由工作、不需雇主另辦工作許可。荷蘭的英語普及度高，國際事務所多，是想留在歐洲發展的學生最常放進第一志願的國家。代價是學費：TU Delft 碩士非歐盟學費 2026/27 為 €25,633，TU/e 為 €21,700，和英國一年制碩士相比並不便宜，而且荷蘭的建築碩士多是兩年。

TU Delft 的 MSc Architecture, Urbanism and Building Sciences 為兩年 120 EC、英語授課；非歐盟申請者 2027 年入學的截止日是 2027 年 1 月 15 日，系統 2026 年 10 月 15 日開放。

瑞士：ETH Zurich 與 EPFL 為什麼還是「高 CP 值」？

ETH 和 EPFL 依瑞士聯邦理工學院委員會的收費規定，從 2025 年秋季起對「為求學而移居瑞士」的外國學生收取三倍學費：每學期 CHF 2,190（原本 CHF 730）。即使如此，一年 CHF 4,380 的學費放在世界頂尖理工學院裡仍然非常低；真正的成本在生活費，EPFL 官方估算外國學生不含學費一年約 CHF 25,000。

畢業後的路比較窄：非歐盟畢業生可以申請最多 6 個月的求職居留，而且是從畢業日起算，不可延長。要留下來，需要雇主替你申請工作許可；瑞士《外國人與融合法》第 21 條對瑞士學位畢業生、且工作具高度學術或經濟利益者，可免除本國勞工優先的限制。適合學術能力強、目標是頂尖學術或高門檻事務所的學生。

義大利：米蘭理工、都靈理工、羅馬大學、IED 怎麼選？

義大利是這份名單裡學費最友善的國家之一，但三所公立大學的算法都不同：

  • 米蘭理工：住在海外的非歐盟學生自動適用最高級距，2026/27 標準修課量為 €3,883.04（含地區稅 €130）。
  • 都靈理工：依國籍的購買力平價 GDP 調整，介於 €600 與 €3,600 之間；2026/27 規章附表中台灣為 €3,446。
  • 羅馬大學 Sapienza：收入申報在海外者依國家分 A／B／C 三級，繳 €300／€700／€1,500；台灣、香港、新加坡、韓國都在 C 級。英語授課的建築相關碩士包括 Architecture (Conservation) 與 Landscape Architecture（以當年課程目錄為準）。
  • IED 歐洲設計學院是私立學校，一年制 Master 課程（例如米蘭的 Interior Design、都靈的 Social Ecological Design）非歐盟全程費用 €22,300，包含 €3,000 註冊費。它更偏室內、展陳與設計實務，和理工大學的建築碩士是不同定位。

畢業後，在義大利拿到碩士學位的學生，可以把學生居留轉成約一年的求職或創業居留，先到當地的就業中心（Centro per l’Impiego）登記求職，期間找到工作就能轉成工作居留。

西班牙：UPC 與 IAAC 的差別在哪裡？

巴塞羅那的兩所學校風格很不一樣。UPC（ETSAB）是公立大學，官方碩士 2026-27 對非歐盟學生的首次修讀學分費是每學分 €45，MBArch 進階建築碩士 60–90 學分，學費大約 €2,700–€4,050，非常便宜；但要注意 MBArch 只有 Contemporary Project 方向是全英語授課。IAAC 是以數位製造、生態與科技為核心的研究型學院，Master in Advanced Architecture 一年制（60 ECTS）非歐盟學費 €17,490、兩年制（120 ECTS）€31,800，都含 €3,800 不退還的註冊費。

西班牙的求職或創業居留許可是這份名單裡最長的：24 個月、不可延長。但申請條件是已取得至少大學學士學歷，而且許可期間不能工作，找到工作後要再申請對應的工作居留。IAAC 的學位屬於與合作大學認證的碩士，是否符合這條路徑，入學前最好先向學校確認。

奧地利：因斯布魯克與維也納應用藝術大學適合誰？

奧地利公立大學對第三國學生的學費統一很低：因斯布魯克大學每學期 €726.72（另加學生會費 €26.20），維也納應用藝術大學（die Angewandte）每學期 €752.92（已含學生會費）。不過兩校的語言條件完全不同：因斯布魯克的建築碩士是德語授課；die Angewandte 的建築 MArch 是英語授課、180 ECTS、6 個學期，等於一個較長的研究型工作室課程。

畢業後，第三國畢業生可以把學生居留延長 12 個月找工作或創業；期間拿到符合學歷、薪資達當地慣常水準的工作合約，就能申請畢業生紅白紅卡，不需勞動市場測試。換句話說，紅白紅卡需要雇主，不是畢業就能直接拿。

比利時：KU Leuven 建築碩士值得申請嗎？

KU Leuven 的 Master of Architecture 為 120 ECTS、全英語授課（也有荷語版本），上課地點在根特或布魯塞爾校區，而不是魯汶本城。2026-27 非歐洲經濟區學生學費為每年 €9,493.92（以 60 學分計），介於荷蘭與南歐之間。畢業後可申請最長 12 個月、不可延長的找工作年，勞動市場不受限，記得在學生居留到期前 15 天提出。

捷克：UMPRUM 適合什麼樣的學生？

布拉格工藝美術學院（UMPRUM，英文常簡稱 AAAD）的 MA Program in English 學費是每學期 CZK 89,000（學校換算約 €3,650），兩年制 4 個學期，建築則是三年 6 個學期。這是一所藝術學院，建築教學以工作室為核心，適合重視創作與工藝、想在中歐生活成本較低的城市讀書的學生。畢業後可申請最長 9 個月、不可延長的求職或創業長期居留。

申請歐洲建築碩士，作品集要準備什麼？

歐洲的建築碩士多半要求作品集，而且看重的方向和美國不太一樣：很多學校更在意你能不能從基地、社會議題或材料實驗出發，把研究一路推到設計。下面三件我指導過的作品，可以當作參考方向——兩件以柏林真實基地為題，一件是材料與結構實驗：

想看更多錄取作品的解析，可以讀看完這五個作品，你會明白名校想要的到底是什麼；如果你同時在比較美國的五年制建築本科，可以看康乃爾建築本科為什麼地位這麼穩、康乃爾建築本科作品集怎麼做，以及普林斯頓建築本科錄取解析。更多學生作品請看作品牆。

怎麼依目標選歐洲建築學校？

  • 想畢業後留歐工作：荷蘭（1 年求職年、期間可自由工作）和比利時（12 個月找工作年）的制度最直接；西班牙時間最長，但期間不能工作。
  • 想進頂尖學術環境、學費又要低：ETH Zurich、EPFL，但要接受只有 6 個月的求職期與較高生活費。
  • 預算有限、重視城市與文化體驗：米蘭理工、都靈理工、羅馬大學、UPC，以及維也納應用藝術大學。
  • 重視數位製造與實驗：IAAC；重視藝術與工作室創作：die Angewandte、UMPRUM。

我指導過的學生裡，也有人拿到米蘭理工、魯汶大學等歐洲名校的錄取。我的建議是：先決定你畢業後想在哪裡生活、做什麼樣的工作，再回頭比較學費和工簽，最後才看排名。

本文依 2026 年 10 月各校與各國官方資料重新查核更新。學費與移民規定可能隨時調整，申請前請以官方最新公告為準。
body.en:
When people talk about studying architecture abroad, most of them think first of the United States and the United Kingdom. Over the past few years, as I have helped students choose schools, I have been putting continental Europe on the list more and more often: the Netherlands, Switzerland, Italy, Spain, Austria, Belgium and the Czech Republic all have strong architecture schools, and at many of them tuition is only a fraction of UK or US fees, while most of these countries also offer a residence permit that lets you stay and look for work after graduation. I studied in the United States and then worked in Berlin for several years, so I know that tuition, and whether you can stay after you graduate, often shape a career more than rankings do.

This post brings together tuition and post-graduation work permits for 14 schools in 7 countries. The original was published in March 2026. This time, in October 2026, I went back to the official websites of the universities and of each country’s immigration authorities and rechecked every figure. Several numbers have already changed (tuition at TU Delft and at ETH Zurich / EPFL, for example), and I have also corrected a few common misunderstandings (Spain’s job-seeking residence is 24 months, for example, and Austria’s Red-White-Red Card requires an employer).

Rechecked in October 2026: the tuition below is for non-EU/EEA students and, unless noted otherwise, for the 2026/27 academic year. Each figure is linked to an official source. Tuition is adjusted every year; before you apply, use the school’s announcement for that year.

Why is Europe worth considering for architecture study?

  • Tuition varies widely: at public universities in Italy, Austria and Spain, non-EU tuition is often a few hundred to a few thousand euros a year. The Netherlands, Belgium and private design schools cost more, but in most cases still less than the UK or the US.
  • There is a formal job-seeking residence after graduation: 1 year in the Netherlands and Belgium, 24 months in Spain, about 1 year in Italy and Austria, 9 months in the Czech Republic, and 6 months in Switzerland.
  • English-taught courses are common, but not at every school and not for every course: this check found that the architecture master’s at the University of Innsbruck is taught in German, and that only some tracks of the MBArch at ETSAB in Barcelona are fully in English. When you choose a school, confirm the language of instruction course by course.

Tuition at 14 European architecture schools (checked October 2026)

School / course (country)Non-EU tuition (official)Notes
TU Delft｜MSc Architecture, Urbanism and Building Sciences (Netherlands)€25,633/year (2026/27)2 years, 120 EC, taught in English; €26,479 for 2027/28｜Official
TU/e (Eindhoven)｜master’s (Netherlands)€21,700/year (2026/27)€22,400 for 2027/28｜Official
ETH Zurich (Switzerland)CHF 2,190/semesterFrom autumn 2025, tuition is three times the previous fee for foreign students who move to Switzerland in order to study｜Official
EPFL (Switzerland)CHF 2,190/semesterThe semester bill, including other fees, is CHF 2,240｜Official
Politecnico di Milano｜Laurea Magistrale (Italy)€3,883.04/yearNon-EU students living abroad are automatically placed in the highest band (including the regional tax of €130)｜Official
Politecnico di Torino (Italy)€600–€3,600 by nationalityIn the annex to the 2026/27 regulations, Taiwan is €3,446｜Official
Sapienza (Italy)€300 / €700 / €1,500 (banded by country)Students who declare income abroad pay a fixed amount; Taiwan is band C at €1,500｜Official
IED｜one-year Master (for example Interior Design in Milan and Social Ecological Design in Turin) (Italy)€22,300 (full course)Includes a €3,000 enrolment fee; the course starts in November 2026｜Official
UPC (ETSAB)｜official master’s, such as the MBArch (Spain)€45/credit (first enrolment)The MBArch is 60–90 credits, about €2,700–€4,050 (excluding administrative fees); only the Contemporary Project track is fully in English｜Official, MBArch
IAAC｜Master in Advanced Architecture (Spain)€17,490 for one year; €31,800 for two yearsIncludes a non-refundable enrolment fee of €3,800; taught in English｜Official
University of Innsbruck (Austria)€726.72/semesterPlus a student-union fee of €26.20; the architecture master’s is taught in German｜Tuition, Course
University of Applied Arts Vienna (die Angewandte) (Austria)€752.92/semesterArchitecture MArch, 180 ECTS, 6 semesters, taught in English｜Tuition, Course
KU Leuven｜Master of Architecture (Belgium)€9,493.92/year (2026/27)120 ECTS, taught at the Ghent or Brussels campus, fully in English (Dutch is also offered)｜Tuition, Course
UMPRUM (AAAD)｜MA Program in English (Czech Republic)CZK 89,000/semester (the official conversion is about €3,650)Architecture is three years, 6 semesters｜Official

A few points stand out. TU Delft’s non-EU master’s tuition for 2026/27 has reached €25,633, higher than the €22,290 in the original post. From autumn 2025, ETH Zurich and EPFL charge foreign students three times the previous tuition, CHF 2,190 per semester, about CHF 4,380 a year, and they are still among the least expensive of the leading technical universities. At all three Italian public universities the calculation depends on nationality or on where income is declared, so students from different countries pay different amounts at the same school.

Can you stay and work after graduation? How do the countries’ job-seeking residence permits compare?

CountryPermitDurationKey points
NetherlandsOrientation year for highly educated persons1 year, cannot be extendedYou may work freely during this period, with no work permit required; once you have a job you can switch to a residence permit such as the highly skilled migrant permit｜IND
SwitzerlandPost-graduation job-seeking residence (L permit)At most 6 months from graduationThe 6 months are counted from the graduation date, not from the expiry of the previous residence permit; limits on paid work are the same as while you are studying｜ETH, SEM
ItalyResidence for job-seeking or entrepreneurship (ricerca lavoro o imprenditorialità)About 1 yearMaster’s graduates can convert their student residence, and must first register as jobseekers at the Centro per l’Impiego; if you find work during the period you can convert to a work residence permit｜Polimi
SpainResidence permit for job-seeking or starting a business24 months, cannot be extendedYou must already hold at least a university bachelor’s degree; you cannot work during the permit, and once you find a job you apply for the corresponding work residence permit｜Spanish Ministry of Migration
AustriaStudent residence extended to look for work or start a business12 monthsIf you obtain a job that matches your qualification during this period, you can apply for the graduate Red-White-Red Card (no labour-market test, but you need an employer and the locally customary wage)｜migration.gv.at
BelgiumSearch year (zoekjaar / search year)Up to 12 months, cannot be extendedNo restriction on the labour market; apply at least 15 days before the student residence expires｜KU Leuven
Czech RepublicLong-term residence for job-seeking or starting a businessUp to 9 months, cannot be extendedYou must have completed an accredited degree course in the Czech Republic｜Czech Ministry of the Interior IPC

Compared with the original post, this check corrects three points. Spain: the current rule is 24 months, it cannot be extended, and you cannot work during that period. Austria: the Red-White-Red Card is not something you “apply for directly, with no employer sponsorship”. You first extend your stay by 12 months to look for work, and you can apply only after you have a job contract from an employer. Italy: what applies to graduates is the residence permit for “job-seeking or entrepreneurship”, not the “awaiting employment” permit for people who are out of work.

The Netherlands: who are TU Delft and TU/e (Eindhoven) for?

The cover at the start of this article is the sloping grass roof of the TU Delft library. The advantage of the Netherlands comes after graduation: once you complete an accredited master’s degree there, you can apply for a one-year orientation-year residence permit. During that year you may work freely, and your employer does not have to arrange a separate work permit. English is widely spoken and there are many international firms, so students who want to build a career in Europe most often put the Netherlands among their first choices. The price is tuition. Non-EU master’s tuition for 2026/27 is €25,633 at TU Delft and €21,700 at TU/e. Next to a one-year master’s in the UK, that is not cheap, and most architecture master’s degrees in the Netherlands take two years.

TU Delft’s MSc Architecture, Urbanism and Building Sciences is two years, 120 EC, and taught in English. For non-EU applicants entering in 2027, the deadline is 15 January 2027, and the system opens on 15 October 2026.

Switzerland: why are ETH Zurich and EPFL still “good value for money”?

Under the fee rules of the ETH Board, from autumn 2025 ETH Zurich and EPFL charge triple tuition to foreign students who “move to Switzerland in order to study”: CHF 2,190 per semester (previously CHF 730). Even so, CHF 4,380 a year is still very low among the world’s leading technical universities. The real cost is living expenses. EPFL officially estimates about CHF 25,000 a year for a foreign student, excluding tuition.

The path after graduation is narrower. Non-EU graduates can apply for a job-seeking residence of at most 6 months, and it is counted from the date of graduation and cannot be extended. To stay on, an employer has to apply for a work permit for you. Article 21 of the Swiss Foreign Nationals and Integration Act waives the priority given to domestic workers for graduates of Swiss degrees whose work is of high academic or economic interest. This suits students with strong academic ability whose aim is top academic work or a highly selective office.

Italy: how do you choose among Politecnico di Milano, Politecnico di Torino, Sapienza and IED?

Italy is one of the most tuition-friendly countries on this list, but the three public universities calculate fees differently:

  • Politecnico di Milano: non-EU students living abroad are automatically placed in the highest band. A standard course load in 2026/27 is €3,883.04 (including the regional tax of €130).
  • Politecnico di Torino: the fee is adjusted by nationality using GDP at purchasing power parity, and falls between €600 and €3,600. In the annex to the 2026/27 regulations, Taiwan is €3,446.
  • Sapienza: students who declare income abroad are placed in country bands A, B and C and pay €300, €700 or €1,500. Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore and South Korea are all in band C. English-taught architecture-related master’s degrees include Architecture (Conservation) and Landscape Architecture (check that year’s course catalogue).
  • IED is a private school. For a one-year Master course (Interior Design in Milan, or Social Ecological Design in Turin, for example), the full non-EU fee is €22,300, including a €3,000 enrolment fee. It leans toward interiors, exhibition design and design practice, a different position from an architecture master’s at a polytechnic.

After graduation, students who earn a master’s degree in Italy can convert their student residence into a job-seeking or entrepreneurship residence of about one year. You first register as a jobseeker at the local employment centre (Centro per l’Impiego); if you find work during that period, you can convert it into a work residence permit.

Spain: what is the difference between UPC and IAAC?

The two schools in Barcelona have very different characters. UPC (ETSAB) is a public university. For official master’s degrees in 2026-27, a non-EU student pays €45 per credit on first enrolment. The MBArch, an advanced architecture master’s, is 60–90 credits, so tuition is about €2,700–€4,050, which is very low. Note that only the Contemporary Project track of the MBArch is taught fully in English. IAAC is a research school centred on digital fabrication, ecology and technology. For the Master in Advanced Architecture, non-EU tuition is €17,490 for the one-year course (60 ECTS) and €31,800 for the two-year course (120 ECTS), and both include a non-refundable enrolment fee of €3,800.

Spain’s residence permit for job-seeking or starting a business is the longest on this list: 24 months, and it cannot be extended. The condition is that you already hold at least a university bachelor’s degree, and you cannot work while the permit is valid. After you find a job you apply again for the corresponding work residence permit. IAAC’s degree is a master’s accredited with a partner university; whether it qualifies for this route is best confirmed with the school before you enrol.

Austria: who are the University of Innsbruck and the University of Applied Arts Vienna for?

Tuition for third-country students at Austrian public universities is uniformly low: €726.72 per semester at the University of Innsbruck (plus a student-union fee of €26.20), and €752.92 per semester at the University of Applied Arts Vienna (die Angewandte), which already includes the student-union fee. The language requirements are completely different. The architecture master’s at the University of Innsbruck is taught in German. The architecture MArch at die Angewandte is taught in English, 180 ECTS over 6 semesters, a longer research-studio course.

After graduation, third-country graduates can extend their student residence for 12 months to look for work or start a business. If during that time you obtain a job contract that matches your qualification and pays the locally customary wage, you can apply for the graduate Red-White-Red Card, with no labour-market test. In other words, the Red-White-Red Card requires an employer. You do not receive it simply by graduating.

Belgium: is the architecture master’s at KU Leuven worth applying for?

KU Leuven’s Master of Architecture is 120 ECTS and taught fully in English (a Dutch-taught version is also offered). Classes are at the Ghent or Brussels campus, not in the city of Leuven itself. For 2026-27, tuition for non-EEA students is €9,493.92 a year (calculated on 60 credits), between the Netherlands and southern Europe. After graduation you can apply for a search year of up to 12 months. It cannot be extended, and there is no labour-market restriction. Apply at least 15 days before your student residence expires.

The Czech Republic: what kind of student is UMPRUM for?

At UMPRUM (AAAD, the Academy of Arts, Architecture and Design in Prague), tuition for the MA Program in English is CZK 89,000 per semester (the school’s conversion is about €3,650). The two-year course is 4 semesters; architecture is three years and 6 semesters. This is an art school, and architecture is taught through the studio. It suits students who care about making and craft and who want to study in a Central European city with a lower cost of living. After graduation you can apply for a long-term residence for job-seeking or starting a business of up to 9 months, and it cannot be extended.

What should a portfolio include for a European architecture master’s?

Most architecture master’s degrees in Europe ask for a portfolio, and what they value differs from the United States. Many schools care more about whether you can start from a site, a social question or a material experiment and carry the research all the way through to a design. The three projects I have supervised below can serve as reference directions — two take a real site in Berlin as their subject, and one is an experiment in material and structure:

For more close readings of admitted work, read After these five projects, you will see what top schools actually want. If you are also comparing five-year architecture undergraduate degrees in the United States, see Why Cornell’s undergraduate architecture degree has such a steady standing, How to make a Cornell undergraduate architecture portfolio, and A reading of Princeton undergraduate architecture admissions. For more student work, see the work wall.

How do you choose a European architecture school for your goal?

  • If you want to stay and work in Europe after graduation: the Netherlands (a one-year orientation year, during which you may work freely) and Belgium (a 12-month search year) have the most straightforward systems. Spain gives you the longest time, but you cannot work during it.
  • If you want a top academic setting and low tuition: ETH Zurich and EPFL, accepting a job-seeking period of only 6 months and a higher cost of living.
  • If your budget is limited and you care about the city and the culture: Politecnico di Milano, Politecnico di Torino, Sapienza, UPC, and the University of Applied Arts Vienna.
  • If you care about digital fabrication and experiment: IAAC. If you care about art and studio making: die Angewandte and UMPRUM.

Among the students I have supervised, some have been admitted to European schools such as Politecnico di Milano and KU Leuven. My advice is to decide first where you want to live after graduation and what kind of work you want to do, then compare tuition and work permits, and look at rankings last.

This article was rechecked and updated in October 2026 against official sources from each school and country. Tuition and immigration rules can change at any time. Before you apply, use the latest official announcements.

q.en: Which architecture schools in Europe have the lowest tuition?

q.zh-Hant: 在歐洲讀完建築碩士，哪個國家畢業後最容易留下來工作？
q.en: After an architecture master’s in Europe, which country makes it easiest to stay and work?

a.zh-Hant: 制度上最直接的是荷蘭：畢業後可申請 1 年求職年，期間可自由工作、不需工作許可。比利時有最長 12 個月的找工作年；西班牙的求職居留有 24 個月，但期間不能工作；瑞士只有自畢業起最多 6 個月。
a.en: The most straightforward system is the Netherlands: after graduation you can apply for a one-year orientation year, during which you may work freely and do not need a work permit. Belgium offers a search year of up to 12 months. Spain’s job-seeking residence lasts 24 months, but you cannot work during that period. Switzerland allows at most 6 months from the date of graduation.

q.zh-Hant: ETH Zurich 和 EPFL 的學費是多少？
q.en: How much is tuition at ETH Zurich and EPFL?

a.zh-Hant: 自 2025 年秋季起，為求學而移居瑞士的外國學生每學期學費 CHF 2,190（一年約 CHF 4,380），是原本 CHF 730 的三倍；EPFL 每學期帳單含雜費為 CHF 2,240。
a.en: From autumn 2025, foreign students who move to Switzerland in order to study pay CHF 2,190 per semester (about CHF 4,380 a year), three times the previous CHF 730. EPFL’s semester bill, including other fees, is CHF 2,240.

q.zh-Hant: TU Delft 建築碩士學費多少？
q.en: How much is tuition for the architecture master’s at TU Delft?

a.zh-Hant: TU Delft 2026/27 非歐盟碩士學費為每年 €25,633，2027/28 為 €26,479；MSc Architecture, Urbanism and Building Sciences 為兩年 120 EC、英語授課。
a.en: TU Delft’s non-EU master’s tuition is €25,633 a year for 2026/27 and €26,479 for 2027/28. The MSc Architecture, Urbanism and Building Sciences is a two-year, 120 EC degree taught in English.

q.zh-Hant: 奧地利紅白紅卡畢業後可以直接申請嗎？
q.en: Can you apply for Austria’s Red-White-Red Card directly after graduation?

a.zh-Hant: 不行。第三國畢業生可先把學生居留延長 12 個月找工作或創業；期間拿到符合學歷、薪資達當地慣常水準的工作合約後，才能申請畢業生紅白紅卡（免勞動市場測試）。
a.en: No. Graduates from third countries can first extend their student residence for 12 months to look for work or start a business. Only after they hold a job contract that matches their qualification and pays the locally customary wage can they apply for the graduate Red-White-Red Card, which is exempt from the labour-market test.

q.zh-Hant: 歐洲建築碩士都是英語授課嗎？
q.en: Are architecture master’s degrees in Europe all taught in English?

a.zh-Hant: 不是。TU Delft、KU Leuven、IAAC、die Angewandte 的建築碩士是英語授課，但因斯布魯克大學的建築碩士是德語授課，UPC 的 MBArch 也只有 Contemporary Project 方向全英語。申請前要逐科確認。
a.en: No. The architecture master’s degrees at TU Delft, KU Leuven, IAAC and die Angewandte are taught in English, but the architecture master’s at the University of Innsbruck is taught in German, and at UPC only the Contemporary Project track of the MBArch is fully in English. Confirm the language course by course before you apply.

posts.abstract_en: Where can you study architecture in Europe, what does it cost, and can you stay to work afterwards? This post compares non-EU tuition and post-study permits at 14 schools, re-checked on official university and government sites on 2026-10-21. Tuition: TU Delft MSc €25,633/yr and TU/e €21,700 (2026/27); ETH Zurich and EPFL CHF 2,190 per semester for foreign students since autumn 2025; Politecnico di Milano €3,883.04; Politecnico di Torino €600–3,600 by nationality; Sapienza €300/€700/€1,500 by country band; IED one-year masters €22,300; UPC official masters €45 per credit; IAAC MAA €17,490 (1 year); Innsbruck €726.72 and die Angewandte €752.92 per semester; KU Leuven Master of Architecture €9,493.92/yr; UMPRUM CZK 89,000 per semester. Post-study: Netherlands 1-year orientation year (work freely), Belgium up to 12 months, Spain 24 months (no work during the permit), Italy about 1 year, Austria 12 months then a Red-White-Red Card with a job offer, Czechia up to 9 months, Switzerland up to 6 months from graduation. Check the language of instruction: Innsbruck's architecture master is taught in German.

title.zh-Hant: 英國藝術設計本科怎麼申請？劍橋 Design、帝國理工 Design Engineering、UCL Slade 入學要求整理（2026 年 10 月官方查核）
title.en: UK art and design undergraduate degrees: Cambridge Design, Imperial Design Engineering and UCL Slade entry requirements (checked October 2026)

summary.zh-Hant: 整理劍橋大學 Design、帝國理工 Design Engineering、UCL Slade Fine Art 與 Art and Technology 四個英國頂尖藝術設計本科的 2027 年入學要求：A-level 成績、作品集格式、ESAT 與面試、UCAS 截止日與海外生學費，2026 年 10 月依官方資料重新查核。
summary.en: Entry requirements for 2027 at four leading UK art and design undergraduate degrees — Cambridge Design, Imperial Design Engineering, and UCL Slade Fine Art and Art and Technology — covering A-level grades, portfolio format, the ESAT and interview, UCAS deadlines and overseas tuition, rechecked against official sources in October 2026.

tldr.zh-Hant: 2027 年入學：劍橋 Design 要 A*AA（數學 A*），面試前繳最多 6 頁 A4 PDF，UCAS 截止 2026 年 10 月 15 日；帝國理工 Design Engineering 要 A*AA（數學 A*）＋ESAT＋線上面試，截止 2027 年 1 月 13 日，海外生學費每年 £47,800；UCL Slade 的 Fine Art BA 與 Art and Technology BA 要 ABB＋最多 20 頁 PDF 作品集，截止 2027 年 1 月 13 日，海外生學費每年 £44,400。
tldr.en: For 2027 entry: Cambridge Design asks for A*AA (A* in Mathematics) and a PDF of at most 6 A4 pages before the interview, with a UCAS deadline of 15 October 2026. Imperial Design Engineering asks for A*AA (A* in Mathematics) plus the ESAT and an online interview, with a deadline of 13 January 2027 and overseas tuition of £47,800 a year. UCL Slade’s Fine Art BA and Art and Technology BA ask for ABB plus a PDF portfolio of at most 20 pages, with a deadline of 13 January 2027 and overseas tuition of £44,400 a year.

body.zh-Hant:
英國一直是藝術設計本科留學的熱門選擇：學制短（多數學士 3 年）、創意產業與實習資源集中，而且頂尖大學也開設了真正以設計或藝術為核心的本科課程。這篇整理三所學校、四個常被問到的本科課程：劍橋大學 Design、帝國理工 Design Engineering、UCL 斯萊德美術學院（Slade）的 Fine Art 與 Art and Technology。

原文發表於 2025 年 7 月，當時寫的是 2026 年入學的資訊。這次我在 2026 年 10 月逐項回到三校官方網站，改成 2027 年入學（2026 年秋季申請）的要求，也修正了幾處已經變動的地方，例如 Slade 純藝作品集現在是「最多 20 頁的單一 PDF」，帝國理工的 UCAS 截止日是 2027 年 1 月 13 日。

2026 年 10 月重新查核：以下以 2027 年入學為準，每筆附官方來源。英國大學每年會更新入學要求、學費與截止日，申請前請以學校當年公告為準。

四個英國頂尖藝術設計本科一覽（2027 年入學）

課程學制A-level 最低要求作品集／測驗UCAS 截止
劍橋大學 Design, BA (Hons) and MDes3 年 BA，可續讀第 4 年 MDesA*AA，數學須 A*（IB 41–42 分、HL 776，數學 HL 7）面試前繳交最多 6 頁 A4 的 PDF 作品（＜15MB）；面試時帶作品集2026 年 10 月 15 日 18:00（英國時間）｜官方、截止日
帝國理工 Design Engineering（MEng）4 年本碩連讀A*AA，數學須 A*（IB 39 分）必考 ESAT（數學 1、數學 2 兩個模組）＋線上面試；面試尾聲可用最多 2 分鐘展示自己的作品2027 年 1 月 13 日 18:00（英國時間）｜官方
UCL Slade｜Fine Art BA4 年（UCAS W100）ABB，至少兩科來自 UCL 推薦科目（IB 34 分）最多 20 頁單一 PDF（≤450MB）＋最多兩支選繳影片2027 年 1 月 13 日；作品集 2027 年 1 月 20 日 14:00 前｜官方、Slade
UCL Slade｜Art and Technology BA3 年（UCAS W102，UCL East）ABB，至少兩科來自 UCL 推薦科目（IB 34 分）最多 20 頁單一 PDF＋強烈建議附一支作品影片（showreel）2027 年 1 月 13 日；作品集截止日官方標示待公布｜官方、Slade

劍橋大學 Design 在學什麼？和建築系差在哪？

劍橋的 Design（Design Tripos）設在建築系底下，把建築、結構工程與材料科學放進同一個學位，核心是用設計回應氣候變遷與永續等建成環境的全球議題。讀完前三年取得 BA (Hons)；成績達標可續讀第四年，取得設計碩士 MDes。

和劍橋建築學位相比，兩者都以設計工作室為核心、也共享部分課程；差別在於 Design 更偏科學與技術基礎，建築則更多處理社會、政治與文化面向的問題。官方說明每學期末以工作室作品、作品集、簡報與作業評量，約占每年成績的一半，其餘為筆試與報告。

申請重點（2027 年入學）：最低 A*AA，數學 A-level 必須 A*（IB 選 Analysis and Approaches HL 7）。面試前要繳交自己的作品，PDF 最多 6 頁 A4、小於 15MB；若受邀面試，要帶近期作品集。官方特別說明作品集不需要放平面圖、剖面圖這類建築性的作品，而是想看你在視覺與材料藝術上的興趣、經驗與能力，例如素描、繪畫、雕塑或攝影；立體作品用照片呈現通常就夠了，也很歡迎各種媒材、不同題材的素描。各學院的作品集要求可能不同，以學院通知為準。劍橋 2027 年入學的申請截止日是 2026 年 10 月 15 日（英國時間 18:00），比多數英國大學早三個月。

帝國理工 Design Engineering 適合什麼樣的學生？

帝國理工的 Design Engineering 由戴森設計工程學院（Dyson School of Design Engineering）開設，是 4 年制 MEng，把傳統工程和現代設計工具與思維結合：前兩年打設計原理、數學、電子、機電與資料科學的基礎，後兩年用選修專攻方向，第三年有 6 個月的帶薪產業實習（官方列出的往年實習單位包括 Dyson、Jaguar Land Rover、Apple）。官方頁面顯示 2025 年申請與錄取比例約 7:1。

申請重點（2027 年入學）：最低 A*AA，數學 A*、另兩科 A（不接受 General Studies 與 Critical Thinking）。必須參加 ESAT，考數學 1 與數學 2 兩個模組；2027 年入學有兩個考試窗口：2026 年 10 月（報名已截止）與 2027 年 1 月 6 日（2026 年 10 月 26 日開放報名、12 月 21 日截止，皆英國時間）。通過篩選者會受邀線上面試，通常在 11 月到 3 月之間；面試最後可以用最多兩分鐘展示自己的作品或項目，所以要精選。2027 年入學海外生學費為每年 £47,800。這個課程本質是工程學位，適合數理強、又喜歡動手做產品與原型的學生。

UCL Slade 的 Fine Art 和 Art and Technology 有什麼不同？

斯萊德美術學院（Slade School of Fine Art）是 UCL 的藝術學院，本科有 Fine Art BA（4 年，W100）、Fine Art BFA（W101）與 Art and Technology BA（3 年，W102）。官方建議 Fine Art 的 BA 和 BFA 擇一申請，而且 Slade 只收你一份作品集。

  • Fine Art BA：實作為主的純藝學位，在倫敦 Bloomsbury 校區。
  • Art and Technology BA：在 UCL East 上課的跨領域實作課程，結合藝術實踐、創意編程、人工智慧、物理運算與網路技術等，作品集可以放概念圖、原型、網站、軟體或程式碼、裝置作品。

申請重點（2027 年入學）：兩者最低都是 A-level ABB（至少兩科來自 UCL 推薦科目），IB 34 分；2027/28 學年海外生學費每年 £44,400。透過 UCAS 申請後，學校會寄送作品集上傳說明；作品集是一個最多 20 頁、450MB 以內的 PDF，圖片建議 300dpi 以上，另可附最多兩支影片（各 5 分鐘、450MB 以內，只收 MPEG／MOV／MP4），第一支放作品影片、第二支可以是翻閱速寫本的影片。不要放 YouTube、Vimeo 等外部連結，因為審查時不能點外部連結；格式不符的作品集不會被審閱。官方也建議一頁放一件完成作品、每頁最多 3 張圖，每件作品標註名稱、日期、尺寸與媒材；Art and Technology 另外要求清楚標示 AI 生成的圖像，並強烈建議附一支作品影片。入圍者 2 月下旬到 3 月面試，英國以外的申請者採線上面試。

三校的作品集要求，對準備方向有什麼啟示？

把三校的要求放在一起看，會發現一件事：英國頂尖大學的設計本科，看的多半不是「像不像建築系作品」，而是你觀察、動手與思考的能力。劍橋明說不需要建築圖；Slade 想看你在學校作業以外、自己主動做的作品；帝國理工則只給你兩分鐘，逼你挑出最能說明思考的項目。以下三件我指導過的本科學生作品，分別對應寫生觀察、媒材實驗與跨領域的混種構想：

想看更多錄取作品的解析，可以讀看完這五個作品，你會明白名校想要的到底是什麼；如果你也在比較美國的建築本科，可以看康乃爾建築本科為什麼地位這麼穩與普林斯頓建築本科錄取解析；想讀研究所的話，可以參考歐洲建築留學怎麼選。更多學生作品請看作品牆。

申請英國藝術設計本科，時間線怎麼排？

  • 2026 年 10 月 15 日：劍橋 UCAS 截止（Design 面試前另需繳交 PDF 作品）。
  • 2026 年 10 月 26 日–12 月 21 日：帝國理工 ESAT 第二窗口報名（2027 年 1 月 6 日考試）。
  • 2027 年 1 月 13 日 18:00：帝國理工與 UCL 的 UCAS 截止。
  • 2027 年 1 月 20 日 14:00：Slade Fine Art 作品集上傳截止（Art and Technology 待公布）。
  • 2027 年 2 月下旬–3 月：Slade 面試；帝國理工面試通常 11 月到 3 月。

我的建議是：作品集至少提前半年開始，先決定你要的是「設計＋工程」（劍橋、帝國理工）還是「藝術實踐」（Slade），再依各校的頁數、格式與面試方式剪裁同一批作品，而不是做三本完全不同的作品集。

本文依 2026 年 10 月三校官方資料重新查核、更新為 2027 年入學資訊。入學要求、學費與截止日可能隨時調整，申請前請以官方最新公告為準。
body.en:
The UK has long been a popular choice for art and design undergraduate study: the degrees are short (most bachelor’s degrees are 3 years), the creative industries and placement opportunities are concentrated, and leading universities also offer undergraduate courses that are genuinely centred on design or art. This post sets out four undergraduate courses people often ask about, at three schools: Cambridge Design, Imperial Design Engineering, and Fine Art and Art and Technology at the UCL Slade School of Fine Art (Slade).

The original was published in July 2025 and covered 2026 entry. This time, in October 2026, I went back to the official websites of all three universities and rewrote the requirements for 2027 entry (applications in autumn 2026), and I corrected several things that have already changed. The Slade fine-art portfolio, for example, is now “a single PDF of at most 20 pages”, and Imperial’s UCAS deadline is 13 January 2027.

Rechecked in October 2026: what follows is for 2027 entry, and each point is linked to an official source. UK universities update entry requirements, tuition and deadlines every year. Before you apply, use the school’s announcement for that year.

Four leading UK art and design undergraduate degrees at a glance (2027 entry)

CourseLengthMinimum A-level requirementPortfolio / testUCAS deadline
Cambridge Design, BA (Hons) and MDes3-year BA, with the option to continue to a fourth-year MDesA*AA, with A* in Mathematics (IB 41–42, HL 776, Mathematics HL 7)Submit a PDF of your work, at most 6 A4 pages (＜15MB), before the interview; bring a portfolio to the interview15 October 2026, 18:00 (UK time)｜Official, Deadlines
Imperial Design Engineering (MEng)4-year integrated master’sA*AA, with A* in Mathematics (IB 39)ESAT required (Mathematics 1 and Mathematics 2) plus an online interview; at the end of the interview you may use up to 2 minutes to show your own work13 January 2027, 18:00 (UK time)｜Official
UCL Slade｜Fine Art BA4 years (UCAS W100)ABB, with at least two subjects from UCL’s preferred subjects (IB 34)A single PDF of at most 20 pages (≤450MB) plus at most two optional videos13 January 2027; portfolio by 14:00 on 20 January 2027｜Official, Slade
UCL Slade｜Art and Technology BA3 years (UCAS W102, UCL East)ABB, with at least two subjects from UCL’s preferred subjects (IB 34)A single PDF of at most 20 pages, plus a strongly recommended work video (showreel)13 January 2027; the official portfolio deadline is marked as to be announced｜Official, Slade

What do you study in Cambridge Design, and how does it differ from architecture?

Cambridge Design (the Design Tripos) sits within the Department of Architecture. It places architecture, structural engineering and materials science in a single degree, and its centre is using design to respond to global issues in the built environment, including climate change and sustainability. After the first three years you are awarded a BA (Hons). If your results meet the standard, you can continue to a fourth year and be awarded the MDes, a master’s in design.

Set beside Cambridge’s architecture degree, both are centred on the design studio and share some courses. The difference is that Design leans further toward a scientific and technical foundation, while architecture spends more time on questions that are social, political and cultural. The university says that studio work, the portfolio, presentations and coursework are assessed at the end of each year and account for about half of that year’s marks. The rest is written examinations and reports.

What matters for the application (2027 entry): the minimum is A*AA, and A-level Mathematics must be an A* (for the IB, Analysis and Approaches at HL 7). Before the interview you submit your own work as a PDF of at most 6 A4 pages, under 15MB. If you are invited to interview, bring a recent portfolio. The university says specifically that the portfolio does not need architectural work such as plans and sections. What they want to see is your interest, experience and ability in the visual and material arts — drawing, painting, sculpture or photography, for example. Photographs are usually enough for three-dimensional work, and sketches in any medium and on any subject are welcome. Portfolio requirements can differ by college, so follow the college’s own notice. Cambridge’s deadline for 2027 entry is 15 October 2026 (18:00 UK time), three months earlier than most UK universities.

What kind of student is Imperial Design Engineering for?

Imperial’s Design Engineering is offered by the Dyson School of Design Engineering. It is a 4-year MEng that joins traditional engineering with contemporary design tools and ways of thinking. The first two years build foundations in design principles, mathematics, electronics, mechatronics and data science. The following two years use electives to specialise. The third year includes a 6-month paid industry placement (past hosts listed on the official page include Dyson, Jaguar Land Rover and Apple). The official page shows an applications-to-admissions ratio of about 7:1 for 2025.

What matters for the application (2027 entry): the minimum is A*AA, with A* in Mathematics and A in two further subjects (General Studies and Critical Thinking are not accepted). You must take the ESAT, in the Mathematics 1 and Mathematics 2 modules. There are two test windows for 2027 entry: October 2026 (registration has already closed) and 6 January 2027 (registration opens on 26 October 2026 and closes on 21 December, all UK time). Applicants who pass the screening are invited to an online interview, usually between November and March. At the end of the interview you may use at most two minutes to show your own work or projects, so choose with care. Overseas tuition for 2027 entry is £47,800 a year. This course is essentially an engineering degree. It suits students who are strong in mathematics and science and who like making products and prototypes by hand.

How do Fine Art and Art and Technology at UCL Slade differ?

The Slade School of Fine Art is UCL’s art school. Its undergraduate degrees are the Fine Art BA (4 years, W100), the Fine Art BFA (W101) and the Art and Technology BA (3 years, W102). The university recommends that for Fine Art you apply to either the BA or the BFA, and Slade accepts only one portfolio from you.

  • Fine Art BA: a practice-led fine art degree, on the Bloomsbury campus in London.
  • Art and Technology BA: an interdisciplinary practice course taught at UCL East, combining art practice, creative coding, artificial intelligence, physical computing and network technologies. The portfolio can include concept drawings, prototypes, websites, software or code, and installation work.

What matters for the application (2027 entry): both have a minimum of A-level ABB (at least two subjects from UCL’s preferred subjects) and IB 34. Overseas tuition for 2027/28 is £44,400 a year. After you apply through UCAS, the school sends instructions for uploading the portfolio. The portfolio is one PDF of at most 20 pages, within 450MB. Images are recommended at 300dpi or above. You may also attach at most two videos (5 minutes and within 450MB each; only MPEG, MOV and MP4), the first a video of the work and the second, if you include one, a video of a sketchbook being turned through. Do not include external links such as YouTube or Vimeo, because reviewers cannot open external links, and a portfolio in the wrong format will not be reviewed. The university also suggests one finished work per page and at most 3 images per page, with each work labelled with title, date, dimensions and medium. Art and Technology also asks you to label AI-generated images clearly, and strongly recommends a video of the work. Shortlisted applicants are interviewed from late February to March. Applicants outside the UK are interviewed online.

What do the three schools’ portfolio requirements suggest about how to prepare?

Put the three schools’ requirements side by side and one thing stands out: on design undergraduate degrees at leading UK universities, what they look at is usually not “whether this looks like architecture-school work”, but your ability to observe, make and think. Cambridge says outright that architectural drawings are not required. Slade wants work you made on your own initiative, beyond school assignments. Imperial gives you only two minutes, which forces you to choose the project that best shows how you think. The three pieces of undergraduate work I have supervised below correspond to observational sketching, a material experiment, and a cross-disciplinary hybrid idea:

For more close readings of admitted work, read After these five projects, you will see what top schools actually want. If you are also comparing architecture undergraduate degrees in the United States, see Why Cornell’s undergraduate architecture degree has such a steady standing and A reading of Princeton undergraduate architecture admissions. If you want to go on to graduate study, see How to choose where to study architecture in Europe. For more student work, see the work wall.

How do you lay out the timeline for a UK art and design undergraduate application?

  • 15 October 2026: Cambridge UCAS deadline (Design also requires a PDF of your work before the interview).
  • 26 October–21 December 2026: registration for Imperial’s second ESAT window (the test is on 6 January 2027).
  • 13 January 2027, 18:00: UCAS deadline for Imperial and UCL.
  • 20 January 2027, 14:00: deadline to upload the Slade Fine Art portfolio (Art and Technology is still to be announced).
  • Late February–March 2027: Slade interviews. Imperial interviews usually run from November to March.

My advice is to start the portfolio at least six months ahead. Decide first whether you want “design + engineering” (Cambridge and Imperial) or “art practice” (Slade), then edit the same body of work to each school’s page count, format and interview, rather than making three completely different portfolios.

This article was rechecked against official sources from the three universities in October 2026 and updated for 2027 entry. Entry requirements, tuition and deadlines can change at any time. Before you apply, use the latest official announcements.

q.zh-Hant: 劍橋大學 Design 本科作品集要準備什麼？
q.en: What should you prepare for the Cambridge Design undergraduate portfolio?

a.zh-Hant: 2027 年入學需在面試前繳交自己的作品，PDF 最多 6 頁 A4、小於 15MB；受邀面試時要帶近期作品集。官方說明不需要放平面圖、剖面圖等建築性作品，想看的是你在視覺與材料藝術上的興趣與能力，例如素描、繪畫、雕塑或攝影，立體作品用照片呈現即可。各學院要求可能不同。
a.en: For 2027 entry you submit your own work before the interview: a PDF of at most 6 A4 pages, under 15MB. If you are invited to interview, bring a recent portfolio. The official guidance says you do not need architectural work such as plans and sections. They want to see your interest and ability in the visual and material arts — drawing, painting, sculpture or photography, for example — and three-dimensional work can be shown in photographs. Requirements may differ by college.

q.zh-Hant: 帝國理工 Design Engineering 需要作品集嗎？
q.en: Does Imperial Design Engineering require a portfolio?

a.zh-Hant: 不需要正式繳交作品集，但必須參加 ESAT（數學 1、數學 2 兩個模組），通過篩選後線上面試；面試最後可以用最多兩分鐘展示自己的作品或項目。最低成績 A*AA，數學需 A*。
a.en: You do not submit a formal portfolio, but you must take the ESAT (the Mathematics 1 and Mathematics 2 modules). If you pass the screening there is an online interview, and at the end you may spend at most two minutes showing your own work or projects. The minimum is A*AA, with A* in Mathematics.

q.zh-Hant: UCL Slade 的作品集格式是什麼？
q.en: What is the portfolio format at UCL Slade?

a.zh-Hant: 一個最多 20 頁、450MB 以內的 PDF，圖片建議 300dpi 以上；可另附最多兩支 5 分鐘、450MB 以內的影片（MPEG、MOV、MP4），不接受 YouTube、Vimeo 等外部連結。Fine Art 的 BA 與 BFA 只能繳交一份作品集，建議擇一申請。
a.en: One PDF of at most 20 pages and within 450MB; images are recommended at 300dpi or higher. You may also attach at most two videos of 5 minutes each, within 450MB (MPEG, MOV or MP4). External links such as YouTube and Vimeo are not accepted. For Fine Art, the BA and the BFA can submit only one portfolio, so it is best to apply to one of them.

q.zh-Hant: 英國藝術設計本科的申請截止日是什麼時候？
q.en: When are the deadlines for UK art and design undergraduate applications?

a.zh-Hant: 2027 年入學：劍橋 2026 年 10 月 15 日 18:00（英國時間）；帝國理工與 UCL 2027 年 1 月 13 日 18:00；Slade Fine Art 作品集另須在 2027 年 1 月 20 日 14:00 前上傳。
a.en: For 2027 entry: Cambridge is 15 October 2026 at 18:00 (UK time). Imperial and UCL are 13 January 2027 at 18:00. The Slade Fine Art portfolio must also be uploaded by 14:00 on 20 January 2027.

q.zh-Hant: 英國頂尖大學藝術設計本科的海外生學費是多少？
q.en: How much is overseas tuition for art and design undergraduate degrees at leading UK universities?

a.zh-Hant: 依官方 2027 年入學資料，帝國理工 Design Engineering 海外生每年 £47,800；UCL Fine Art BA 與 Art and Technology BA 為 2027/28 學年每年 £44,400。劍橋的海外生學費依課程而定，請查官方學費頁。
a.en: On the official figures for 2027 entry, Imperial Design Engineering charges overseas students £47,800 a year. UCL’s Fine Art BA and Art and Technology BA are £44,400 a year for 2027/28. Cambridge overseas tuition depends on the course; check the official tuition page.

title.en: KU Leuven Master of Architecture (Brussels or Ghent): tuition, portfolio and admission requirements (checked October 2026)

summary.zh-Hant: 整理魯汶大學 KU Leuven 英授 Master of Architecture 的最新資訊：2 年 120 ECTS、布魯塞爾或根特校區、三個 Engagement 專業方向、2026/27 非歐洲經濟區學費、TOEFL／IELTS 門檻、最多 20 頁的數位作品集與申請時程，2026 年 10 月依官方資料重新查核。

tldr.zh-Hant: KU Leuven Master of Architecture 是 2 年、120 ECTS 的全英語碩士，在布魯塞爾或根特校區上課，入學時選 Urban Cultures、Craftsmanship 或 Mediating Tactics 其中一個方向；2026/27 非歐洲經濟區學費每年 €9,493.92；需建築或相關學位、TOEFL iBT 79 或 IELTS 6.5、最多 20 頁的數位作品集與一封推薦信；非歐洲經濟區申請者一般以 3 月 1 日前送件為目標，實際截止日以官方 Application Window 查詢為準。
tldr.en: The KU Leuven Master of Architecture is a two-year, 120 ECTS master’s taught entirely in English, in Brussels or Ghent. At entry you choose one track: Urban Cultures, Craftsmanship, or Mediating Tactics. Non-EEA tuition for 2026/27 is €9,493.92 per year. You need a degree in architecture or a related field, TOEFL iBT 79 or IELTS 6.5, a digital portfolio of at most 20 pages, and one letter of recommendation. Non-EEA applicants generally aim to submit before 1 March; the actual deadline should be checked in the official Application Window.

body.zh-Hant:
魯汶大學（KU Leuven）是很多人在歐洲找英語授課建築碩士時一定會看到的名字。它的 Master of Architecture 是 2 年、120 ECTS 的全英語碩士，但上課地點不在魯汶本城，而是布魯塞爾或根特校區擇一；學費在西歐英授建築碩士裡也相對親民。

原文發表於 2025 年 7 月。這次我在 2026 年 10 月回到 KU Leuven 官方課程頁與招生頁逐項重查，更新了學費（原文寫每年 €7,771，2026/27 學年非歐洲經濟區學生為每年 €9,493.92）、語言成績門檻與申請時程，也補上課程現在的三個專業方向。

2026 年 10 月重新查核：以下以 KU Leuven 2026–2027 課程指南與招生頁為準，每筆附官方來源。學費每年可能依物價指數調整，申請截止日依國籍與學年而異，送件前請以官方最新公告為準。

KU Leuven 建築碩士一覽（2026–2027 官方資料）

項目內容
課程Master of Architecture（Brussels／Ghent），授予 Master of Science｜布魯塞爾、根特
學制2 年、120 ECTS，英語授課（另有荷語版本），建築學院（Faculty of Architecture）開設
上課地點布魯塞爾或根特校區；課程跨校區、跨英荷語碩士開設
專業方向入學時選一個 Engagement：Urban Cultures、Craftsmanship、Mediating Tactics
學費（非歐洲經濟區）2026/27 學年每年 €9,493.92（以 60 學分計）｜官方學費結構
學歷建築或相關領域的學士或碩士學位｜入學要求
英語TOEFL iBT 79 或 IELTS Academic 6.5（總分最低值；也接受 CAE、CPE、ITACE C1／C2，不接受 Duolingo）｜語言要求
附加材料數位作品集（最多 20 頁投影片）＋一封推薦信

布魯塞爾還是根特？兩個校區差在哪？

兩個校區開的是同一個 Master of Architecture，官方課程頁的內容幾乎一樣，申請時選擇想就讀的校區即可。差別主要在城市：官方形容布魯塞爾校區位在行政首都的中心，是歐洲政治與商業的決策中心，城市充滿反差，被當成建築學生的理想實驗室；根特則是「人的尺度」的城市，也是法蘭德斯最大的大學城。喜歡大城市、國際組織與都市議題的人可以看布魯塞爾；想要生活節奏慢一點、步行尺度的城市，可以看根特。

另外要分清楚：KU Leuven 還有一個工學院開的 Architectural Engineer（建築工程師）學位，和建築學院的 Architect（建築師）學位是兩條不同的路，官方課程頁也特別提醒申請者先弄清楚兩者差異。

課程在學什麼？三個 Engagement 怎麼選？

這個碩士以設計驅動研究（Design Driven Research, DDR）為核心：在設計工作室裡透過「動手做、想像與反思」回應社會與空間議題，同時修歷史與理論、建築技術與專業實務。入學時要選一個 Engagement 作為專業方向，它決定你的設計工作室與碩士論文：

  • Urban Cultures：城市動態與社會議題。
  • Craftsmanship：材料、技術與製作過程。
  • Mediating Tactics：連結空間、人與脈絡的策略。

官方課程頁列出的排名是 Times Higher Education 藝術與人文學科第 18 名、QS 建築與建成環境學科 51–100 名（原文引用的 2024 QS 建築第 37 名，以官方頁目前標示為準）。

作品集要準備什麼？

官方對非法蘭德斯學歷申請者的附加要求很精簡：一份數位作品集，最多 20 頁投影片，呈現學士或碩士階段的學術項目；格式、版面與表現技法都不限，但要能完整呈現你的學術成果，特別是建築設計，從單一物件到都市設計的整個尺度；只收電子檔，紙本不受理。另需一封由大學教師，或能客觀評估你的專業人士簽署的推薦信。

20 頁很少，所以關鍵是「挑」：與其把每個項目都放進來，不如讓 3 到 5 個項目涵蓋不同尺度，並且能對應你想選的 Engagement。以下三件我指導過的學生作品，剛好分別對應三個方向：

想看歐洲其他建築碩士的學費與畢業後工簽比較，可以讀歐洲建築留學怎麼選？14 所頂尖院校學費與工簽整理；想了解名校怎麼看作品集，可以讀看完這五個作品，你會明白名校想要的到底是什麼。更多學生作品請看作品牆。

申請流程與時間線

  • 線上申請：在法蘭德斯以外取得學歷的申請者，須透過招生辦公室線上申請，並上傳所有申請都需要的核心文件（文件清單）。
  • 截止日：官方說明部分英授課程有固定截止日，要用 Application Window 工具依學年、國籍與課程查詢；多個學院公告非歐洲經濟區學生的一般截止日是 3 月 1 日。2027–28 學年的最終註冊期限是 2027 年 9 月 22 日，之後一律不受理（官方）。我的建議是以入學當年 3 月 1 日前送件為目標，留時間辦簽證與找住宿。
  • 開學：學年於 9 月中開始（2026–27 學年為 2026 年 9 月 16 日）。
  • 畢業後：比利時有最長 12 個月、不可延長的找工作年（search year），須在學生居留到期前提出（官方）。

KU Leuven 適合什麼樣的申請者？

KU Leuven 創立於 1425 年，1968 年法語區分出成為今天的新魯汶大學（UCLouvain），是歷史悠久的研究型大學。它的建築碩士適合三種人：想用合理學費讀英授建築碩士、對「從設計中做研究」有興趣，以及想在布魯塞爾或根特這種中型歐洲城市生活與累積經驗的人。如果你更在意畢業後留在歐洲工作，記得把比利時的找工作年和其他國家的工簽一起比較。

我從 2017 年至今累積 12,000+ 小時設計教學與設計諮詢，指導過的學生也拿到魯汶大學等歐洲名校的錄取。我的建議是：先決定你想走哪個 Engagement，再回頭從舊作品裡挑能支撐這個方向的項目，用 20 頁講清楚你是怎麼思考與動手的。

本文依 2026 年 10 月 KU Leuven 官方資料重新查核更新。學費、入學要求與截止日可能隨時調整，申請前請以官方最新公告為準。
body.en:
KU Leuven is a name almost everyone comes across when looking in Europe for an English-taught master’s in architecture. Its Master of Architecture is a two-year, 120 ECTS degree taught entirely in English, but classes are not held in the city of Leuven. You choose either the Brussels campus or the Ghent campus, and the tuition is relatively affordable among English-taught architecture master’s degrees in Western Europe.

The original post was published in July 2025. In October 2026 I went back to the official KU Leuven programme pages and admissions pages and rechecked them point by point, updating the tuition (the original said €7,771 a year; for non-EEA students in 2026/27 it is €9,493.92 a year), the language-score thresholds, and the application timeline, and adding the three specialisations the programme has now.

Rechecked in October 2026: the notes below follow the KU Leuven 2026–2027 programme guide and admissions pages, and each point cites an official source. Tuition may be adjusted each year in line with the consumer price index, and application deadlines differ by nationality and academic year. Before you submit, check the latest official announcement.

KU Leuven Master of Architecture at a glance (official 2026–2027 information)

FieldContent
ProgrammeMaster of Architecture (Brussels / Ghent), awarding a Master of Science｜Brussels, Ghent
Structure2 years, 120 ECTS, taught in English (a Dutch-taught version also exists), offered by the Faculty of Architecture
CampusBrussels or Ghent; taught across campuses and jointly with the Dutch-taught master’s
SpecialisationChoose one Engagement at entry: Urban Cultures, Craftsmanship, or Mediating Tactics
Tuition (non-EEA)€9,493.92 per year in 2026/27 (calculated on 60 credits)｜Official tuition structure
Prior degreeA bachelor’s or master’s degree in architecture or a related field｜Admission requirements
EnglishTOEFL iBT 79 or IELTS Academic 6.5 (minimum overall score; CAE, CPE, and ITACE C1/C2 also accepted; Duolingo not accepted)｜Language requirements
Additional materialsA digital portfolio (at most 20 slides) and one letter of recommendation

Brussels or Ghent? How do the two campuses differ?

Both campuses offer the same Master of Architecture, and the official programme pages are almost identical. When you apply, you choose the campus where you want to study. The difference is mainly the city. Officially, the Brussels campus sits in the centre of the administrative capital, a decision-making centre for European politics and business. The city is full of contrasts and is treated as an ideal laboratory for architecture students. Ghent is a city at “human scale,” and the largest university city in Flanders. If you want a large city, international organisations, and urban questions, look at Brussels. If you want a slower pace of life and a city at walking scale, look at Ghent.

There is a further distinction to keep straight. KU Leuven also offers an Architectural Engineer degree through the engineering faculty, and that is a different path from the Architect degree offered by the Faculty of Architecture. The official programme page specifically reminds applicants to understand the difference between the two first.

What does the programme teach? How do you choose among the three Engagements?

This master’s is centred on Design Driven Research (DDR): in the design studio you respond to social and spatial questions through “making, imagining, and reflecting,” while also studying history and theory, building technology, and professional practice. At entry you choose one Engagement as your specialisation, and it determines your design studio and your master’s thesis:

  • Urban Cultures: urban dynamics and social questions.
  • Craftsmanship: materials, technique, and the process of making.
  • Mediating Tactics: strategies that connect space, people, and context.

The rankings listed on the official programme page are 18th in the Times Higher Education Arts and Humanities ranking and 51–100 in the QS Architecture and Built Environment ranking (the original post cited 37th in the 2024 QS architecture ranking; follow what the official page currently shows).

What should the portfolio include?

The official additional requirements for applicants with a degree from outside Flanders are brief: one digital portfolio of at most 20 slides, presenting academic projects from the bachelor’s or master’s. Format, layout, and technique of representation are all unrestricted, but the portfolio has to present your academic work in full, especially architectural design, across the whole range of scales from a single object to urban design. Only electronic files are accepted; paper copies are not. You also need one letter of recommendation signed by a university teacher, or by a professional who can assess you objectively.

Twenty pages is very little, so the key is selection: rather than including every project, let three to five projects cover different scales and line up with the Engagement you want to choose. The three student works I have supervised below happen to correspond, one each, to the three directions:

For a comparison of tuition and post-graduation work permits at other architecture master’s degrees in Europe, read How do you choose where to study architecture in Europe? Tuition and work permits at 14 leading schools; to see how leading schools read a portfolio, read Read these five projects and you will see what top schools actually want. For more student work, see the project wall.

Application process and timeline

  • Online application: applicants who earned their degree outside Flanders must apply online through the admissions office and upload the core documents required for every application (document list).
  • Deadlines: the university states that some English-taught programmes have a fixed deadline, which you look up with the Application Window tool by academic year, nationality, and programme. Several faculties announce 1 March as the general deadline for non-EEA students. The final registration deadline for 2027–28 is 22 September 2027, and nothing is accepted after that (official). I suggest aiming to submit before 1 March of the year you enter, so you have time to arrange a visa and find housing.
  • Start of term: the academic year begins in mid-September (16 September 2026 for 2026–27).
  • After graduation: Belgium has a search year of at most 12 months, which cannot be extended. You must apply before your student residence permit expires (official).

Who is KU Leuven a good fit for?

KU Leuven was founded in 1425. In 1968 the French-speaking section split off and became today’s UCLouvain. It is a long-established research university. Its architecture master’s suits three kinds of people: those who want an English-taught architecture master’s at a reasonable tuition, those interested in “doing research through design,” and those who want to live and build experience in a mid-sized European city such as Brussels or Ghent. If staying in Europe to work after graduation matters more to you, compare Belgium’s search year with the work permits of other countries.

Since 2017 I have accumulated 12,000+ hours of design teaching and design advising, and students I have supervised have been admitted to KU Leuven and other leading European schools. My suggestion: decide which Engagement you want to follow, then go back through older work and choose the projects that can support that direction, and use the 20 pages to make clear how you think and how you make.

This article was rechecked and updated against official KU Leuven sources in October 2026. Tuition, admission requirements, and deadlines may change at any time. Before you apply, take the latest official announcement as final.

keywords: 魯汶大學 建築碩士
魯汶 建築 申請
布魯塞爾 建築碩士

q.zh-Hant: KU Leuven 建築碩士在哪裡上課？
q.en: Where is the KU Leuven Master of Architecture taught?

a.zh-Hant: Master of Architecture 在布魯塞爾或根特校區上課，兩個校區開的是同一個課程，申請時擇一；課程跨校區並與荷語碩士共同開設，不在魯汶本城。
a.en: The Master of Architecture is taught at the Brussels or Ghent campus. The two campuses offer the same programme, and you choose one when you apply. The programme runs across campuses and is taught jointly with the Dutch-taught master’s. It is not taught in the city of Leuven.

q.zh-Hant: KU Leuven 建築碩士學費多少？
q.en: How much is tuition for the KU Leuven Master of Architecture?

a.zh-Hant: 依 KU Leuven 官方學費結構，2026/27 學年非歐洲經濟區學生的學費為每年 €9,493.92（以 60 學分計），金額每年可能依物價指數調整。
a.en: Under KU Leuven’s official tuition structure, tuition for non-EEA students in 2026/27 is €9,493.92 per year (calculated on 60 credits). The amount may be adjusted each year in line with the consumer price index.

q.zh-Hant: KU Leuven 建築碩士作品集有什麼要求？
q.en: What are the portfolio requirements for the KU Leuven Master of Architecture?

a.zh-Hant: 一份數位作品集，最多 20 頁投影片，呈現學士或碩士階段的學術項目，尤其是從物件到都市尺度的建築設計；格式、版面與技法不限，只收電子檔，紙本不受理。另需一封推薦信。
a.en: One digital portfolio of at most 20 slides, presenting academic projects from the bachelor’s or master’s, especially architectural design across scales from the object to the city. Format, layout, and technique are unrestricted. Only electronic files are accepted; paper copies are not. You also need one letter of recommendation.

q.zh-Hant: KU Leuven 的英語成績要求是多少？
q.en: What English scores does KU Leuven require?

a.zh-Hant: 官方最低總分為 TOEFL iBT 79 或 IELTS Academic 6.5，也接受 Cambridge CAE、CPE 與 ITACE C1／C2，不接受 Duolingo；在澳洲、英語加拿大、愛爾蘭、紐西蘭、英國或美國校區取得英語授課學歷者可免。個別課程可能要求更高分數。
a.en: The official minimum overall score is TOEFL iBT 79 or IELTS Academic 6.5. Cambridge CAE, CPE, and ITACE C1/C2 are also accepted. Duolingo is not. Applicants who earned an English-taught qualification at a campus in Australia, English-speaking Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, or the United States may be exempt. Individual programmes may require a higher score.

q.zh-Hant: KU Leuven 建築碩士的申請截止日是什麼時候？
q.en: When is the application deadline for the KU Leuven Master of Architecture?

a.zh-Hant: 部分英授課程有固定截止日，須用官方 Application Window 工具依學年、國籍與課程查詢；多個學院公告非歐洲經濟區學生的一般截止日為 3 月 1 日。2027–28 學年最終註冊期限為 2027 年 9 月 22 日。
a.en: Some English-taught programmes have a fixed deadline. Use the official Application Window tool to check by academic year, nationality, and programme. Several faculties announce 1 March as the general deadline for non-EEA students. The final registration deadline for 2027–28 is 22 September 2027.

source.note: 改寫自作者微信公眾號原文

posts.abstract_en: KU Leuven's Master of Architecture is a two-year, 120 ECTS English-taught Master of Science offered by the Faculty of Architecture at its Brussels or Ghent campus (not in Leuven itself), alongside a Dutch-taught version. Built around Design Driven Research, it asks students to pick one of three Engagements at the start, Urban Cultures, Craftsmanship or Mediating Tactics, which shapes their design studios and thesis. Re-checked on official KU Leuven pages in October 2026: the 2026/27 non-EEA tuition fee is EUR 9,493.92 a year (60 credits; the original 2025 article said EUR 7,771); applicants need a bachelor's or master's degree in architecture or a related field, TOEFL iBT 79 or IELTS Academic 6.5 (no Duolingo), a digital portfolio of at most 20 slides covering academic architectural design from object to urban scale, and one recommendation letter. Some English-taught programmes have fixed deadlines listed in the official application-window tool; several faculties give 1 March as the general non-EEA deadline. Belgium offers graduates a search year of up to 12 months.

title.zh-Hant: 從 ED 被拒到普林斯頓建築錄取：早申策略、文書收尾與等待放榜的心態復盤
title.en: From an Early Decision rejection to Princeton architecture: early-round strategy, essays and mindset

summary.zh-Hant: 一位學生早申 ED 哥倫比亞被拒，常規輪拿到普林斯頓建築方向 A.B. 錄取。整理 ED 與普林斯頓 SCEA 的規則取捨、2026–27 普林斯頓常規輪時程與 Arts Supplement、被拒後文書怎麼收尾、作品集三個項目，以及等待放榜的心態，2026 年 10 月依官方資料查核。
summary.en: A student was rejected from Columbia Early Decision and admitted in the regular round to Princeton’s A.B. in architecture. The post covers the choice between ED and Princeton SCEA, the 2026–27 Princeton regular-round timeline and Arts Supplement, how to finish the essays after a rejection, three portfolio projects, and the mindset of waiting for decisions, checked against official sources in October 2026.

tldr.zh-Hant: ED 被拒不代表夢校無望：這位學生早申哥倫比亞 ED 被拒，常規輪錄取普林斯頓（A.B.，建築方向）與密西根、南加大等校。普林斯頓採不具約束力的單一選擇提前行動（SCEA），申請者不能同時申請其他美國私校的早申，所以早申輪只能在私校 ED 與普林斯頓 SCEA 之間二選一；普林斯頓常規輪主申請 1 月 1 日截止、建築作品集透過選填 Arts Supplement 於 1 月 8 日前提交、3 月下旬放榜。被拒後關鍵是保留真實立場、補清楚敘事，而不是整份推翻自己。
tldr.en: An Early Decision rejection does not mean a dream school is out of reach: this student was rejected from Columbia ED and then, in the regular round, admitted to Princeton (A.B., architecture) and to the University of Michigan, USC, and other schools. Princeton uses non-binding Single-Choice Early Action (SCEA), and applicants cannot also apply early to other private universities in the United States, so the early round is a choice between ED at a private university and Princeton SCEA. Princeton’s regular-round main application is due on 1 January, the architecture portfolio is submitted through the optional Arts Supplement by 8 January, and decisions are released in late March. After a rejection, the task is to keep your real position and make the narrative clear, rather than to overturn yourself entirely.

body.zh-Hant:
早申（ED）被拒，是很多建築申請者最難熬的時刻。今年我指導的一位學生，早申輪 ED 了哥倫比亞大學，結果被拒；但到了常規輪（RD），她拿到了普林斯頓大學建築方向 A.B. 的錄取，同時還錄取了密西根大學安娜堡建築本科（附獎學金）、南加州大學等校。

這篇不談作品集技巧（那部分我在普林斯頓建築本科作品集錄取解析已經拆過），而是整理她從 ED 被拒到普林斯頓錄取的完整過程：早申策略怎麼排、被拒之後文書怎麼收尾、等待放榜時心態怎麼穩住，以及我在旁邊看到的關鍵。

2026 年 10 月重新查核：文中普林斯頓與哥倫比亞的申請制度與截止日，均依兩校招生官網 2026–27 申請季資訊更新，每筆附官方來源；送件前請再以官網最新公告為準。

她的申請結果一覽

項目內容
背景美國高中（未修 AP 課程），未加權 GPA 4.0
早申（ED）哥倫比亞大學（Columbia）——被拒
最終錄取普林斯頓大學（A.B.，建築方向）
其他錄取密西根大學安娜堡建築本科（附獎學金）、南加州大學（附獎學金）、伊利諾大學香檳分校、加州大學聖塔芭芭拉分校、華盛頓大學（西雅圖）、德州大學奧斯汀分校

ED 被拒，問題出在哪裡？

她選哥倫比亞 ED，是因為喜歡紐約的節奏感與行動力。事後她自己的檢討很誠實：一是自我定位與陳述偏「唯心」，講的是自己相信的樣子，招生官不一定接得住；二是她不喜歡被「糾錯」，ED 送出前沒有把個人陳述（PS）整份打掉重整，而是在拉扯中盡量把當下想清楚的東西塞進小文書裡。

我的看法是：ED 被拒很少是單一原因，學校的名額結構、科系配比都會影響結果，不必把它解讀成「你不夠好」。真正要做的是在常規輪截止前，分辨哪些是可以補強的（敘事是否清楚、作品是否回答了問題），哪些是不該改的（你真實的關注與立場）。她後來沒有改成一個「看起來更合理」的版本，而是把那幾個月反覆糾結的問題，寫成了普林斯頓小文書的回答。

為什麼不是普林斯頓早申？先搞懂 ED 和 SCEA 的規則

很多家長會問：既然普林斯頓是夢校，為什麼不直接早申普林斯頓？因為兩種早申規則互相排斥：

  • 哥倫比亞 ED 是有約束力的：11 月 1 日截止，12 月中放榜；一旦錄取，必須接受並撤回其他所有申請（Columbia 官方 ED 說明）。
  • 普林斯頓是單一選擇提前行動（Single-Choice Early Action，SCEA）：11 月 1 日截止、12 月中放榜，錄取不具約束力，可以到 5 月 1 日再決定；但申請 SCEA 的人，不能同時申請美國其他私立大學的任何早申計畫（公立大學、國際大學與滾動錄取的非約束性早申除外）（Princeton 官方日期與規則）。

所以早申輪只能二選一：ED 一所私校，或 SCEA 普林斯頓。她選了哥倫比亞 ED，普林斯頓就只能走常規輪。這不是錯誤的選擇，而是取捨：ED 被拒後，她的普林斯頓、密西根、南加大等申請仍然完整地留在常規輪。

普林斯頓常規輪要準備什麼？（2026–27 官方時程）

項目常規輪（RD）單一選擇提前行動（SCEA）
Common App 與普林斯頓專屬問題1 月 1 日11 月 1 日
Graded Written Paper（老師批改過的寫作）1 月 1 日11 月 1 日
選填 Arts Supplement（建築作品集由此提交）1 月 8 日11 月 6 日
放榜3 月下旬12 月中
回覆入學期限5 月 1 日

標準化考試方面，申請 2027 年秋季入學（2026–27 申請季）仍為 test optional；但普林斯頓已公告，從 2027–28 申請季（2028 年秋季入學）起恢復要求 SAT 或 ACT（Princeton 官方考試政策）。

對 ED 被拒的學生來說，12 月中到 1 月初只有兩三週：普林斯頓的 Arts Supplement 比主申請晚一週截止，作品集還有一點調整空間。她的普林斯頓小文書，就是在截止當天才完成終稿。

普林斯頓看到的是什麼？作品集裡的三個項目

她說建築吸引她的不是 permanence（永恆），而是一種「translation」（轉譯）的能力：把語言無法完整承載的秩序感、文化記憶，甚至人與空間之間微妙的權力關係，轉成可以被體驗的形式。她的興趣很散，從天文、物理、數學、哲學、政治、經濟到國畫與攝影；建築是少數能同時容納這些好奇心的學科。這條主線貫穿了她的三個代表項目：

第一個項目讓她第一次體會到，一個抽象構想怎樣同時整合人文視角、不同利害關係人的立場、美學策略和落地性。第二個項目則是把前一次從分區（zoning）、設計製作到簡報（pitching）的完整經驗，搬到暑期課程裡再用一次：大部分準備只有三天，她仍把結果做完，也拿到教授很高的評價。

她的心得很值得低年級學生參考：所謂「成熟度」不是遙不可及的終點，而是可以累積的能力——先去理解更高層級項目的執行邏輯，再回頭定義自己當下能做到的最大產出。即使暑期課程在外人看來很「水」，近距離接觸學科裡的人，也能延伸出很多可以繼續開發的課題。

ED 被拒之後，心態怎麼穩住？

  • 不要整份推翻自己：被拒後最常見的反應是把文書全部重寫成「更合理」的版本。她選擇保留真實的立場，只把糾結了幾個月的問題想清楚，寫進回答裡。
  • 允許「懸而未決」：高中最後一學期（美國 senior 下學期）她刻意放鬆，把忙碌時捨棄的生活感受撿回來，多陪家人、維繫友情。她說，比起十幾頁的申請 PDF，自己對自己的了解更清楚。
  • 放榜週給自己安排生活：她和朋友約好，無論結果如何都出去吃一頓，避免把情緒全押在單一結果上。南加大先給了她 2027 年春季入學的錄取，算是定心丸；普林斯頓則是她最後才打開的那封信。

給申請者的選校建議

她的建議是：每一所學校都有足以吸引大多數高中生的學術資源，所以官網的學校研究很重要，但也可以去看和你背景、想法相近的學生寫的文字、做的活動，去感受那個社群的氛圍，再想像一下：你想呈現的個人表達，會不會在那個學術與人際網絡裡產生共振。

回頭整理申請材料時，她才發現自己一路選修了學校最難的社會科學、數學與物理課，在每個節點展現的求知慾是貫穿始終的。這也是我常提醒學生的：與其不斷修正一個「看起來更合理」的自己，不如承認已經發生的選擇本身，就是最直接的路徑記錄，再用作品集和文書把這條線講清楚。

我的觀察：她身上的「記者特質」

這位學生是從社群平台上找到我的。之後每個寒暑假和春假，只要時間允許，她幾乎都會到工作室推進作品。她對老師的意見始終開放，但不是被動接受，而是帶著自己的觀察、判斷與反思來碰撞，常常從很不一樣的角度切入。

我曾說她有很強的「記者特質」：善於觀察、願意思考、敢於質疑，會一直追問事物背後的邏輯。這種特質不是每個人都適合，也不總是輕鬆的，但當她把這些思考轉化為建築設計，作品就不只是形式，而是她的人格氣質、思維方式與價值判斷。她也常和自己「死磕」，細節堅持到最後一刻，時間常常因此很緊；但正是這份對自我的要求，讓她一路逼近自己真正想要的表達。

我從 2017 年至今累積 12,000+ 小時設計教學與設計諮詢。ED 被拒不是終點：只要常規輪的申請完整、作品集能說清楚你怎麼觀察與提出問題，夢校的門仍然開著。想看更多名校錄取作品，可以讀看完這五個作品，你會明白名校想要的到底是什麼，或到作品牆看完整作品。
body.en:
An Early Decision (ED) rejection is one of the hardest moments for many architecture applicants. A student I advised this year applied ED to Columbia in the early round and was rejected. In the regular round (RD), she was admitted to Princeton’s A.B. in architecture, and she was also admitted to undergraduate architecture at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor (with a scholarship), USC, and other schools.

This post leaves portfolio technique aside (I have already taken that apart in an admissions reading of a Princeton undergraduate architecture portfolio). It sets out her full path from the ED rejection to the Princeton offer: how to set an early-round strategy, how to finish the essays after a rejection, and how to keep your footing while you wait for decisions, and the key things I saw while working beside her.

Rechecked in October 2026: the application systems and deadlines for Princeton and Columbia in this article were updated from both admissions websites for the 2026–27 cycle, and each point has an official source. Before you submit, check the latest announcement on the official sites again.

Her application results at a glance

FieldContent
BackgroundA US high school (no AP courses), unweighted GPA 4.0
Early application (ED)Columbia — rejected
Final admissionPrinceton (A.B., architecture)
Other offersUniversity of Michigan undergraduate architecture in Ann Arbor (with a scholarship), USC (with a scholarship), UIUC, UC Santa Barbara, University of Washington (Seattle), UT Austin

The ED rejection: where was the problem?

She chose Columbia ED because she liked New York’s sense of rhythm and its drive to act. Looking back, her own account was honest. First, her self-positioning and her statement lived on the level of belief: she described the person she believed herself to be, and an admissions officer would not necessarily be able to take that in. Second, she dislikes being “corrected.” Before she submitted ED she did not scrap the personal statement (PS) and rebuild it. In that back-and-forth she tried to pack into the short essays whatever she had managed to clarify at the time.

My view is that an ED rejection rarely has a single cause. How many places a school has, and how those places are distributed across departments, both affect the result. There is no need to take it as “you are not good enough.” Before the regular-round deadline, sort out what can be strengthened (whether the narrative is clear, and whether the work answers the question) and what should stay as it is (your real concerns and your position). She did not recast herself into a version that “looked more reasonable.” She took the questions she had turned over for those months and wrote them into her answers to Princeton’s short essays.

Why not apply early to Princeton? Start with the ED and SCEA rules

Many parents ask: if Princeton is the dream school, why not apply early to Princeton directly? Because the two early-round rules exclude each other:

  • Columbia ED is binding: the deadline is 1 November, and decisions come in mid-December. Once admitted, you must accept and withdraw every other application (Columbia’s official ED explanation).
  • Princeton is Single-Choice Early Action (SCEA): the deadline is 1 November, decisions come in mid-December, and an offer is not binding, so you can decide until 1 May. Someone applying SCEA cannot at the same time apply to any early plan at another private university in the United States (public universities, universities outside the United States, and non-binding early plans with rolling admission are exceptions) (Princeton’s official dates and rules).

So the early round is a choice of one: ED at one private university, or SCEA at Princeton. She chose Columbia ED, so Princeton could only be a regular-round application. That was a sound trade-off: after the ED rejection, her applications to Princeton, the University of Michigan, USC, and the others were still fully intact in the regular round.

What do you prepare for Princeton’s regular round? (official 2026–27 timeline)

FieldRegular round (RD)Single-Choice Early Action (SCEA)
Common App and the Princeton-specific questions1 January1 November
Graded Written Paper (writing marked by a teacher)1 January1 November
Optional Arts Supplement (the architecture portfolio is submitted here)8 January6 November
Decisionslate Marchmid-December
Deadline to reply1 May

On standardized tests, applications for fall 2027 entry (the 2026–27 cycle) remain test optional. Princeton has announced that from the 2027–28 cycle (fall 2028 entry) it will again require the SAT or ACT (Princeton’s official testing policy).

For a student rejected in ED, mid-December to early January is only two or three weeks. Princeton’s Arts Supplement is due a week after the main application, so the portfolio still has a little room to adjust. She finished the final draft of her Princeton short essays on the deadline day itself.

What did Princeton see? Three projects in the portfolio

She says what draws her to architecture is not permanence, but a capacity for “translation”: turning a sense of order, cultural memory, and even the subtle power relations between people and space — things language cannot fully carry — into a form that can be experienced. Her interests run wide, from astronomy, physics, mathematics, philosophy, politics, and economics to Chinese painting and photography. Architecture is one of the few disciplines that can hold all of these curiosities at once. That line runs through her three representative projects:

The first project was the first time she saw how one abstract idea can hold, at the same time, a humanities perspective, the positions of different stakeholders, an aesthetic strategy, and the prospect of actually carrying it out. The second project took a previous complete run, from zoning through design and making to pitching, and used it again in the summer course: most of the preparation was only three days, she still finished the result, and the professor rated it highly.

Her takeaway is one younger students can use: what gets called “maturity” is not a distant endpoint. It is a capacity you can accumulate — first understand how a more advanced project is carried out, then come back and define the largest output you can produce where you are now. Even when a summer course looks thin to outsiders, being close to people in the discipline can open many questions you can keep developing.

After an ED rejection, how do you keep your footing?

  • Do not overturn yourself entirely: the most common reaction after a rejection is to rewrite every essay into a “more reasonable” version. She chose to keep her real position, and only to think through the questions she had wrestled with for months and write them into the answers.
  • Allow things to stay unresolved: in the last term of high school (the spring of senior year in the US) she deliberately eased off, picked back up the feel of daily life she had set aside while she was busy, spent more time with her family, and kept her friendships. She said that, set beside an application PDF of ten or more pages, she understood herself more clearly.
  • Plan a life for decision week: she and a friend agreed to go out for a meal whatever the result, so the feeling would not all rest on a single outcome. USC first offered her admission for spring 2027 entry, which steadied her. Princeton was the letter she opened last.

School-choice advice for applicants

Her advice: every school has academic resources that would attract most high-school students, so research on the official website matters, and you can also read writing by students whose background and thinking are close to yours, and look at the activities they take on, to get a feel for that community. Then imagine whether the personal expression you want to put forward would resonate inside that academic and interpersonal network.

Only when she went back over her application materials did she see that she had kept choosing the hardest social-science, mathematics, and physics courses the school offered, and that the curiosity she showed at each point ran all the way through. This is also what I often tell students: acknowledge that the choices already made are themselves the most direct record of the path, rather than keep revising toward a self that “looks more reasonable,” and then use the portfolio and the essays to make that line clear.

What I saw: the “reporter” quality in her

This student found me through a social platform. After that, every winter break, summer break, and spring break, whenever time allowed, she almost always came to the studio to push the work forward. She stayed open to her teachers’ comments, and she met them with her own observation, judgment, and reflection, often coming in from a quite different angle.

I once said she has a strong “reporter” quality: she observes well, is willing to think, dares to question, and keeps asking about the logic behind things. This quality does not suit everyone, and it is not always easy. When she turns that thinking into architectural design, the work is more than form. It carries her temperament, her way of thinking, and her value judgments. She also often drives herself hard, holding the details to the last moment, so time is often very short. That demand she places on herself is what kept bringing her closer to the expression she actually wanted.

Since 2017 I have accumulated 12,000+ hours of design teaching and design advising. An ED rejection is not the end: if the regular-round application is complete and the portfolio can say clearly how you observe and how you pose a question, the door to a dream school is still open. To see more admitted work from leading schools, read Read these five projects and you will see what top schools actually want, or go to the project wall for the full projects.

keywords: 普林斯頓 建築 錄取
ED 被拒 RD 逆襲
美國建築本科 申請
普林斯頓 建築本科 案例
Princeton architecture admission after ED rejection
early decision rejected then admitted Princeton

q.zh-Hant: ED 被拒之後，還有機會錄取普林斯頓嗎？
q.en: After an ED rejection, is there still a chance of admission to Princeton?

a.zh-Hant: 有。本文的學生早申 ED 哥倫比亞被拒，常規輪錄取普林斯頓建築方向 A.B.。ED 被拒後，常規輪的申請仍完整保留；關鍵是在截止前把敘事補清楚、讓作品集回答「你怎麼觀察與提出問題」。
a.en: Yes. The student in this article was rejected from Columbia ED and admitted in the regular round to Princeton’s A.B. in architecture. After an ED rejection, the regular-round applications remain fully in place. The key is to clarify the narrative before the deadline and let the portfolio answer how you observe and how you pose questions.

q.zh-Hant: 可以同時 ED 其他學校又早申普林斯頓嗎？
q.en: Can you apply ED to another school and also apply early to Princeton?

a.zh-Hant: 不行。普林斯頓採單一選擇提前行動（SCEA），申請者不能同時申請美國其他私立大學的任何早申計畫；公立大學、國際大學與滾動錄取的非約束性早申除外。所以早申輪只能在一所私校的 ED 與普林斯頓 SCEA 之間二選一。
a.en: No. Princeton uses Single-Choice Early Action (SCEA). Applicants cannot at the same time apply to any early plan at another private university in the United States. Public universities, universities outside the United States, and non-binding early plans with rolling admission are exceptions. In the early round you therefore choose between ED at one private university and Princeton SCEA.

q.zh-Hant: 普林斯頓常規輪的截止日是什麼時候？
q.en: When is Princeton’s regular-round deadline?

a.zh-Hant: 依普林斯頓官網 2026–27 申請季資訊，常規輪主申請（含普林斯頓專屬問題與 Graded Written Paper）1 月 1 日截止，選填 Arts Supplement 1 月 8 日截止，3 月下旬放榜，5 月 1 日前回覆是否入學。
a.en: According to Princeton’s website for the 2026–27 cycle, the regular-round main application (including the Princeton-specific questions and the Graded Written Paper) is due on 1 January, the optional Arts Supplement is due on 8 January, decisions come in late March, and you reply on whether you will enrol by 1 May.

q.zh-Hant: 普林斯頓建築作品集要怎麼提交？
q.en: How do you submit an architecture portfolio to Princeton?

a.zh-Hant: 建築作品透過選填的 Optional Arts Supplement 提交，常規輪 1 月 8 日、SCEA 11 月 6 日截止，須先送出大學申請，才能在申請者入口上傳。
a.en: Architecture work is submitted through the optional Arts Supplement. The regular-round deadline is 8 January and the SCEA deadline is 6 November. You must submit the university application first before you can upload it in the applicant portal.

q.zh-Hant: 普林斯頓申請需要 SAT 或 ACT 嗎？
q.en: Does a Princeton application require the SAT or ACT?

a.zh-Hant: 申請 2027 年秋季入學（2026–27 申請季）仍為 test optional；普林斯頓已公告從 2027–28 申請季（2028 年秋季入學）起恢復要求 SAT 或 ACT。
a.en: Applications for fall 2027 entry (the 2026–27 cycle) remain test optional. Princeton has announced that from the 2027–28 cycle (fall 2028 entry) it will again require the SAT or ACT.
