q.zh-Hant: UAL MA Cities 讀幾年？學費多少？
q.en: How long is UAL MA Cities, and what does it cost?

a.zh-Hant: Extended Full Time，2 學年共 60 週、180 學分；2027/28 入學國際生學費每年 £20,240，英國本地生每年 £7,700，可分期繳納。
a.en: It is Extended Full Time: 2 academic years, 60 weeks and 180 credits in total. For 2027/28 entry, international tuition is £20,240 a year and UK home tuition is £7,700 a year. Fees can be paid in instalments.

q.zh-Hant: UAL MA Cities 2027 年入學的申請截止日是什麼時候？
q.en: When is the application deadline for UAL MA Cities entry in 2027?

a.zh-Hant: 第一輪 2026 年 12 月 1 日、第二輪 2027 年 2 月 17 日，皆為格林威治時間下午 1 點；2 月 17 日後若仍有名額，會繼續收件至額滿。
a.en: Round one is 1 December 2026 and round two is 17 February 2027, both at 1:00 pm Greenwich Mean Time. If places remain after 17 February, applications stay open until the course is full.

q.zh-Hant: UAL MA Cities 作品集有什麼要求？
q.en: What are the portfolio requirements for UAL MA Cities?

a.zh-Hant: 學校通知後 7 天內透過 PebblePad 提交，最多 10 頁（含影片任務）；要展現不同城市尺度的興趣、專業經驗與實作能力，可放研究、實驗與進行中的作品，挑選與課程契合的內容，並反思協作作品中的合作角色。
a.en: Submit via PebblePad within 7 days of the school’s notice, up to 10 pages including the video task. It should show an interest in different urban scales, professional experience and the ability to make work. Research, experiments and work in progress can be included. Choose content that fits the course, and reflect on the role of collaboration in work made with others.

q.zh-Hant: 申請 UAL MA Cities 需要什麼英語成績和背景？
q.en: What English scores and academic background do you need to apply for UAL MA Cities?

a.zh-Hant: IELTS 6.5，單項不低於 5.5；學歷為相關領域二等一學士或同等學歷，涵蓋建築、各類設計、景觀、城市規劃等；課程偏好有一年以上工作經驗者，通常不招收本科直升生，但可透過 AP(E)L 以文書、相關經歷與推薦信爭取。
a.en: IELTS 6.5, with no component below 5.5. The degree requirement is an upper second-class bachelor’s degree or equivalent in a related field, including architecture, the various design disciplines, landscape and urban planning, among others. The course prefers applicants with more than one year of work experience and does not usually admit students coming straight from an undergraduate degree, but through AP(E)L a case can be made with the statement, relevant experience and references.

q.zh-Hant: 室內設計背景適合申請城市設計方向的碩士嗎？
q.en: Is an interior design background a good fit for a master’s in urban design?

a.zh-Hant: 適合。室內設計擅長人的尺度與空間體驗，關鍵是作品集要證明你能把議題從個人或室內尺度推到城市公共空間與系統層面，例如從人與寵物的關係推演到城市共享空間規則。
a.en: Yes. Interior design is strong at the human scale and in spatial experience. The portfolio has to show that you can take an issue from the personal or interior scale up to urban public space and to systems, for example from the relationship between people and pets to rules for shared space in the city.

posts.abstract_en: A case study of an interior design graduate with a modest GPA who received six master's offers, including MA Cities at Central Saint Martins, University of the Arts London, the University of Sydney Master of Urban Design and the University of Edinburgh MA Interior, cross-checked against the UAL MA Cities course page in October 2026. MA Cities is a 60-week, two-year extended full-time, 180-credit MA; 2027/28 international fees are GBP 20,240 per year. Deadlines for September 2027 entry are 1 December 2026 and 17 February 2027 (1pm GMT). Applicants need an upper second-class degree in a relevant field and IELTS 6.5 with 5.5 in each skill; the course prefers candidates with at least one year of work experience. Applications start with a 500-word personal statement and CV, followed by a video task and a digital portfolio of up to 10 pages, and possibly a 15-20 minute online interview. The post explains how a personal project on shared urban space for people and dogs, developed through physical models, matched the course's selection criteria of moving from personal concerns to infrastructural and planetary scales.

title.zh-Hant: 從帆船與海洋環保出發，RD 拿下康乃爾景觀建築：一本主線清楚的本科作品集怎麼做（2026 年 10 月官方查核）
title.en: From sailing to Cornell Landscape Architecture (BSLA): an ocean-themed undergraduate portfolio that won in RD (checked October 2026)

summary.zh-Hant: ED 落空、劍橋 pool 後未獲錄取，他在 RD 補上一個帆船基地船屋項目，最後拿到康乃爾景觀建築（BSLA）、萊斯與卡內基美隆 B.Arch、UCL、港大 Design+、柏克萊等錄取。整理他以海洋環保為主線的作品集、活動與文書策略，並對照康乃爾官網：BSLA 屬 CALS、作品集 10–12 件且小於 20 MB。
summary.en: After ED produced no offer and a Cambridge pool ended with no college place, he added a sailing-base boathouse project for RD and was admitted to Cornell Landscape Architecture (BSLA), Rice and Carnegie Mellon B.Arch, UCL, HKU Design+, UC Berkeley, and others. This post sets out his ocean-conservation portfolio, activities, and essay strategy against Cornell’s website: BSLA is in CALS, and the portfolio is 10–12 works under 20 MB.

tldr.zh-Hant: 康乃爾景觀建築本科（BSLA）屬農業與生命科學學院（CALS），是可通往執照的第一專業學位，符合 LAAB、CLARB 與 NYSED 要求；申請必交作品集，共 10–12 件、每件附標題、尺寸、意圖與媒材說明，數位提交、總大小小於 20 MB。康乃爾建築 B.Arch. 則在 AAP，需經 SlideRoom 交作品集並完成影片面試。本文案例以海洋環保為作品集主線，ED 落空後在 RD 前補上一個「純建築」船屋項目，最終錄取康乃爾 BSLA 等多所名校。
tldr.en: Cornell’s undergraduate landscape architecture degree (BSLA) is in the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS). It is a license-qualifying first professional degree that meets LAAB, CLARB, and NYSED requirements. Applicants must submit a portfolio of 10–12 works, each with a title, dimensions, intent, and a note on media, submitted digitally, with a total size of less than 20 MB. Cornell’s architecture B.Arch. is in AAP and requires a portfolio through SlideRoom plus a video interview. This case takes ocean conservation as the portfolio through-line. After an unsuccessful ED, he added a “purely architectural” boathouse project before RD and was admitted to Cornell BSLA and several other leading schools.

body.zh-Hant:
一位從八年級就開始接觸建築的高中生，ED 沒有拿到結果、劍橋進了 pool 卻沒有學院接收，最後在 RD 輪拿到康乃爾大學 Bachelor of Science in Landscape Architecture（BSLA，景觀建築學士），並同時錄取萊斯 B.Arch、卡內基美隆 B.Arch、倫敦大學學院建築、港大 Design+、柏克萊建築等多所學校，最後選擇了康乃爾。

他的作品集幾乎都圍繞同一條主線：海洋環保。這條主線從他開帆船時看到的海面污染開始，一路發展成實驗模型、陶瓷珊瑚、堆肥系統，最後在 RD 前補上一個「真正的建築項目」。這篇整理他的申請過程與作品集策略，並對照康乃爾官網的景觀建築本科資訊。

2026 年 10 月重新查核：康乃爾 BSLA 的學院歸屬、認證、作品集規格與高中課程要求，均依康乃爾官網更新；送件前請再以官網最新公告為準。本文不列各校截止日與學費，請以各校官網為準。

康乃爾景觀建築本科（BSLA）重點一覽（官方資料）

項目內容
所屬學院農業與生命科學學院（CALS），不是建築藝術與規劃學院（AAP）；屬 STEM 認定學程
學位性質可通往執照的第一專業學位（license-qualifying, first professional degree），符合 LAAB、CLARB 與紐約州教育廳（NYSED）三個機構的要求
作品集必交；共 10–12 件作品，每件附簡短說明（標題、尺寸、設計意圖、媒材），隨 BSLA 申請以數位方式提交，檔案總大小需小於 20 MB
作品集可放的媒材徒手畫、繪畫、攝影、平面設計與渲染圖、花園設計及其他創作；用來評估視覺思考與設計能力
高中課程英文 4 年、數學 4 年（含 pre-calculus）、科學 3 年（含生物與化學，強烈建議物理），並強烈建議再多修 1 年科學
課程特色以一連串設計工作室課為核心，師生一對一；鼓勵大三出國交換（如丹麥、新加坡、荷蘭）

以上出自 康乃爾 CALS 景觀建築 BSLA 官方頁、CALS 景觀建築主修頁與康乃爾本科招生 FAQ。要特別注意：同樣在康乃爾，建築（B.Arch.）在 AAP，需透過 AAP 的 SlideRoom 提交作品集並完成影片面試；景觀建築在 CALS，作品集規格與提交方式不同。兩者是不同學院、不同申請路徑，選專業前要先想清楚。想了解康乃爾建築本科的作品集，可讀如何做出一份康乃爾建築本科喜歡的作品集與康乃爾建築本科為什麼地位這麼穩。

申請季的起伏：ED 落空，RD 翻盤

他的第一封錄取來自英國雪菲爾大學，那時他還在趕其他學校的文書。開心沒多久，就收到提前申請的拒信；更讓他難過的是劍橋——被放進 pool，最後卻沒有學院接收。後來陸續收到喬治亞理工等學校的錄取，但當時心態不好，總覺得這些學校比不上被拒的那幾所，開始懷疑自己的能力。

轉折出現在 RD 前。他決定再做一個專門為 RD 準備的作品，結果在做模型的過程中，反而慢慢解開心結、沒那麼緊張了。RD 第一封結果是卡內基美隆的 B.Arch 錄取；之後萊斯 B.Arch 在常春藤放榜前一天出結果——這個學程收的人非常少，他又是 RD，原本做好被拒的準備，結果錄取了。隔天常春藤放榜，他先拿到柏克萊，接著打開康乃爾，看到 Congratulations。康乃爾一直是他的夢校之一，他 ED 沒有申康乃爾，原本有點後悔，最後以這種方式「再續前緣」。

他的心得很簡單：等結果時心態淡一點，反而順一點。申請的不確定性很大，與其每天焦慮，不如把精力放回作品本身。

作品集主線：從帆船上看見的海洋問題

他的作品集最早定下方向，是從一個海洋環保項目開始的。我們和他聊了很多他開帆船時看到的東西：海面上的污染、海洋生態的變化，以及他對這些問題的真實感受。指導老師很快看出這不只是一個「環保主題」，而是可以發展成整本作品集的主線。

其中一個關鍵作品是模擬海岸水位變化的實驗模型：我們反覆錄製多段影片，觀察潮汐空間中污染物如何堆積。這種「用實驗找規律」的做法，讓作品不只是好看，而是有研究過程可以說。

同一條主線上，他也用樹脂、貝殼與海灘撿來的珊瑚碎片，做出一片被過度開發的海岸切片；再用陶土捏塑出布滿小孔的珊瑚單元，作為海洋生物的棲所，並把它延伸成邀請其他人一起參與的珊瑚復育行動。

補上活動短板：真實、難以複製的經歷

他自評在獎項上不算強，但活動經歷補上了一部分。最有代表性的是廚餘回收項目：很少國際學校學生願意真的去碰這種「吃力不討好」的事，但正因為如此，它和常見的紀錄片、刊物類活動拉開了距離——不精緻，但真實、很難被複製。這個項目從一個廚餘桶開始，先做成系統模型，最後做成可以運轉的機器。

他也在最後一個暑假參與鄉村實踐項目，從畫圖一路走到和工廠、老師、不同團隊溝通，推動一個 1:1 的可持續模型真正建造出來，並在上百人面前講解。這些經歷後來都成為文書裡的素材。

RD 前的關鍵一步：補一個「純建築」項目

ED 沒有結果之後，他意識到作品集雖然主題線很明確，卻缺少一個更「純建築」的項目。於是他用 3–4 週，圍繞自己平常開帆船的基地，設計了一座船屋：思考能不能把環境科學和建築結合，讓建築不只是空間，也能參與海洋生態修復。

  • 做工精細：大量切木條、切木板，用細木桿與交織接頭搭出整座結構。
  • 接上主線：沒有把它做成孤立的建築練習，而是和前面的海洋環保作品連在一起，既補上建築專業度，又不脫離個人敘事。
  • 接受意外：倒透明蠟做海水時底板有點變色，後來發現效果反而更好——海底本來就不是單一色調，而是複雜、混合、略帶渾濁的。
  • 記錄過程：畫了大量草圖與手繪，完整呈現從想法、推敲到成型的過程。

這個項目也讓他確認了自己為什麼要學建築，英國 UCAS 個人陳述與美國的 Why Major 文書都寫到了這段經歷。對照康乃爾 BSLA 官網「用作品集評估視覺思考與設計能力」的說明，一條從觀察、實驗、材料到空間的完整主線，正是這種能力最好的證明。

他為什麼能被錄取？四個復盤重點

  1. 成績有基本盤：成績不一定是最亮眼的部分，但至少沒有拖後腿。
  2. 用活動補足獎項：廚餘回收、鄉村實踐這類真實投入的經歷，讓他和其他申請者拉開差距。
  3. 表達能力：萊斯的文書兩版就定稿，康乃爾的文書在截止前 7 天才開始寫，但他的英文表達能力在學校相對突出。
  4. 心態：美本申請本身有很大的不確定性，保持好心態，相信自己會去到最適合的學校。

給申請者的建議：在 11 年級暑假前找到你的「底牌」

他最想提醒後來者的是：申請季裡最該相信的，不是空泛的「自己」，而是你寫下來、做出來的東西。不管是 Activities List 還是文書，都要問自己：我寫的這些，和別人到底有什麼不一樣？它可以有點怪、不標準，但只要有特點，招生官就會記住你。

前提是不能完全交給運氣。他建議所有人在 11 年級暑假之前，想清楚自己的「超級底牌」是什麼——一個活動、一個項目、一段別人很難複製的經歷都可以。重點不是看起來多高級，而是它夠不夠硬、能不能在關鍵時刻撐住你。對他來說，那張底牌就是作品集。

寫在最後

從八年級第一次接觸建築到高三拿到康乃爾錄取，這位學生用了將近四年，把一個帆船少年對海洋的觀察，變成一本主線清楚、材料豐富、有實驗也有建築的作品集。我從 2017 年至今累積 12,000+ 小時設計教學與設計諮詢，最常提醒學生的是：作品集的主線要來自你真正關心的事，再用不同尺度與媒材把它推深；ED 沒有結果時，與其否定自己，不如冷靜找出作品集缺的那一塊，在 RD 前補上。想看更多錄取作品，可以讀看完這五個作品，你會明白名校想要的到底是什麼，或直接瀏覽作品牆。
body.en:
A high school student who first encountered architecture in eighth grade came out of ED without an offer, and at Cambridge he was placed in the pool but no college took him. In the RD round he was admitted to Cornell University’s Bachelor of Science in Landscape Architecture (BSLA), and at the same time to Rice B.Arch, Carnegie Mellon B.Arch, UCL Architecture, HKU Design+, UC Berkeley Architecture, and other schools. In the end he chose Cornell.

Almost his whole portfolio turns on one through-line: ocean conservation. It starts with the pollution he saw on the water while sailing, grows into experimental models, ceramic coral, and a composting system, and, before RD, adds a “real architecture project.” This post sets out his application process and portfolio strategy, set against Cornell’s official pages on the undergraduate landscape architecture degree.

Rechecked in October 2026: which college Cornell BSLA belongs to, its accreditation, the portfolio specifications, and the high school course requirements are all updated from Cornell’s website. Before you submit, take the latest notice on the official site as final. This article does not list each school’s deadlines or tuition. Use each school’s website.

Cornell undergraduate landscape architecture (BSLA) at a glance (official information)

TopicDetails
CollegeCollege of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS), not the College of Architecture, Art, and Planning (AAP); a STEM-designated programme
Nature of the degreeA license-qualifying, first professional degree that meets the requirements of three bodies: LAAB, CLARB, and the New York State Education Department (NYSED)
PortfolioRequired; 10–12 works in total, each with a short note (title, dimensions, design intent, media), submitted digitally with the BSLA application; total file size must be less than 20 MB
Media the portfolio may includeFreehand drawing, painting, photography, graphic design and renderings, garden design, and other creative work; used to assess visual thinking and design ability
High school courses4 years of English, 4 years of mathematics (including pre-calculus), 3 years of science (including biology and chemistry, with physics strongly recommended), and 1 further year of science is strongly recommended
CurriculumCentered on a sequence of design studios, with one-to-one teaching; exchange study abroad in the third year is encouraged (for example Denmark, Singapore, and the Netherlands)

The above is drawn from the Cornell CALS Landscape Architecture BSLA page, the CALS landscape architecture major page, and the Cornell undergraduate admissions FAQ. One distinction matters: also at Cornell, architecture (B.Arch.) is in AAP and requires a portfolio submitted through AAP’s SlideRoom plus a video interview; landscape architecture is in CALS, and the portfolio specifications and the submission method are different. They are different colleges and different application paths, so think it through before you choose a major. To understand the undergraduate architecture portfolio at Cornell, read How to make a portfolio that Cornell’s undergraduate architecture likes and Why Cornell’s undergraduate architecture holds its standing so steadily.

The swings of application season: ED falls through, RD turns it around

His first offer came from the University of Sheffield in the UK, while he was still rushing essays for other schools. The pleasure did not last. Rejection letters from his early applications arrived, and what hurt more was Cambridge: he had been placed in the pool, and in the end no college took him. Offers from Georgia Tech and other schools came in after that, but his frame of mind was poor. He kept feeling those schools did not measure up to the ones that had rejected him, and he began to doubt his own ability.

The turn came before RD. He decided to make one more work prepared specifically for RD, and while he was building the model the knot slowly came undone and he grew less anxious. The first RD result was an offer from Carnegie Mellon’s B.Arch. Rice B.Arch then released its result the day before the Ivy League decisions: this programme admits very few people, and he was applying RD, so he had prepared himself for a rejection. He was admitted. The next day the Ivy League decisions came out. He first got UC Berkeley, then opened Cornell and saw Congratulations. Cornell had always been one of his dream schools. He had not applied to Cornell ED and had regretted that a little, and this was how that connection was renewed.

His takeaway is simple: while you wait for results, a lighter frame of mind makes things go more smoothly. Admission is highly uncertain. Put the energy back into the work itself instead of spending every day anxious.

The portfolio through-line: ocean problems seen from a sailboat

The portfolio’s direction was set early, starting from an ocean-conservation project. We talked with him at length about what he saw while sailing: pollution on the surface of the sea, changes in marine ecology, and what he actually felt about these problems. The instructor quickly saw that this was not only an “environmental theme,” but a through-line that could grow into the whole portfolio.

One key work is an experimental model that simulates changing water levels along the coast: we recorded clip after clip, watching how pollutants accumulate in the tidal space. This way of “finding patterns through experiment” means the work is not only good to look at. There is a research process to talk about.

On the same through-line, he also used resin, shells, and coral fragments picked up on the beach to make a section of an overdeveloped coast. He then pinched clay into coral units full of small holes, as habitat for marine life, and extended that into a reef-restoration effort that invites other people to take part.

Filling the gap in activities: real experiences that are hard to copy

By his own account he was not strong on awards, but his activities made up part of that. The clearest example is a kitchen-waste recycling project. Few students at international schools are willing to take on this kind of thankless work, and that is exactly why it stands apart from the usual documentaries and publications. It is not polished, but it is real and hard to copy. The project started with one kitchen-waste bin, became a system model, and ended as a machine that could run.

In his last summer he also joined a rural practice project, moving from drawing all the way to talking with the factory, teachers, and different teams, pushing a 1:1 sustainability model until it was actually built, and presenting it to an audience of more than a hundred. These experiences later became material for his essays.

The key step before RD: add a “purely architectural” project

After ED produced no result, he realized that although the portfolio’s thematic line was clear, it lacked a more “purely architectural” project. So he spent 3–4 weeks designing a boathouse around the base where he usually sailed, asking whether environmental science and architecture could be combined so that a building would be more than space and could also take part in restoring marine ecology.

  • Fine craft: he cut a great many wooden strips and boards, and built the whole structure from thin wooden rods and interwoven joints.
  • Tied to the through-line: he did not make it an isolated architecture exercise. He connected it to the earlier ocean-conservation works, adding architectural rigor without leaving his personal narrative.
  • Accept the accident: when he poured clear wax for the seawater, the base discolored slightly, and he later found the effect was better. The seabed is not a single tone. It is complex, mixed, and a little turbid.
  • Record the process: he made a large number of sketches and hand drawings, showing the full path from the idea, through working it out, to the finished form.

This project also confirmed for him why he wanted to study architecture. Both his UK UCAS personal statement and his US Why Major essay wrote about this experience. Set against the Cornell BSLA website’s note that the portfolio is used “to assess visual thinking and design ability,” a complete through-line from observation, experiment, and material to space is the best evidence of that ability.

Why was he admitted? Four points from the review

  1. A solid academic base: the grades were not necessarily the brightest part, but they did not hold him back.
  2. Activities made up for awards: real commitments such as kitchen-waste recycling and rural practice set him apart from other applicants.
  3. Ability to write: the Rice essays were finished in two drafts, and he started the Cornell essays only 7 days before the deadline, but his English expression stood out at his school.
  4. Mindset: US undergraduate admission itself is highly uncertain. Keep a steady mindset, and trust that you will end up at the school that suits you.

Advice for applicants: find your “ace” before the summer of 11th grade

What he most wants later applicants to hear is this: in application season, the thing to trust is not a vague “self,” but what you have written down and made. Whether it is the Activities List or the essays, ask yourself: how is what I have written actually different from other people’s? It can be a little odd and off the standard pattern. If it has a character of its own, an admissions officer will remember you.

That only holds if you do not leave the whole thing to luck. He suggests that everyone, before the summer of 11th grade, work out what their “strongest card” is. An activity, a project, or an experience other people would find hard to copy will do. What matters is not how impressive it looks, but whether it is solid enough to hold you up when it counts. For him, that card was the portfolio.

In closing

From a first encounter with architecture in eighth grade to a Cornell offer in his senior year, this student spent nearly four years turning a young sailor’s observations of the ocean into a portfolio with a clear through-line, rich materials, experiments, and architecture. From 2017 to today I have accumulated 12,000+ hours of design teaching and design consulting. What I remind students of most often is this: a portfolio’s through-line should come from something you truly care about, and then you push it deeper through different scales and media. When ED brings no result, calmly find the piece the portfolio is missing and fill it in before RD, rather than writing yourself off. To see more admitted work, read Read these five works and you will see what top schools actually want, or browse the project wall.

keywords: 康乃爾 景觀建築 作品集
美本 建築 作品集 主線
卡內基美隆 建築 錄取
建築本科 作品集 案例

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾景觀建築本科（BSLA）屬於哪個學院？
q.en: Which college is Cornell’s undergraduate landscape architecture degree (BSLA) in?

a.zh-Hant: 屬於農業與生命科學學院（CALS），不是建築藝術與規劃學院（AAP）。BSLA 是 STEM 認定、可通往執照的第一專業學位，符合 LAAB、CLARB 與紐約州教育廳的要求。
a.en: It is in the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS), not the College of Architecture, Art, and Planning (AAP). BSLA is a STEM-designated, license-qualifying first professional degree that meets the requirements of LAAB, CLARB, and the New York State Education Department.

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾 BSLA 作品集有什麼要求？
q.en: What are the portfolio requirements for Cornell BSLA?

a.zh-Hant: 共 10–12 件作品，每件附簡短說明（標題、尺寸、設計意圖、媒材），隨 BSLA 申請以數位方式提交，總檔案小於 20 MB；可放徒手畫、繪畫、攝影、平面設計、渲染圖、花園設計等，用來評估視覺思考與設計能力。
a.en: 10–12 works, each with a short note (title, dimensions, design intent, and media), submitted digitally with the BSLA application, with a total file size of less than 20 MB. The portfolio may include freehand drawing, painting, photography, graphic design, renderings, garden design, and similar work, and is used to assess visual thinking and design ability.

q.zh-Hant: 申請康乃爾景觀建築和建築 B.Arch. 有什麼不同？
q.en: How does applying to Cornell landscape architecture differ from applying to the architecture B.Arch.?

a.zh-Hant: 景觀建築在 CALS，作品集依 CALS 規定提交；建築 B.Arch. 在 AAP，需透過 AAP 的 SlideRoom 提交作品集並完成影片面試。兩者學院、課程與申請路徑都不同。
a.en: Landscape architecture is in CALS, and the portfolio is submitted under CALS rules. The architecture B.Arch. is in AAP, and you must submit a portfolio through AAP’s SlideRoom and complete a video interview. The two differ in college, curriculum, and application path.

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾 BSLA 對高中課程有什麼要求？
q.en: What high school course requirements does Cornell BSLA list?

a.zh-Hant: 官網列出英文 4 年、數學 4 年（含 pre-calculus）、科學 3 年（含生物與化學，強烈建議物理），並強烈建議再多修 1 年科學。
a.en: The website lists 4 years of English, 4 years of mathematics (including pre-calculus), and 3 years of science (including biology and chemistry, with physics strongly recommended), and strongly recommends 1 further year of science.

q.zh-Hant: ED 沒錄取，RD 前還能怎麼補強作品集？
q.en: If ED does not lead to an offer, how can you still strengthen the portfolio before RD?

a.zh-Hant: 冷靜找出作品集缺的那一塊。這個案例的主線很清楚，但缺少「純建築」項目，於是用 3–4 週做了一個與主線相連的船屋設計，補上建築專業度，又不脫離個人敘事。
a.en: Calmly find the piece the portfolio is missing. In this case the through-line was clear, but a “purely architectural” project was missing, so he spent 3–4 weeks on a boathouse design connected to that through-line, adding architectural rigor without leaving the personal narrative.

posts.abstract_en: A case study of a high-school student who, after an unsuccessful early round and a Cambridge pool without placement, was admitted in Regular Decision to Cornell University's Bachelor of Science in Landscape Architecture (BSLA), alongside B.Arch offers from Rice and Carnegie Mellon and offers from UCL, HKU Design+ and UC Berkeley, and chose Cornell. Facts were cross-checked against Cornell CALS and Cornell undergraduate admissions pages in October 2026: the BSLA is a STEM-designated, license-qualifying first professional degree housed in the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, complying with LAAB, CLARB and NYSED; applicants submit a digital portfolio of 10-12 captioned pieces under 20 MB, while Cornell's B.Arch is in AAP and uses SlideRoom plus a video interview. The post explains an ocean-conservation portfolio thread that grew from sailing: a tide experiment tank model, a resin coral shoreline model, ceramic coral reef pieces, a kitchen-waste compost system and, added before RD, a wooden-rod boathouse for a sailing base that filled the gap of a pure architecture project.

title.zh-Hant: ED 錄取萊斯建築 B.Arch：用一堆舊衣服回應快時尚，一本主線一致的本科作品集怎麼做（2026 年 10 月官方查核）
title.en: Rice Architecture B.Arch by Early Decision: a sustainability portfolio built from secondhand clothes (checked October 2026)

summary.zh-Hant: 成績不是最突出，作品集一度「散」和「亂」，她最後以 ED 錄取第一志願萊斯大學建築 B.Arch。整理她以可持續性與「空間如何影響情緒」為主線的作品集、用二手衣物回應快時尚的大型裝置，並對照萊斯官網：ED I 11 月 1 日截止、12 月中旬前放榜，作品集 10 頁、15 MB，兩題 250 字建築文書。
summary.en: Her grades were not the strongest, and the portfolio was at one point “scattered” and “messy,” yet she was admitted by ED to her first choice, the architecture B.Arch at Rice University. This post sets out a portfolio built on sustainability and “how space affects emotion,” including a large installation of secondhand clothes answering fast fashion, against Rice’s website: ED I closes on November 1 with decisions by mid-December, the portfolio is 10 pages and 15 MB, and there are two architecture essays of 250 words each.

tldr.zh-Hant: 萊斯大學 Early Decision 具約束力：ED I 11 月 1 日截止、12 月中旬前放榜，ED II 1 月 4 日截止、1 月下旬前放榜，錄取後須撤回其他申請。建築申請者必交作品集：單一 PDF、上限 15 MB、最多 10 頁（不含封面），不要求建築主題或專業水準，不鼓勵電腦製圖；另有兩題各 250 字的建築補充文書。本文案例以可持續性與情緒空間為主線，用回收衣物、咖啡渣磚、懸吊框架與紙地景模型，讓成績、活動、作品集與文書互相印證，ED 錄取萊斯 B.Arch。
tldr.en: Rice University Early Decision is binding: ED I closes on November 1, with decisions by mid-December, and ED II closes on January 4, with decisions by late January. If admitted, you must withdraw your other applications. Architecture applicants must submit a portfolio: a single PDF, a maximum of 15 MB, and at most 10 pages (not including the cover). An architecture theme is not required, a professional standard is not required, and computer drawings are discouraged. There are also two architecture supplement essays of 250 words each. This case takes sustainability and emotional space as its through-line, and uses recycled clothes, coffee-ground bricks, a suspended frame, and a paper landscape model so that the grades, activities, portfolio, and essays confirm one another. She was admitted to the Rice B.Arch by ED.

body.zh-Hant:
一位美國高中、修 AP 課程的學生，從 10 年級暑假前開始準備作品集，最後以 Early Decision（ED）錄取她的第一志願：萊斯大學（Rice University）建築學院的 Bachelor of Architecture。她的成績不是最突出的，作品集也曾經一度顯得「散」和「亂」；最後讓她拿到錄取的，是一條從成績、活動、作品集到文書都互相印證的主線。

這篇整理她的選校理由、作品集策略與給學弟妹的建議，並對照萊斯大學官網的 ED 規則、作品集規格與建築申請文書題目。萊斯建築的學制與 Preceptorship 完整介紹，請見萊斯大學建築本科值得申請嗎？。

2026 年 10 月重新查核：ED 截止與放榜時間、作品集規格、補充文書題目、學院規模與 Preceptorship，均依萊斯大學招生辦公室與建築學院官網更新；送件前請再以官網最新公告為準。本文不列學費與語言分數，請以官網為準。

萊斯建築本科 ED 申請重點一覽（官方資料）

項目內容
ED 性質具約束力（binding），適合把萊斯當第一志願的學生；可同時申請其他學校的非約束性計畫，但被萊斯錄取後須撤回其他申請，並在期限內繳交入學訂金確認
ED 截止與放榜ED I：11 月 1 日截止、12 月中旬前放榜；ED II：1 月 4 日截止、1 月下旬前放榜
作品集建築申請者必交，透過 Rice Admission Student Portal 上傳；單一 PDF、以姓名命名、上限 15 MB；橫向 A4 或 Letter、圖片 150～300 dpi；首頁為姓名封面，內容最多 10 頁（不含封面）
作品集取向展現創作潛力，不要求以建築為主題、也不要求專業水準；可放素描、繪畫、攝影、模型等；不鼓勵機械製圖或電腦製圖；每件作品標註標題、媒材、年份與情境（獨立或團體、課堂、暑期課程等）
建築補充文書兩題各 250 字：為什麼決心學建築、哪些經歷讓你選擇萊斯建築學院；描述一棟讓你印象深刻的建築、場所或城市，以及它如何影響你對建築的理解
學院規模34 位教師、12 位職員，本科生 131 人、研究生 62 人
Preceptorship1968 年正式成立，安排在 B.Arch. 第 4 與第 5 年之間；在學院遴選的頂尖事務所實習至少 9 個月並支領具競爭力的薪資；大四需以作品集申請第五年課程

以上出自萊斯大學國際生本科申請頁、萊斯建築學院概覽頁、萊斯建築本科頁與Preceptorship 官方頁。要特別注意：ED 是有約束力的，一旦錄取就要撤回其他學校的申請，所以只有在你確定萊斯就是第一志願時才適合用 ED。

為什麼是萊斯？她的選校理由

她曾在四個國家生活，很早就感受到空間如何改變人的情緒、行為與安全感。比起只關注某一個尺度，她更想在「從材料到結構、從光線到動線、從個體到社區」的綜合系統裡做判斷與取捨，所以建築從高中開始就是她的第一選擇。

她在 11 年級暑假第一次認識萊斯，最打動她的有三點：

  • 小規模、高密度的 studio 教學：全院本科生只有一百多人，代表更密集的討論與更直接的教授回饋。
  • 一年的 Preceptorship 帶薪實習：在越來越重視真實項目經驗的建築業，她很看重這種把學習與實踐綁在一起的培養方式。
  • Residential college 住宿學院制度：她重視一個彼此連結、互相支持的學生社區；這也正是萊斯申請文書會問到的主題之一。

她在 12 月中旬收到 ED 錄取——和官網寫的「ED I 於 12 月中旬前放榜」一致。那天她以為會提早放榜，提前一小時起床守在信箱前，點開信的瞬間直接哭了出來。

錄取關鍵：所有材料在同一條主線上

她自己的復盤是：能拿到錄取，關鍵不是某一個單點優勢，而是成績、活動、作品集與文書都盡量扎實，並且在同一條主線上保持一致。她做的項目、參加的活動、作品集的表達方式，以及文書裡的思考方向互相印證，招生官看到的就不是零散的標籤，而是一個有清楚興趣起點、有真實行動、也有持續成長軌跡的人。

她的作品集圍繞兩個核心主題：可持續性，以及空間如何影響人的情緒與行為。每個項目都從現實問題出發，把社會議題轉譯成空間語言或材料語言，而不是停留在概念層面。例如用回收咖啡渣壓製磚塊、再延伸成社區空間的材料研究：

另一條線則是情緒與空間：她用懸吊的椴木夾板與折疊 PVC 片，討論「禁錮感」如何讓空間收緊；也用折疊、剝離的紙平面，把一片湖畔坡地變成由路徑與遮蔽構成的地景。

最重要的作品：用一堆舊衣服回應快時尚

她最喜歡的作品是〈Threads of Excess〉（過量之線）。這個項目回應快時尚帶來的過度消費：人們不斷被潮流推著走，買了許多並不真正需要的衣服。她希望用一種直觀、帶有壓迫感的空間形式，讓人在身體層面感受到「過量」，而不只是在文字上理解。

  • 材料本身就是概念：她從學校社區收集大量二手衣物與鞋盒作為主要材料，讓作品直接建立在真實的消費循環之中，也逼自己挑戰更大尺度的製作與結構組織。
  • 從小草模開始：先做小尺度草模、完成初版，再一路深化。
  • 用規則收斂「散」和「亂」：最大的困難是整體配色的統一，以及衣物與結構如何形成合理的堆疊邏輯。解法是先建立配色規則，再用結構邏輯限制堆疊方式，經過多輪試擺與調整，讓作品既有強烈的視覺衝擊，也有清楚的內在邏輯。

對她來說，這個作品代表了她想成為的建築師：用深思熟慮的設計與低成本、容易取得的材料，把抽象的社會問題轉化成可以被真實體驗的空間，最後回到「人」的需求。這也正好對上萊斯官網的作品集取向——不要求建築主題或專業水準，而是看創作潛力。一件用舊衣服做的大型裝置，只要問題清楚、過程可說，就是很有說服力的作品。

同一條可持續主線上，她還做了一座收集冰川融水、以可觀看的層疊水槽淨化的展廊（見融冰邊緣），把環保從「被討論」變成「被使用」；以及一件用鐵絲與拾得物件組成、色彩飽滿的集合裝置：

從「無措」到穩定節奏

她坦言整個作品集過程都帶著一種「無措感」，尤其在看過很多高品質作品之後，很清楚自己和頂尖學校之間的差距。最難的是兩個階段：項目方向剛確定時，以及中後期要把概念落到形式與表達時——想法很多，卻不知道怎麼收斂。

轉折是建立起穩定的工作節奏之後：先把問題拆成具體任務、把邏輯鏈梳理完整，再用模型反覆驗證，帶著階段成果去討論、快速拿到回饋並修正。她住得離工作室很遠，但幾乎每個假期都回來集中製作，回到學校後也維持每週固定的線上課程推進進度。

給申請者的四個建議

  1. GPA 穩住：作品再強，成績始終是基本門檻。
  2. 作品集越早開始越好：她在 10 年級暑假前就開始接觸作品集，把時間線拉長，作品才能逐步成熟，也避免在申請前的暑假被動趕工。
  3. 學會和焦慮共處：和同學比較幾乎無法避免，但每個人的節奏不同；重點是清楚自己的短板，讓壓力推動進步，而不是被壓垮。
  4. 選校看項目本身，文書寫出連續性：真正了解學校的建築項目，而不是只看排名；文書不是羅列經歷，而是讓招生官讀到一個真實、立體、有連續性的人，並把作品集裡的項目和建築相關的課外活動串成完整的個人敘事。萊斯的兩題建築文書（為什麼學建築、哪棟建築或城市打動你）正好是串起這條主線的地方。

寫在最後

認識這位學生兩年多，她的起跑點並不算特別高，但非常自驅、懂得自我要求：每個假期都第一個回到工作室，申請前還親自飛去美國訪校，向正在萊斯就讀的學長請教學校風氣與申請細節。我從 2017 年至今累積 12,000+ 小時設計教學與設計諮詢，最常提醒學生的是 Thinking by Making——用動手引發思考，讓材料與模型替你把問題想清楚。萊斯的作品集只有 10 頁，與其塞滿技法練習，不如像她一樣，放幾件從真實問題出發、能看出「怎麼想、怎麼試、怎麼改」的作品。想看更多錄取案例，可以讀從帆船與海洋環保出發，RD 拿下康乃爾景觀建築、看完這五個作品，你會明白名校想要的到底是什麼，或直接瀏覽作品牆。
body.en:
A student at a US high school, taking AP courses, began preparing her portfolio before the summer of 10th grade and was admitted by Early Decision (ED) to her first choice: the Bachelor of Architecture at Rice University’s School of Architecture. Her grades were not the strongest, and the portfolio at one point looked “scattered” and “messy.” What won her the offer was a through-line on which the grades, the activities, the portfolio, and the essays all confirmed one another.

This post sets out her reasons for choosing the school, her portfolio strategy, and her advice for younger students, set against the ED rules, portfolio specifications, and architecture application essay prompts on Rice’s website. For a full account of Rice Architecture’s degree structure and the Preceptorship, see Is Rice University’s undergraduate architecture worth applying to?.

Rechecked in October 2026: ED deadlines and decision dates, portfolio specifications, supplement essay prompts, the size of the school, and the Preceptorship are all updated from the Rice University admission office and the School of Architecture website. Before you submit, take the latest notice on the official site as final. This article does not list tuition or language scores. Use the official website.

Rice undergraduate architecture ED application at a glance (official information)

TopicDetails
Nature of EDBinding, for students who treat Rice as their first choice. You may apply at the same time to non-binding plans at other schools, but if Rice admits you, you must withdraw your other applications and pay the enrollment deposit by the deadline to confirm
ED deadlines and decisionsED I: deadline November 1, decisions by mid-December; ED II: deadline January 4, decisions by late January
PortfolioRequired of architecture applicants, uploaded through the Rice Admission Student Portal; a single PDF, named with your name, maximum 15 MB; landscape A4 or Letter, images at 150–300 dpi; the first page is a cover with your name, and the content is at most 10 pages (not including the cover)
Portfolio approachShows creative potential, and does not require an architecture theme or a professional standard; sketches, paintings, photography, models, and similar work may be included; mechanical drawings and computer drawings are discouraged; label each work with a title, media, year, and context (independent or group, a class, a summer course, and so on)
Architecture supplement essaysTwo prompts of 250 words each: why you are determined to study architecture, and which experiences led you to choose the Rice School of Architecture; describe a building, place, or city that left a strong impression, and how it affected your understanding of architecture
Size of the school34 faculty, 12 staff, 131 undergraduates, and 62 graduate students
PreceptorshipFormally established in 1968, placed between year 4 and year 5 of the B.Arch.; an internship of at least 9 months at a leading firm selected by the school, paid a competitive salary; in the fourth year, students must apply to the fifth-year curriculum with a portfolio

The above comes from the Rice University international undergraduate application page, the Rice School of Architecture overview page, the Rice undergraduate architecture page, and the official Preceptorship page. One point matters: ED is binding. Once you are admitted, you must withdraw your applications to other schools, so ED fits only when you are sure Rice is your first choice.

Why Rice? Her reasons for choosing the school

She has lived in four countries and, from early on, felt how space changes a person’s emotions, behavior, and sense of safety. More than focusing on a single scale, she wanted to judge and choose inside an integrated system “from material to structure, from light to circulation, from the individual to the community,” so from high school on, architecture has been her first choice.

She first got to know Rice in the summer of 11th grade. Three things moved her most:

  • Small-scale, high-density studio teaching: the whole school has only a hundred-plus undergraduates, which means denser discussion and more direct feedback from professors.
  • A one-year paid Preceptorship internship: in a profession that cares more and more about real project experience, she valued this way of training, which binds learning and practice together.
  • The residential college system: she values a student community that is connected and mutually supportive. This is also one of the themes Rice’s application essays ask about.

She received her ED offer in mid-December, consistent with the website’s line that “ED I decisions are released by mid-December.” That day she thought the decisions might come out early. She got up an hour early and waited at her inbox, and the moment she opened the letter she burst into tears.

The key to the offer: every part on the same through-line

Her own review is this: the offer did not come from one single advantage. The grades, activities, portfolio, and essays were each made as solid as she could make them, and kept consistent on the same through-line. The projects she made, the activities she joined, the way the portfolio speaks, and the direction of thought in the essays confirm one another. What an admissions officer sees is not a scatter of labels, but a person with a clear starting point of interest, real action, and a continuing path of growth.

Her portfolio turns on two core themes: sustainability, and how space affects a person’s emotions and behavior. Every project starts from a real problem and translates a social issue into spatial language or material language, rather than staying at the level of a concept. One example is a material study that presses recycled coffee grounds into bricks and then extends them into a community space:

The other line is emotion and space. With suspended basswood plywood and folded PVC sheets, she discusses how a “sense of confinement” tightens space. With folded and peeled paper planes, she turns a lakeside slope into a landscape of paths and shelter.

The most important work: answering fast fashion with a pile of old clothes

Her favorite work is Threads of Excess. The project responds to the overconsumption that fast fashion produces: people are continually pushed along by trends and buy many clothes they do not truly need. She wanted a direct, oppressive spatial form so that people would feel “excess” in the body, and not only understand it in words.

  • The material itself is the concept: she collected a large amount of secondhand clothes and shoeboxes from the school community as the main materials, so the work sits directly inside a real cycle of consumption, and so she had to challenge herself at a larger scale of making and structural organization.
  • Start from a small study model: she made a small-scale study model first, finished a first version, and then kept developing it.
  • Use rules to pull in the “scatter” and the “mess”: the hardest part was unifying the overall color, and finding a reasonable stacking logic between the clothes and the structure. The way through was to set color rules first, then use structural logic to limit how things stacked. After many rounds of trial placement and adjustment, the work had a strong visual impact and a clear internal logic.

For her, this work stands for the architect she wants to become: with carefully considered design and low-cost, easy-to-find materials, turn an abstract social problem into a space that can actually be experienced, and come back at the end to what people need. This also lines up with the portfolio approach on Rice’s website — it does not ask for an architecture theme or a professional standard, and it looks at creative potential. A large installation made from old clothes, when the problem is clear and the process can be told, is a very persuasive work.

On the same sustainability through-line, she also made a gallery that collects glacial meltwater and purifies it in a stack of tanks you can watch (see Edge of Thaw), turning environmental care from “something discussed” into “something used”; and a richly colored assemblage of wire and found objects:

From feeling at a loss to a steady rhythm

She is frank that the whole portfolio process carried a feeling of being at a loss, especially after she had seen a lot of high-quality work and could see clearly the gap between herself and the top schools. Two stages were the hardest: when a project’s direction had just been set, and the middle-to-late stage, when the concept had to land in form and presentation. She had many ideas and did not know how to bring them in.

The turn came after she built a steady working rhythm: break the problem into concrete tasks, sort the chain of logic out fully, then test it again and again with models, take each stage’s result into discussion, get feedback quickly, and revise. She lived far from the studio, but almost every holiday she came back to make work intensively, and after she returned to school she kept a fixed online class each week to move the work forward.

Four pieces of advice for applicants

  1. Hold the GPA steady: however strong the work is, grades remain the basic threshold.
  2. Start the portfolio as early as you can: she began working with a portfolio before the summer of 10th grade. A longer timeline lets the work mature step by step, and keeps the summer before applications from turning into a forced rush.
  3. Learn to live with the anxiety: comparing yourself with classmates is almost impossible to avoid, but everyone’s pace is different. Know your own weak points, and let the pressure push you forward instead of crushing you.
  4. Choose a school by its projects, and write continuity into the essays: really understand a school’s architecture projects, not only its ranking. An essay is not a list of experiences. It lets an admissions officer read a real, rounded person with continuity, and it strings the projects in the portfolio together with architecture-related extracurriculars into a complete personal narrative. Rice’s two architecture essays (why study architecture, and which building or city moved you) are exactly where that through-line gets tied together.

In closing

I have known this student for more than two years. Her starting point was not especially high, but she is strongly self-driven and knows how to demand things of herself: every holiday she was the first one back in the studio, and before applying she flew to the United States herself to visit the school and ask a senior student then at Rice about the culture and the details of applying. From 2017 to today I have accumulated 12,000+ hours of design teaching and design consulting. What I remind students of most often is Thinking by Making — use making to spark thinking, and let materials and models think the problem through for you. Rice’s portfolio is only 10 pages. Like her, put in a few works that start from a real problem and show “how you thought, how you tried, and how you changed it,” rather than packing the pages with technique exercises. To see more admitted cases, read From sailing and ocean conservation to Cornell Landscape Architecture in RD, Read these five works and you will see what top schools actually want, or browse the project wall.

keywords: 萊斯大學 建築 ED
快時尚 建築作品集
可持續 建築作品集 案例
萊斯 建築 補充文書

q.zh-Hant: 萊斯大學的 Early Decision 有約束力嗎？什麼時候放榜？
q.en: Is Rice University’s Early Decision binding? When are decisions released?

a.zh-Hant: 有。萊斯 ED 是具約束力的計畫，可同時申請其他學校的非約束性計畫，但被萊斯錄取後必須撤回其他申請。ED I 於 11 月 1 日截止、12 月中旬前放榜；ED II 於 1 月 4 日截止、1 月下旬前放榜。
a.en: Yes. Rice ED is a binding plan. You may apply at the same time to non-binding plans at other schools, but if Rice admits you, you must withdraw your other applications. ED I closes on November 1, with decisions by mid-December. ED II closes on January 4, with decisions by late January.

q.zh-Hant: 萊斯建築作品集有什麼規格？
q.en: What are the specifications for the Rice Architecture portfolio?

a.zh-Hant: 透過 Rice Admission Student Portal 上傳單一 PDF，以姓名命名、上限 15 MB；橫向 A4 或 Letter、圖片 150～300 dpi；首頁為姓名封面，內容最多 10 頁（不含封面）。每件作品標註標題、媒材、年份與製作情境。
a.en: Upload a single PDF through the Rice Admission Student Portal, named with your name, with a maximum of 15 MB. Use landscape A4 or Letter, with images at 150–300 dpi. The first page is a cover with your name, and the content is at most 10 pages (not including the cover). Label each work with a title, media, year, and the context in which it was made.

q.zh-Hant: 萊斯建築作品集一定要放建築作品嗎？
q.en: Does the Rice Architecture portfolio have to include architecture work?

a.zh-Hant: 不一定。官網說作品集用來展現創作潛力，不要求以建築為主題、也不要求專業水準，可放素描、繪畫、攝影、模型等；建築或設計作品可以放，但不鼓勵機械製圖或電腦製圖。
a.en: Not necessarily. The website says the portfolio is used to show creative potential. It does not require an architecture theme, and it does not require a professional standard. Sketches, paintings, photography, models, and similar work may be included. Architecture or design work may be included, but mechanical drawings and computer drawings are discouraged.

q.zh-Hant: 萊斯建築申請要寫哪些補充文書？
q.en: Which supplement essays does a Rice Architecture application require?

a.zh-Hant: 除了萊斯共同的補充文書外，建築申請者另有兩題各 250 字：為什麼決心學建築、哪些經歷讓你選擇萊斯建築學院；以及描述一棟讓你印象深刻的建築、場所或城市，並反思它如何影響你對建築的理解。
a.en: Besides Rice’s shared supplement essays, architecture applicants have two further prompts of 250 words each: why you are determined to study architecture, and which experiences led you to choose the Rice School of Architecture; and describe a building, place, or city that left a strong impression, and reflect on how it affected your understanding of architecture.

q.zh-Hant: 成績不是最突出，怎麼讓作品集更有說服力？
q.en: If your grades are not the strongest, how do you make the portfolio more persuasive?

a.zh-Hant: 讓成績、活動、作品集與文書在同一條主線上互相印證。這個案例以可持續性與「空間如何影響情緒」為主線，每個項目都從現實問題出發，例如用二手衣物做大型裝置回應快時尚，並用配色規則與結構邏輯把作品從「散」收斂到清楚。
a.en: Let the grades, activities, portfolio, and essays confirm one another on the same through-line. This case uses sustainability and “how space affects emotion” as the through-line. Every project starts from a real problem, for example a large installation of secondhand clothes answering fast fashion, and color rules plus structural logic pull the work from “scattered” into something clear.

posts.abstract_en: A case study of a US high-school student (AP curriculum) admitted by Early Decision to her first choice, the Bachelor of Architecture at Rice University's School of Architecture. Facts were cross-checked against Rice admission and Rice School of Architecture pages in October 2026: Early Decision is binding; ED I closes November 1 with decisions by mid-December, ED II closes January 4 with decisions by late January; architecture applicants upload a single PDF portfolio of up to 10 pages plus a title page, 15 MB maximum, which should show creative potential and need not be architectural or professional, with mechanical or computer drafting discouraged; two 250-word architecture essays are required. The school has 34 faculty, 131 undergraduate and 62 graduate students, and a Preceptorship of at least nine paid months between the fourth and fifth years. The post explains a portfolio thread of sustainability and how space shapes emotion and behaviour: a large installation of secondhand clothes and shoeboxes responding to fast fashion, coffee-ground bricks, a suspended basswood and PVC frame, a folded-paper landscape and a wire assemblage, with grades, activities, portfolio and essays reinforcing one narrative.

title.zh-Hant: 一本作品集拿下賓大 M.Arch 與事務所實習：用實體模型讓作品集有溫度（2026 年 10 月官方查核）
title.en: One portfolio for a UPenn M.Arch offer and an internship: physical models that give a portfolio warmth (checked October 2026)

summary.zh-Hant: GPA 3.1、雅思 6.5，他靠一本四個項目、一條主題的作品集，錄取賓大 Weitzman M.Arch、魯汶、UCL、密西根與聖路易華盛頓大學，還拿到事務所實習。整理他用實體模型取代部分圖面、以哈爾科夫戰後重建競圖為核心的作品集策略，並對照賓大官網：2027 年 1 月 6 日截止、作品集單一 PDF 30 MB／20 頁。
summary.en: With a GPA of 3.1 and IELTS 6.5, he used one portfolio of four projects on a single theme to gain admission to the University of Pennsylvania Weitzman M.Arch, KU Leuven, UCL, the University of Michigan, and Washington University in St. Louis, and he also received a practice internship. This post sets out his strategy of replacing some drawings with physical models, centered on a Kharkiv post-war reconstruction competition, and checks it against the Penn website: a deadline of January 6, 2027, and a single PDF of 30 MB and 20 pages.

tldr.zh-Hant: 賓大 Weitzman 設計學院 M.Arch 2027 秋季入學：2027 年 1 月 6 日美東 23:59 截止、3 月 4 日放榜、申請費 80 美元；需作品集、3 封推薦信、500 字以內 Personal Statement 與 Community Essay、成績單、履歷與英語成績（建議 IELTS 7 各項 7 或 TOEFL 100 各項 25）。作品集為單一 PDF、30 MB 以內、最多 20 頁，審查重點是連貫地展現視覺與空間能力及對材料與構造的理解，而非建築設計熟練度。本文案例用一條主題串起四個本科項目，並以雷射切割與 3D 列印的實體模型取代部分圖面，錄取賓大等 M.Arch。
tldr.en: University of Pennsylvania Weitzman School of Design M.Arch for fall 2027 entry: the deadline is January 6, 2027 at 23:59 Eastern Time, decisions are released on March 4, and the application fee is USD 80. Required materials are a portfolio, 3 letters of recommendation, a Personal Statement and a Community Essay of no more than 500 words, transcripts, a resume, and an English score (suggested IELTS 7 with 7 in each band, or TOEFL 100 with 25 in each section). The portfolio is a single PDF of no more than 30 MB and at most 20 pages. Review looks for a coherent demonstration of visual and spatial ability and an understanding of materials and construction, rather than proficiency in architectural design. The case here threads four undergraduate projects on one theme, replaces some drawings with laser-cut and 3D-printed physical models, and gained M.Arch admission at Penn and other schools.

body.zh-Hant:
一位寧波諾丁漢大學建築本科畢業生，GPA 3.1、雅思 6.5，在本科學校課設成績並不突出的情況下，靠一本作品集拿到賓夕法尼亞大學（UPenn）Weitzman 設計學院 Master of Architecture，以及魯汶大學 Master of Architecture、倫敦大學學院（UCL）MArch Architectural Design、密西根大學安娜堡與聖路易華盛頓大學的 M.Arch 錄取；他收到的第一封錄取來自賓州州立大學，並附獎學金與助教（TA）機會。同一本作品集，也讓他在申請季期間拿到心儀事務所的實習機會。

這篇整理他的作品集策略——四個項目一條主題、用實體模型取代一部分圖面、從本科既有項目整理而不是全部重做——並對照賓大 Weitzman 官網 2027 秋季入學的 M.Arch 申請規定。

2026 年 10 月重新查核：截止日、放榜日、申請費、作品集規格與英語成績建議，均依賓大 Weitzman 設計學院官網（Fall 2027 申請週期）更新；學生當年的分數與錄取屬個人經驗，送件前請再以官網最新公告為準。

賓大 M.Arch 2027 秋季申請重點一覽（官方資料）

項目內容
截止日2027 年 1 月 6 日美東時間 23:59（M.Arch、MS Arch 及多數 MSD 項目）；MLA、MCP 等為 1 月 13 日
放榜2027 年 3 月 4 日美東時間中午 12 點
申請費80 美元，不退費，送出申請時以信用卡支付
M.Arch 申請材料線上申請、作品集、3 封推薦信、Personal Statement（500 字以內）與 Community Essay、成績單／學歷認證、履歷、國際生英語成績；M.Arch 另列有先修要求（prerequisites）
作品集規格單一 PDF、不超過 30 MB、最多 20 頁（封面與目錄不計）；不接受網站或紙本作品集；送出後不能再修改或替換
作品集看什麼官網說明：審查教師比較不看建築設計的熟練度，而是看能否連貫地展現視覺與空間能力，並建立在對材料與構造的基本理解之上；可放繪畫、雕塑、攝影、平面／工業／室內設計與建築、景觀、城市設計
英語成績（建議最低）IELTS 總分 7、各項 7；TOEFL（2026 年 1 月 21 日前的 120 分制）總分 100、各項 25；Duolingo 135。完全以英語授課、至少三年的本科學位可免
團隊作品作品集內容須為本人原創；放入專業或團隊作品時，必須清楚標示自己的角色與負責部分

以上出自賓大 Weitzman 研究生申請說明頁（How to Apply）、申請政策頁與申請常見問題頁。官網也說明學院不在申請前審閱作品集、不提供回饋。值得注意的是，這位學生當年的雅思 6.5 低於目前官網建議的 IELTS 7；英語門檻請以申請當季官網為準，不要拿個案分數當標準。

為什麼作品集能打動賓大？一套完整的思考主題

他自己的復盤是：作品集有一套完整的思考主題，讓不同尺度、不同功能的四個項目之間關係連貫，主題上又夠豐富——四個項目的選擇與表達都是反覆篩選過的。這和官網「連貫地展現視覺與空間能力」的說法正好呼應。

另一個關鍵是動手能力。他大量使用雷射切割、FDM 與 SLA 等不同類型的 3D 列印來做實體模型，這些都是研究生階段會大量用到的工具。錄取後，賓大一位老師寫信給他，信中特別肯定了作品集「概念豐富、關注社會議題，並展現扎實的技術與表現能力」。

最重要的項目：為戰後的哈爾科夫雕塑認同

作品集裡他最喜歡的項目，是本科畢業後用一個月完成的國際競圖：為烏克蘭哈爾科夫一棟在戰爭中受損的住宅大樓做重建設計（Kharkiv Housing Challenge）。他把這個項目當成真正意義上的畢業設計，也是本科學習成果的集大成。

他問自己的問題是：戰爭結束後，建築除了修好破損的房屋，還能做什麼？他的回答是把建築本身當成一種空間雕塑，用空間與光影紀念在戰爭中受傷的人、消解精神上的創傷：

  • 把交通核改造成三座採光井：利用原有建築的交通盒，把自然光一路引進地下的避難空間，再圍繞這條光的變化安排不同機能。
  • 先做大量案例分析：只有想法是第一步，關鍵是什麼樣的空間與形式語言能「用建築紀念戰爭創傷」；他也在形式上致敬了本科階段影響他很深的幾位建築師。
  • 渲染只挑一個空間：既然概念是紀念性的雕塑，就只渲染一個最具代表性的空間；重點不是模型多細、參數多高，而是把理想的氛圍表達出來。

用實體模型讓作品集「有溫度」

他坦言自己不擅長渲染，一開始也覺得做實體模型很麻煩，於是一味地畫各種圖紙。可是排版時總覺得項目沒有辨識度，像是在機械地證明「我會畫各種圖」。我看過一遍就判斷問題在於缺少合適的模型來表達；他起初很固執，認為模型的效果有限，真正卡住他的其實是不知道怎麼把模型恰當地放進作品集——每個項目要做什麼模型、怎麼做、做完怎麼用，直接決定表現效果。

以這個項目為例：為了呈現原建築的混凝土質感，模型主體用灰色卡紙雷射切割；這是一個適應性再利用（adaptive reuse）項目，為了凸顯新增的部分、也因為那些曲面用傳統方式很難加工，新建部分改用 3D 列印。不同材料與設備的對比，本身就在說明「哪裡是舊的、哪裡是新加的」，也讓模型照片比單純的線圖更有層次。當每個項目的模型都做完並放進作品集後，他突然覺得整本作品集不再冷冰冰，而是「充滿了溫度」。

四個項目怎麼選？善用本科既有的積累

他沒有全部挑學校課設來改，而是選了限制更少、自由度更高的項目：一個學校課設、兩個參加過的競賽，以及一個由研究論文延伸出來的設計。能在兩個月內極限完成整本作品集，靠的就是本科期間項目的積累。

這段時間他也經歷了最困難的階段：申請前最後兩個月，健身時不小心砸斷了手指，模型還沒做、英語成績還沒考出來、還有三個項目等著完成。他的方法是把剩下的時間用到極致，每天從早上十點做到凌晨三點，把作品集一點一點磨出來。

過程中他最大的轉變是：以前受學校課設影響，以為一個項目要面面俱到、事無巨細地畫很多圖才算完成；但作品集裡的項目不需要面面俱到，而是要清楚表達核心想法——要畫什麼圖、為什麼這樣畫、畫好的圖放在哪裡最合適，都要有邏輯。

給研究生申請者的四個建議

  1. 成績：作品集是建築申請最重要的材料，但好成績絕對是加分項，課設要重視；如果成績已成定局，一本優秀的作品集仍有機會逆風翻盤。
  2. 計劃：作品集、整理材料、文書、語言考試，每個環節都需要大量時間，合理的時間規劃能讓你更從容地產出更好的項目。
  3. Thinking by Making：開始做比什麼都重要，很多靈感是在推進項目的過程中出現的，不要想太多，大膽去做。
  4. 善用本科期間的項目：課設或競賽經過適當整理都能放進作品集，比完全重做新項目省時省力，也能把精力留給其他項目與申請材料。

寫在最後

我從 2017 年至今累積 12,000+ 小時設計教學與設計諮詢。這位學生最讓我印象深刻的，是他對細節的執著：圖紙精細、模型精緻，剖面特別有空間感。他在作品集準備過程中常常陷入嚴苛的自我審視，但也正是在一次次的自我批評與反思中成長；當他真正理解 Thinking by Making——用動手引發思考——之後，就開始用模型與實作去探索抽象的想法，找到屬於自己的表達方式。賓大官網說得很清楚：他們看的不是建築設計有多熟練，而是視覺與空間能力，以及對材料與構造的理解。一張好的模型照片，往往比十張面面俱到的圖更能證明這一點。想看更多研究生申請內容，可以讀哥大 GSAPP M.Arch 作品集解析、魯汶大學建築碩士介紹，或直接瀏覽作品牆。
body.en:
An architecture graduate of the University of Nottingham Ningbo China, with a GPA of 3.1 and IELTS 6.5, did not have outstanding studio grades at his undergraduate school. With one portfolio he still gained admission to the University of Pennsylvania (UPenn) Weitzman School of Design Master of Architecture, and also to the KU Leuven Master of Architecture, the UCL MArch Architectural Design, and the M.Arch at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor and at Washington University in St. Louis. The first offer he received came from Pennsylvania State University, together with a scholarship and a teaching assistant (TA) opportunity. The same portfolio also brought him, during the application season, an internship at a practice he wanted to join.

This post sets out his portfolio strategy—four projects on one theme, physical models in place of some of the drawings, and a portfolio shaped from existing undergraduate projects rather than rebuilt from scratch—and checks it against the fall 2027 M.Arch application requirements on the University of Pennsylvania Weitzman website.

Rechecked in October 2026: the deadline, the decision date, the application fee, the portfolio specifications, and the suggested English scores are updated from the University of Pennsylvania Weitzman School of Design website (Fall 2027 application cycle). The student’s scores and admissions that year are personal experience. Before you submit, follow the latest announcement on the official website.

Penn M.Arch fall 2027 application essentials at a glance (official information)

CategoryContent
DeadlineJanuary 6, 2027, 23:59 Eastern Time (M.Arch, MS Arch, and most MSD projects); MLA, MCP, and others are January 13
Decisions12:00 noon Eastern Time on March 4, 2027
Application feeUSD 80, non-refundable, paid by credit card when the application is submitted
M.Arch application materialsOnline application, portfolio, 3 letters of recommendation, a Personal Statement (within 500 words) and a Community Essay, transcripts / credential verification, a resume, and an English score for international students; the M.Arch also lists prerequisites
Portfolio specificationsA single PDF, no more than 30 MB, at most 20 pages (cover and table of contents not counted); websites and printed portfolios are not accepted; after submission it cannot be revised or replaced
What the portfolio is read forThe website states: reviewers look less at proficiency in architectural design, and look at whether an applicant can coherently demonstrate visual and spatial ability, grounded in a basic understanding of materials and construction; drawing, sculpture, photography, graphic / industrial / interior design, and architecture, landscape, and urban design may be included
English scores (suggested minimum)IELTS 7 overall, 7 in each band; TOEFL (the 120-point scale from before January 21, 2026) 100 overall, 25 in each section; Duolingo 135. An undergraduate degree taught entirely in English for at least three years may be exempt
Team workPortfolio content must be the applicant’s own original work; when professional or team work is included, the applicant’s own role and the parts they were responsible for must be clearly indicated

The above is taken from the University of Pennsylvania Weitzman graduate application page (How to Apply), the admissions policies page, and the admissions FAQ page. The website also states that the school does not review portfolios before an application and does not provide feedback. This student’s IELTS 6.5 that year is below the IELTS 7 currently suggested on the website. For the English threshold, follow the official site for the cycle you are applying in. A single applicant’s score is not the standard.

Why did the portfolio move Penn? A complete thematic thread

His own review put it this way: the portfolio had a complete thematic thread, so that the relationships among four projects of different scales and different functions stayed coherent, and the theme was rich enough—the selection and the expression of all four projects had been filtered again and again. That matches the website’s line about coherently demonstrating visual and spatial ability.

Another key was hands-on ability. He used laser cutting extensively, along with different types of 3D printing such as FDM and SLA, to make physical models. These are tools used heavily in graduate study. After he was admitted, a Penn teacher wrote to him and specifically praised the portfolio as “rich in concepts, attentive to social issues, and a demonstration of solid technical and representational ability.”

The most important project: sculpting identity for post-war Kharkiv

The project he likes most in the portfolio is an international competition he finished in one month after his undergraduate degree: a reconstruction design for a residential building in Kharkiv, Ukraine, damaged in the war (Kharkiv Housing Challenge). He treated this project as a graduation project in the true sense, and as the culmination of what he had learned as an undergraduate.

The question he asked himself was: Once the war is over, what can architecture do besides repair damaged houses? His answer was to treat the building itself as a kind of spatial sculpture, and to use space, light, and shadow to commemorate people injured in the war and to ease psychological trauma:

  • Turn the circulation core into three light wells: using the existing building’s circulation core, he brought natural light all the way into the underground shelter, then arranged different functions around the way that light changes.
  • Begin with extensive case studies: an idea is only the first step. What matters is what kind of space and formal language can “commemorate the trauma of war through architecture.” In the form, he also paid homage to several architects who had influenced him deeply during his undergraduate years.
  • Render only one space: because the concept is a commemorative sculpture, he rendered only the single most representative space. The point is not how detailed the model is or how high the parameters run, but whether the atmosphere he wanted comes through.

Physical models that give the portfolio “warmth”

He was frank that he is not good at rendering. At the start he also found physical models a lot of trouble, so he drew sheet after sheet. When he laid the pages out, the projects never had a recognizable character. It felt like mechanically proving that “I can draw every kind of drawing.” After one look, I judged that the problem was the lack of a suitable model to carry the idea. He was stubborn at first and thought a model could only do so much. What actually held him up was not knowing how to place a model properly in the portfolio—what model each project needed, how to make it, and how to use it after it was made. Those choices directly decide how the work comes across.

Take this project as an example. To present the concrete quality of the existing building, the body of the model was laser-cut from grey card. This is an adaptive reuse project. To make the additions stand out, and because those curved surfaces are hard to fabricate in a conventional way, the new parts were 3D-printed. The contrast between different materials and different equipment itself explains “what is old and what has been added,” and it gives the model photographs more depth than line drawings alone. Once the model for every project was finished and placed in the portfolio, he suddenly felt the whole portfolio was no longer cold. It was “full of warmth.”

How were the four projects chosen? Make use of what the undergraduate years had already built up

He did not choose only school studio projects to rework. He chose projects with fewer limits and more freedom: one school studio project, two competitions he had entered, and one design developed from a research paper. Finishing the whole portfolio within two months, at the limit of what the time allowed, depended on the projects he had accumulated as an undergraduate.

This was also the hardest stretch he went through. In the last two months before applying, he accidentally broke a finger while working out. The models were not yet made, the English score was not yet out, and three projects were still waiting to be finished. His way through it was to use the remaining time to the limit, working every day from 10 a.m. to 3 a.m. and polishing the portfolio bit by bit.

The biggest shift in the process was this. School studio projects had led him to think a project was finished only when it covered every angle and set down drawing after drawing in full detail. A project in a portfolio does not need to cover every angle. It needs to express the core idea clearly—which drawings to make, why they are drawn that way, and where a finished drawing belongs all have to follow a logic.

Four suggestions for graduate applicants

  1. Grades: the portfolio is the most important material in an architecture application, but good grades are absolutely a plus, and studio work deserves real attention. If the grades are already settled, an excellent portfolio can still turn the result around against the headwind.
  2. Planning: the portfolio, organizing the materials, the written statements, and the language test each need a great deal of time. A sound schedule lets you produce better projects with more ease.
  3. Thinking by Making: starting the work matters more than anything else. Many ideas show up while a project is moving forward. Overthinking it helps less than beginning. Be bold and make the work.
  4. Make use of undergraduate projects: a studio project or a competition, edited with care, can go into a portfolio. That saves the time and effort of making entirely new projects, and it leaves energy for the other projects and the rest of the application.

In closing

From 2017 to now I have accumulated 12,000+ hours of design teaching and design consulting. What stayed with me most about this student was his insistence on detail: precise drawings, refined models, and sections with a particularly strong sense of space. While preparing the portfolio he often sank into harsh self-scrutiny, and he grew through that repeated self-criticism and reflection. Once he truly understood Thinking by Making—letting the act of making set thinking in motion—he began to use models and making to explore abstract ideas, and found a way of expressing them that was his own. Penn’s website says it plainly: what they look at is visual and spatial ability, and an understanding of materials and construction, rather than how proficient the architectural design is. One good photograph of a model often proves that more than ten drawings that try to cover every angle. For more on graduate applications, you can read a close reading of the Columbia GSAPP M.Arch portfolio, an introduction to the KU Leuven Master of Architecture, or browse the project board directly.

q.zh-Hant: 賓大 M.Arch 2027 秋季入學什麼時候截止？什麼時候放榜？
q.en: When is the Penn M.Arch deadline for fall 2027 entry, and when are decisions released?

a.zh-Hant: 依賓大 Weitzman 設計學院官網，M.Arch 截止日為 2027 年 1 月 6 日美東時間 23:59，放榜為 2027 年 3 月 4 日美東時間中午 12 點；申請費 80 美元、不退費。
a.en: According to the University of Pennsylvania Weitzman School of Design website, the M.Arch deadline is January 6, 2027 at 23:59 Eastern Time, and decisions are released at 12:00 noon Eastern Time on March 4, 2027. The application fee is USD 80 and is non-refundable.

q.zh-Hant: 賓大 M.Arch 作品集有什麼規格？
q.en: What are the specifications for the Penn M.Arch portfolio?

a.zh-Hant: 單一 PDF、不超過 30 MB、最多 20 頁，封面與目錄不計入頁數；不接受網站或紙本作品集，送出申請後不能再修改或替換。放入團隊或專業作品時，必須清楚標示自己的角色與負責部分。
a.en: A single PDF, no more than 30 MB, and at most 20 pages. The cover and table of contents do not count toward the page total. Websites and printed portfolios are not accepted, and the file cannot be revised or replaced after the application is submitted. When team or professional work is included, the applicant’s own role and the parts they were responsible for must be clearly indicated.

q.zh-Hant: 賓大審查建築作品集看重什麼？
q.en: What does Penn look for when it reviews an architecture portfolio?

a.zh-Hant: 官網說明，審查教師比較不看建築設計的熟練度，而是看能否連貫地展現視覺與空間能力，並建立在對材料與構造的基本理解之上；作品可以包含繪畫、雕塑、攝影、各類設計與建築、景觀、城市設計。
a.en: The website explains that reviewers look less at proficiency in architectural design and more at whether an applicant can coherently demonstrate visual and spatial ability, grounded in a basic understanding of materials and construction. Work may include drawing, sculpture, photography, various kinds of design, and architecture, landscape, and urban design.

q.zh-Hant: 賓大 M.Arch 的英語成績要求是多少？
q.en: What English-language scores does the Penn M.Arch ask for?

a.zh-Hant: 官網列出的建議最低分數為 IELTS 總分 7、各項 7；TOEFL（2026 年 1 月 21 日前的 120 分制）總分 100、各項 25；Duolingo 135。若本科完全以英語授課且至少三年，可免交英語成績。
a.en: The suggested minimum scores listed on the website are IELTS 7 overall with 7 in each band; TOEFL (the 120-point scale from before January 21, 2026) 100 overall with 25 in each section; and Duolingo 135. If an undergraduate degree was taught entirely in English for at least three years, the English score may be waived.

q.zh-Hant: 不擅長渲染，作品集怎麼做出說服力？
q.en: If you are not good at rendering, how can a portfolio still be convincing?

a.zh-Hant: 可以用實體模型取代一部分圖面。這個案例用灰色卡紙雷射切割呈現原有混凝土建築、用 3D 列印做新增部分，材料對比本身就說明了改造邏輯；渲染只挑一個最有代表性的空間，重點是表達氛圍而不是參數。
a.en: Some of the drawings can be replaced with physical models. In this case, grey card was laser-cut to represent the existing concrete building, and 3D printing was used for the new parts. The contrast in materials itself explains the logic of the alteration. The rendering picks only one of the most representative spaces, and the point is to express atmosphere rather than parameters.
