posts.abstract_en: A case study of a graduate of the University of Nottingham Ningbo China (GPA 3.1, IELTS 6.5) admitted to the Master of Architecture at the University of Pennsylvania Weitzman School of Design, with M.Arch offers from KU Leuven, UCL (MArch Architectural Design), the University of Michigan and WashU in St. Louis, plus a first offer with scholarship from Penn State. Facts were cross-checked against Weitzman's How to Apply, admissions policies and FAQ pages in October 2026: for Fall 2027 the M.Arch deadline is January 6, 2027 (11:59 pm Eastern), decisions are released March 4, 2027, the fee is US$80; the portfolio is one PDF of at most 30 MB and 20 pages (cover and contents excluded), no websites or paper; faculty look less for architectural design competence than for a coherent demonstration of visual and spatial abilities grounded in material and construction; suggested minimum English scores are IELTS 7 (7 per band), TOEFL 100 (25 per section, old scale) or Duolingo 135. The post explains a four-project portfolio unified by one theme, built from existing undergraduate work (one studio project, two competitions, one research-led design), and a Kharkiv post-war housing competition entry whose three light wells bring daylight to an underground shelter and memorial hall, expressed through laser-cut greyboard and 3D-printed section models instead of exhaustive drawings.

title.zh-Hant: ED 被延到 RD 仍錄取康乃爾建築本科：活動少，靠八個實體項目的作品集翻盤（2026 年 10 月官方查核）
title.en: Deferred from ED, admitted RD to Cornell B.Arch: an eight-project physical-model portfolio that made up for few activities (checked October 2026)

summary.zh-Hant: 康乃爾 ED 被延到 RD、課外活動偏少，他靠八個實體項目的作品集，最後錄取康乃爾 B.Arch，以及南加大、伊利諾香檳、東北大學與伊利諾理工。整理他等待放榜的心態、選校邏輯與垂直綠化塔「翠綠立面」的做法，並對照康乃爾 AAP 官網：ED 11 月 1 日、RD 1 月 2 日截止，作品集 15–20 張、每項目最多 2 張，加 3 分鐘影片面試。
summary.en: Deferred from Cornell ED to RD, and with few extracurricular activities, he relied on a portfolio of eight physical projects and was admitted to the Cornell B.Arch, as well as USC, UIUC, Northeastern, and Illinois Tech (IIT). This post sets out how he waited for decisions, how he chose schools, and how he made the vertical greening tower “Verdant Facade,” and checks that against the Cornell AAP website: an ED deadline of November 1, an RD deadline of January 2, a portfolio of 15–20 images with at most 2 per project, and a 3-minute video interview.

tldr.zh-Hant: 康乃爾 AAP 五年制建築學士（B.Arch.）申請者須經 SlideRoom 提交作品集與影片面試：Early Decision 截止 11 月 1 日、Regular Decision 截止 1 月 2 日，逾期不收；作品集 15–20 張、每個項目最多 2 張，強調手繪與多元媒材；影片須連續拍攝、不剪輯、3 分鐘以內，回答三題；禁止外包與 AI 生成圖像，團隊作品須標註角色。本文案例 ED 被延到 RD、活動經歷少，以八個實體項目（含蒙德里安風格垂直綠化塔）的作品集錄取康乃爾 B.Arch 與南加大等校。
tldr.en: Applicants to the five-year Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch.) at Cornell AAP must submit a portfolio and a video interview through SlideRoom. The Early Decision deadline is November 1 and the Regular Decision deadline is January 2, and late submissions are not accepted. The portfolio is 15–20 images, with at most 2 images per project, and it emphasizes hand drawing and a range of media. The video must be filmed continuously, left unedited, and kept within 3 minutes, answering three questions. Outsourcing and AI-generated images are prohibited, and team work must credit the applicant’s role. In this case, an applicant deferred from ED to RD, with few activities, was admitted to the Cornell B.Arch and to USC and other schools with a portfolio of eight physical projects, including a Mondrian-style vertical greening tower.

body.zh-Hant:
一位美高 AP 體系的學生，從高二春天開始準備作品集、到申請前的暑假完成，最後拿到康乃爾大學建築學士（Bachelor of Architecture，B.Arch）錄取，同一季也錄取南加州大學（USC）、伊利諾大學厄巴納－香檳分校（UIUC）、東北大學與伊利諾理工學院（IIT）。特別的是，他在康乃爾的 Early Decision（ED）先被延到 Regular Decision（RD），課外活動也偏少——最後靠的是一本由八個實體項目構成的作品集。

這篇整理他從 ED 被延後到 RD 錄取的心態、選校邏輯與作品集做法，並對照康乃爾 AAP 建築學院官網目前公布的 B.Arch 作品集規定。

2026 年 10 月重新查核：作品集截止日、張數、影片面試與上傳規定，均依康乃爾 AAP 建築本科招生頁更新；學生的經歷屬個人經驗，送件前請再以官網最新公告為準。

康乃爾 B.Arch 作品集規定一覽（官方資料）

項目內容
學制五年制建築學士（B.Arch.），屬專業學位課程
必交材料除康乃爾大學一般申請要求外，B.Arch 申請者必須提交作品集與影片面試；任何一項作品集要求未達成，申請不予審查
作品集截止日Early Decision 新生：11 月 1 日；Regular Decision 新生：1 月 2 日；逾期不收。Fall 2027 不接受外校轉學申請
上傳方式只接受經 Cornell AAP SlideRoom 上傳，不接受其他方式
張數15–20 張，每個項目最多 2 張
內容建議手繪（草圖與完整作品）與多元媒材：繪畫、尺規圖、設計作品、雕塑、影片、攝影、木工及其他工藝
影片面試連續拍攝、總長不超過 3 分鐘、不可剪輯；回答三題：如何表達創造力？描述一件創作項目的設計過程與影響？為什麼想讀建築？
圖說與標註圖片清楚、除非是作品一部分否則不放文字；說明建議 50 字（英文）以內，交代意圖、過程與成果；註明尺寸、媒材，以及在課堂、作品集工作坊或獨立完成
原創與團隊不可把作品集外包給第三方，包含 AI 生成圖像；團隊作品須標註合作者並說明自己的角色

以上出自康乃爾 AAP 建築本科招生頁（Undergraduate Admissions: Architecture）。官網也列出學院希望看到的特質，例如「Rigorous Makers」——主動發展並精進技術與創作能力的人，以及「Broad Thinkers」——興趣橫跨科學與人文的人；這兩點正好對應這位學生的作品集與背景。

ED 被延到 RD：與其慌張，不如順其自然地把後路準備好

他用 ED 申請康乃爾，結果被延到 RD 重新審。他坦言不可能毫無反應，但選擇不歇斯底里地慌張：等待期間有焦慮，可是在拿到保底學校的錄取之後，他其實已經做好去那裡讀的心理準備。放榜前一天，USC 先錄取了他；康乃爾放榜那天，他刻意等到晚上才打開結果——最後是錄取。

從這段經驗可以整理出三個實際做法：

  • 被延後不等於被拒：ED 被延到 RD 的申請會在常規輪重新審查，這段時間應該把 RD 學校的作品集與文書照常完成，而不是停在原地等。
  • 先把保底學校確定下來：手上有一份可以接受的錄取，等待夢校結果時心態會穩很多。
  • 作品集是延後期間最可控的變數：康乃爾 RD 作品集截止日是 1 月 2 日，各校的作品集張數與格式不同，需要分別調整。

選校：沒有「夢校」，但要選綜合實力強的環境

他說自己其實沒有夢校的概念：無論學校遠近好壞，沒有去讀之前，永遠不知道在讀時、畢業後會發生什麼；當然，去更好的學校更好，所以在老師建議下，把目標定在美國頂尖的建築學院——康乃爾。吸引他的是康乃爾的綜合實力：工程、科學、農業等學科單獨拿出來都很強，他覺得在這樣的環境裡學什麼都會有好的氛圍與動力。

他也給了一個很務實的建議：如果有排名稍低、但自己真正喜歡、而且有相關課外活動支撐的專業方向，可以大膽申請，不必把所有籌碼壓在同一個方向上——萬一 ED 沒錄，至少在別的學校還有機會讀自己喜歡的專業。

八個實體項目：最喜歡的是垂直綠化塔「翠綠立面」

整本作品集共完成八個實體項目，類型與方向各不相同，每個項目都有自己的出發點和表達方式。他最喜歡的是垂直綠化項目「翠綠立面」（Verdant Facade），視覺語言借用了荷蘭藝術家蒙德里安的直線與矩形風格：

  • 選風格的理由很直接：垂直線條與這種風格很酷、沒有太多複雜聯想，就是直覺上的契合。
  • 先做案例研究：調研了西安、馬來西亞、廣州等城市的垂直綠化案例，看大量參考圖之後才開始動手。
  • 用材料自由組合：以不同粗細、長短的木條組成線條與網格等矩形結構，再點綴不同色系的植物。
  • 卡住時先動手：他一度糾結形態應該像一棵樹，還是更像一棟樓；最後的結論是不讓自己被某個想法困住，先動手做了再說，反而找到更自然的方向。

這個做法和康乃爾官網的要求很一致：官網希望看到多元媒材與「Rigorous Makers」，也要求每張圖附上意圖、過程與成果的簡短說明。像「翠綠立面」這樣的實體項目，正好能在兩張以內同時交代完成品與製作過程。

同一本作品集的其他項目：崖邊海灘屋與「燈塔守護人的家」

另一個實體項目「崖邊海灘屋」從旅途中看過的建築記憶出發，想像一棟位於海灘上方山坡的住宅，問的是：一個家如何同時讓人感到受庇護、又向景色敞開？地形用層疊板材、沙與彩繪海面堆出來，圓形房間由狹長走道與共用樓梯串連。

還有一個項目以小說 The Light Keeper 為起點。很多人第一反應會以為這是替燈塔守護人這個職業設計的住宅，其實不是——他設計的是小說裡一位有特殊經歷的具體人物的家。整個項目的重點是讓這個「家」的故事完整、帶有特定氛圍；他在情感轉譯上處理得非常細膩，這也和他本身的性格有關。

活動經歷少，怎麼補？把精力放在作品集深度

他申請時有一個明顯弱勢：幾乎沒有什麼活動經歷。正因為清楚這一點，他把更多精力放在作品集的深度打磨上，也願意為新事物下功夫。他也坦白，暑假有一段時間很枯燥、幾乎沒有動力、靈感也快枯竭，但想到「這個暑假的付出程度和最終結果成正比」，還是逼自己把事情做完。

做作品集之前，他對建築的印象多半停留在城市裡的高樓大廈；做完之後才真正意識到，建築牽涉很多其他領域的知識，核心是如何把這些知識應用在不同功能、不同環境的建築裡。

從計算機轉向建築：每一步都沒有白走

回頭看，他一開始其實比較傾向深入學習計算機。學了一段時間後，他經歷過一段迷惘：程式訓練初期多半停留在概念、邏輯和系統層面，而建築與空間設計給了他另一種把抽象概念具體化的方式。後來他把過去的計算機基礎，和空間設計裡更具物理性、更落地的表達結合起來，也參加了大學夏校，持續用作品展現自己的思考。

以我 12,000+ 小時設計教學與設計諮詢的經驗來看，對十六、七歲的高中生而言，太早用一個專業名稱定義自己並不是最重要的。真正重要的，是在持續探索中找到自己想表達的價值；作品集也不只是幾件作品的集合，而是一個幫助學生在迷惘中慢慢看見自己、把內在感受轉化成外在表達的過程。這位學生心思細膩、感受力強，能捕捉細微的情緒、空間關係和生活經驗，再把它們轉化成圖像、模型和空間語言——這正是康乃爾錄取背後最有說服力的部分。

給申請季的建議

  • 保持一個不會讓自己後悔的心態：全力以赴之後，無論結果好壞都不會有遺憾。
  • 弱項要用強項補：活動少，就把作品集做深；實體模型、製作過程、案例研究都能證明投入程度。
  • 照官網規格重新剪裁作品集：康乃爾要求 15–20 張、每個項目最多 2 張、附 3 分鐘以內不剪輯的影片面試，且禁止外包與 AI 生成圖像；八個項目放進 20 張以內，就必須每個項目只挑最有代表性的畫面。
  • 不要把所有籌碼壓在同一方向：有真正喜歡、又有活動支撐的方向，可以一起申請。
body.en:
A student in a U.S. high school AP curriculum began preparing his portfolio in the spring of 11th grade and finished it the summer before he applied. He was admitted to the Cornell University Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch), and in the same cycle to the University of Southern California (USC), the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC), Northeastern University, and Illinois Tech (IIT). What is particular here is that his Cornell Early Decision (ED) was first deferred to Regular Decision (RD), and his extracurricular activities were also few. What carried the application in the end was a portfolio built from eight physical projects.

This post sets out his mindset from the ED deferral to the RD admission, how he chose schools, and how he made the portfolio, and it checks that against the B.Arch portfolio requirements currently published on the Cornell AAP architecture website.

Rechecked in October 2026: the portfolio deadlines, the number of images, the video interview, and the upload rules are updated from the Cornell AAP undergraduate architecture admissions page. The student’s experience is personal. Before you submit, follow the latest announcement on the official website.

Cornell B.Arch portfolio requirements at a glance (official information)

CategoryContent
Degree structureA five-year Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch.), a professional degree
Required materialsBeyond Cornell University’s general application requirements, B.Arch applicants must submit a portfolio and a video interview. If any portfolio requirement is left unmet, the application is not reviewed
Portfolio deadlinesEarly Decision first-year applicants: November 1; Regular Decision first-year applicants: January 2. Late submissions are not accepted. Fall 2027 does not accept transfer applications from other institutions
Upload methodAccepted only by upload through Cornell AAP SlideRoom. No other method is accepted
Number of images15–20 images, at most 2 per project
Suggested contentHand drawing (sketches and finished works) and a range of media: painting, drafted drawings, design work, sculpture, video, photography, woodworking, and other crafts
Video interviewFilmed in one continuous take, no more than 3 minutes in total, and left unedited. Answer three questions: How do you express creativity? Describe the design process and the impact of one creative project? Why do you want to study architecture?
Captions and labelsImages should be clear, and text stays off the image unless it is part of the work. A note of 50 words (in English) or fewer is suggested, covering intention, process, and outcome. State the dimensions, the medium, and whether the work was completed in class, in a portfolio workshop, or independently
Original work and teamsOutsourcing the portfolio to a third party is prohibited, and that includes AI-generated images. Team work must name the collaborators and explain one’s own role

The above comes from the Cornell AAP undergraduate architecture admissions page (Undergraduate Admissions: Architecture). The website also lists qualities the college hopes to see, for example “Rigorous Makers”—people who actively develop and refine technical and creative ability—and “Broad Thinkers”—people whose interests span the sciences and the humanities. Those two points line up with this student’s portfolio and background.

Deferred from ED to RD: let the backup come together, and leave the panic aside

He applied to Cornell through ED and was deferred to RD for a second review. He admitted that feeling nothing was impossible, and he chose to keep clear of a hysterical panic. The wait brought anxiety, and after a safety-school offer arrived he was in fact already prepared to go and study there. The day before decisions, USC admitted him first. On the day Cornell released its decisions, he deliberately waited until evening to open the result. It was an offer.

Three practical steps come out of that experience:

  • A deferral is not a rejection: an application deferred from ED to RD is reviewed again in the regular round. During that time, finish the portfolios and essays for the RD schools as usual, rather than stopping in place to wait.
  • Secure a safety school first: with one offer you can accept already in hand, waiting on a dream-school result feels much steadier.
  • The portfolio is the most controllable variable during a deferral: Cornell’s RD portfolio deadline is January 2. Image counts and formats differ by school, so each one needs its own adjustment.

Choosing schools: there is no “dream school,” and the aim is an environment strong across the board

He said he did not really hold the idea of a dream school. Far or near, stronger or less so, until you go and study there, you never know what will happen while you are enrolled or after you graduate. A stronger school is the better place to be, so on a teacher’s advice he set his aim on a leading architecture college in the United States—Cornell. What attracted him was Cornell’s overall strength: engineering, the sciences, agriculture, and other fields are each strong on their own. He felt that studying anything in that environment would come with a good atmosphere and real drive.

He also offered a very practical suggestion. Where a direction is ranked a little lower, genuinely liked, and backed by related extracurricular activities, it is worth applying with confidence. There is room to apply in more than one direction. If ED ends without an offer, you still have a chance, at another school, to study a subject you like.

Eight physical projects: the favorite is the vertical greening tower “Verdant Facade”

The portfolio completed eight physical projects in all. The types and directions differ, and each project has its own starting point and its own way of speaking. The one he likes most is the vertical greening project “Verdant Facade.” Its visual language borrows the straight lines and rectangles of the Dutch artist Mondrian:

  • The reason for the style was straightforward: vertical lines and this style look cool, and they carry few complicated associations. The fit was intuitive.
  • Case studies came first: he researched vertical greening cases in Xi'an, Malaysia, Guangzhou, and other cities, and he started making only after looking through a large number of reference images.
  • Materials were combined freely: wooden sticks of different thicknesses and lengths form lines, grids, and other rectangular structures, and plants from different color ranges are set in as accents.
  • When he was stuck, he made something first: for a while he turned over whether the form should be more like a tree or more like a building. He decided to keep a single idea from trapping him, started making, and found a more natural direction that way.

This way of working lines up with what Cornell’s website asks for. The site wants to see a range of media and “Rigorous Makers,” and it asks each image to carry a short note on intention, process, and outcome. A physical project such as “Verdant Facade” can, within two images, show both the finished piece and how it was made.

Other projects in the same portfolio: Cliffside Beach House and “the lighthouse keeper’s home”

Another physical project, “Cliffside Beach House,” starts from buildings he remembered seeing on a trip. It imagines a house on a hillside above a beach, and it asks: how can a home make a person feel sheltered and, at the same time, open to the view? The terrain is built up from layered sheet material, sand, and a painted sea. The round rooms are linked by long, narrow passages and a shared stair.

Another project begins with the novel The Light Keeper. Many people’s first reaction is to take this as a house designed for the occupation of lighthouse keeper. What he designed is a home for one specific character in the novel, a person with a particular experience. The point of the whole project is to make the story of this “home” complete and to give it a specific atmosphere. He handled the translation of feeling with great fineness, and that is also tied to his own temperament.

Few activities: how do you make up for that? Put the effort into the depth of the portfolio

He had one clear weakness at the time of application: almost no activities on his record. Because he knew that, he put more of his effort into polishing the portfolio in depth, and he was willing to work hard at things that were new to him. He was also frank that part of the summer was dull, that he had almost no drive, and that his ideas were nearly used up. The thought that “the effort this summer takes and the final result stand in proportion” still pushed him to finish.

Before the portfolio, his picture of architecture mostly stopped at the towers of a city. After he finished, he saw that architecture draws on knowledge from many other fields, and that the core is how to apply that knowledge to buildings of different functions and in different settings.

From computing toward architecture: every step counted

Looking back, he had at first leaned toward going further into computing. After studying it for a while, he went through a period of being lost. Early training in programming mostly stays at the level of concepts, logic, and systems, while architecture and spatial design gave him another way of making abstract concepts concrete. Later he joined that foundation in computing to the more physical, more down-to-earth expression of spatial design. He also took part in a university summer school, and he kept using projects to show how he thinks.

From my 12,000+ hours of design teaching and design consulting, for high-school students of 16 or 17, defining yourself too early by the name of one major is not what matters most. What matters is finding, through continued exploration, the value you want to express. A portfolio is more than a collection of several works. It is a process that helps a student, while lost, slowly see themselves and turn an inner feeling into an outward expression. This student notices fine detail and feels things strongly. He can catch slight emotions, spatial relationships, and lived experience, then turn them into images, models, and a spatial language. That is the most persuasive part behind the Cornell offer.

Suggestions for application season

  • Keep a state of mind you will be glad you kept: after you have given it everything, a strong result and a hard result alike leave no regret behind.
  • Let a strength carry a weak point: where activities are few, make the portfolio deep. Physical models, the process of making, and case studies can all show the degree of commitment.
  • Cut the portfolio again to the specifications on the website: Cornell asks for 15–20 images, at most 2 per project, plus an unedited video interview of no more than 3 minutes, and it prohibits outsourcing and AI-generated images. Fitting eight projects into 20 images or fewer means each project shows only its most representative views.
  • Let the applications cover more than one direction: a direction you truly like, and that activities support, can go in alongside the others.

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾建築本科（B.Arch）作品集什麼時候截止？
q.en: When is the portfolio deadline for Cornell’s undergraduate architecture degree (B.Arch)?

a.zh-Hant: 依康乃爾 AAP 官網，Early Decision 新生作品集截止日為 11 月 1 日，Regular Decision 新生為 1 月 2 日，只接受經 Cornell AAP SlideRoom 上傳，逾期不收；Fall 2027 不接受外校轉學申請。
a.en: According to the Cornell AAP website, the Early Decision first-year portfolio deadline is November 1, and the Regular Decision first-year deadline is January 2. Submissions are accepted only through Cornell AAP SlideRoom, and late work is not accepted. Fall 2027 does not accept transfer applications from other institutions.

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾 B.Arch 作品集要放幾張？有什麼規定？
q.en: How many images does a Cornell B.Arch portfolio include, and what are the rules?

a.zh-Hant: 15–20 張，每個項目最多 2 張；官網建議展示手繪（草圖與完整作品）與多元媒材，圖片除非是作品一部分否則不放文字，說明約 50 字（英文）以內，並註明尺寸、媒材與完成情境。不可外包或使用 AI 生成圖像，團隊作品須標註合作者與個人角色。
a.en: 15–20 images, with at most 2 images per project. The website suggests showing hand drawing (sketches and finished works) and a range of media. Text stays off an image unless it is part of the work. The note should be within about 50 words (in English), and should state the dimensions, the medium, and the context in which the work was completed. The portfolio may not be outsourced, and AI-generated images may not be used. Team work must credit the collaborators and the applicant’s own role.

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾 B.Arch 的影片面試要回答什麼？
q.en: What does the Cornell B.Arch video interview ask?

a.zh-Hant: 須上傳一段連續拍攝、不剪輯、總長不超過 3 分鐘的影片，回答三題：如何表達創造力？描述一件藝術、設計、建築或社會行動項目的設計過程與影響？為什麼想讀建築？
a.en: You must upload one video filmed continuously, left unedited, and no longer than 3 minutes in total, answering three questions: How do you express creativity? Describe the design process and the impact of one art, design, architecture, or social-action project? Why do you want to study architecture?

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾 ED 被延到 RD 還有機會嗎？
q.en: If Cornell defers an ED application to RD, is there still a chance?

a.zh-Hant: 有。本文案例就是 ED 被延到 RD 後在常規輪錄取。被延後期間建議照常完成其他學校的申請、先確定一份可接受的錄取，並把作品集照各校規格調整好，而不是停下來等待。
a.en: Yes. The case in this post was admitted in the regular round after being deferred from ED to RD. While deferred, finish applications to the other schools as usual, secure one acceptable offer first, and adjust the portfolio to each school’s specifications, rather than stopping to wait.

q.zh-Hant: 課外活動很少，申請建築本科怎麼補強？
q.en: With very few extracurricular activities, how can an undergraduate architecture application be strengthened?

a.zh-Hant: 把精力放在作品集深度。這位學生活動經歷少，便以八個實體項目呈現研究、動手製作與情感轉譯的能力；康乃爾官網也明確希望看到多元媒材與主動精進技術的「Rigorous Makers」。
a.en: Put the effort into the depth of the portfolio. This student had few activities, so he used eight physical projects to show research, hands-on making, and the ability to translate feeling. Cornell’s website also explicitly hopes to see a range of media and “Rigorous Makers” who actively refine their technique.

posts.abstract_en: A case study of an American-curriculum (AP) high school student who was deferred from Early Decision to Regular Decision at Cornell and then admitted to the five-year Bachelor of Architecture at the College of Architecture, Art, and Planning (AAP), with further offers from USC, UIUC, Northeastern and IIT, despite having few extracurricular activities. Facts were checked against the Cornell AAP undergraduate architecture admissions page in October 2026: B.Arch applicants must submit a portfolio and a video interview through Cornell AAP SlideRoom by November 1 (Early Decision) or January 2 (Regular Decision); Fall 2027 is closed to external transfers; the portfolio has 15-20 slides with no more than two per project, emphasising freehand drawing and a range of media; the unedited video is at most three minutes and answers three prompts; outsourcing and AI-generated images are not allowed and group work must credit collaborators. The post covers the student's mindset while deferred, his school-selection logic, and an eight-project physical-model portfolio including a Mondrian-inspired vertical-greening stick tower (Verdant Facade), a cliffside beach house site model and a home for a character from the novel The Light Keeper.

title.zh-Hant: 4 份作品集都錄取康乃爾建築本科：他們把生活經驗「轉譯」成空間（2026 年 10 月官方查核）
title.en: Four portfolios, four Cornell B.Arch offers: how admitted students translated everyday experience into space (checked October 2026)

summary.zh-Hant: 四份風格完全不同的作品集都錄取康乃爾 B.Arch：繪畫與陶瓷、計算設計、遊戲敘事、生態行動。拆解它們的共同點——從個人經驗出發、保留過程證據、多媒材、價值方向具體，並對照康乃爾 AAP 官網：作品集 15–20 張、每項目最多 2 張，ED 11 月 1 日、RD 1 月 2 日截止，加 3 分鐘影片面試。
summary.en: Four portfolios in completely different styles were admitted to the Cornell B.Arch: painting and ceramics, computational design, game narrative, and ecological action. They share a start in personal experience, process kept as evidence, multiple media, and a concrete direction of values, set against the Cornell AAP site: 15–20 images, at most 2 per project, Early Decision due November 1, Regular Decision due January 2, and a 3-minute video interview.

tldr.zh-Hant: 康乃爾建築本科（五年制 B.Arch.，NAAB 認證、STEM）不要求作品集「很像建築」，官網要的是展現技能與個人觀點的自由手繪與多元媒材：15–20 張、每個項目最多 2 張，經 SlideRoom 上傳，ED 11 月 1 日、RD 1 月 2 日截止，另交 3 分鐘內不剪輯的影片面試，禁止外包與 AI 生成圖像。四份錄取作品集的共同點是「轉譯」：把身體、運動、遊戲、海洋與家鄉記憶等個人經驗，透過草圖、模型、實驗與數位工具變成空間系統。
tldr.en: Cornell undergraduate architecture (a five-year B.Arch., NAAB-accredited and listed as a STEM project) does not require a portfolio that "looks like architecture." The site asks for freehand drawing and a range of media that show skill and a personal point of view: 15–20 images, at most 2 per project, uploaded through SlideRoom, with Early Decision due November 1 and Regular Decision due January 2, plus an unedited video interview of no more than 3 minutes. Outsourcing and AI-generated images are prohibited. What the four admitted portfolios share is "translation": personal experience — the body, movement, games, the ocean, and hometown memory — turned, through sketches, models, experiments, and digital tools, into spatial systems.

body.zh-Hant:
今年有四份風格完全不同的作品集，都拿到了康乃爾大學建築學士（Bachelor of Architecture，B.Arch）錄取。很多家長和學生一聽到「康乃爾建築本科」，第一反應是：作品集是不是必須很像建築專業？是不是要畫很多建築圖、要有很厲害的渲染？這四份作品集給出的答案恰恰相反。

它們當然有模型、圖紙、草圖、材料實驗和數位建模，但真正讓它們成立的，不是「看起來像建築作品集」，而是每個學生都把自己的生活經驗、觀察方式、興趣系統和價值判斷，轉譯成了空間——他們不是在證明自己已經是建築師，而是在證明自己已經具備成為建築師的思維方式。

2026 年 10 月重新查核：學制、作品集規定、截止日與影片面試題目，均依康乃爾 AAP 官網更新；四位學生的作品屬個人案例，送件前請再以官網最新公告為準。

康乃爾 B.Arch 作品集官方要求是什麼？

項目官方內容
學制五年制專業學位（B.Arch.），經 NAAB 認證，並列為 STEM 項目
課程重點強調設計，同時涵蓋理論、歷史、技術、表現與結構；學生透過模型與圖紙溝通想法，在類比與數位表現之間流動；前三年為核心課程，最後四個學期鼓勵跨學科
必交材料作品集＋影片面試，只接受經 Cornell AAP SlideRoom 上傳
截止日Early Decision 新生 11 月 1 日；Regular Decision 新生 1 月 2 日；逾期不收。Fall 2027 不接受外校轉學申請
張數15–20 張，每個項目最多 2 張
內容展現申請者作為未來建築學生的技能與觀點：自由手繪（草圖與完整作品），以及繪畫、尺規構成圖、設計作品、雕塑、影片、攝影、木工與其他工藝
影片面試連續拍攝、不剪輯、總長不超過 3 分鐘，回答三題：你如何表達創造力？描述一件藝術、設計、建築或社會行動項目的設計過程與影響；為什麼想讀建築？
原創要求不可外包給第三方，包含 AI 生成圖像；團隊作品須標註合作者與自己的角色

以上出自康乃爾 AAP 建築本科招生頁與康乃爾 AAP 建築系本科項目頁。招生頁也列出學院重視的特質，例如 Expressive Designers、Creative Thinkers、Spatial Changemakers、Cultural Innovators、Rigorous Makers、Empathic Individuals、Broad Thinkers——不是只看「建築成品」，而是看一個學生如何觀察、轉譯、製作與表達。

四份作品集的共同答案是什麼？先建立自己的世界觀

這四份作品集風格完全不同，卻有一個共同特徵：每個項目背後都有一個明確的「為什麼」。不是為了做模型而做模型，也不是為了展示軟體而展示軟體，而是從個人經驗、社會議題、材料觀察或文化記憶出發，逐步變成空間系統。

四位學生的強項也不同，說明康乃爾並不只接受某一種「標準建築生」：

  • 繪畫與陶瓷型：以油畫、針管筆、麥克筆、鉛筆素描與陶瓷，處理身體、審美壓力與結構觀察。
  • 計算設計型：從高爾夫球飛行軌跡、寵物運動、電影《The Substance》裡的身體焦慮、真菌生長等經驗出發，轉成模型系統與參數化結構。
  • 遊戲敘事型：從越獄影集、Unity 逃脫遊戲、垂直綠化、遊戲裡的城堡與神殿出發，抽取空間組織、敘事路徑與運動體驗。
  • 生態行動型：圍繞廚餘、海洋污染、客家建築、珊瑚生態與社區教育，形成一條長期觀察與行動的主線。

為什麼不要「空降概念」？題目要和自己有關

很多學生做建築作品集時，最常見的問題是題目很大、但和自己沒有關係：一上來就做「未來城市」「生態社區」「永續建築」，概念聽起來正確，作品裡卻看不到個人觀察，也看不到為什麼這個學生非做不可。

這四份作品集避開了這個坑，項目大多來自真實經歷：有人從身體與美的焦慮出發，有人從高爾夫揮桿的空間弧線出發，有人從帆船經驗與海洋污染出發，有人從遊戲空間和動漫建築出發，也有人從家族鄉村記憶和客家建築出發。

繪畫與陶瓷型的學生，最值得放進作品集的反而不是前半部分的模型，而是後段的繪畫、陶瓷與素描：她把不現實的美貌標準轉化為紅、藍兩組身體形象——紅色指向外部評價帶來的壓迫，藍色指向自我懷疑與飲食焦慮。建築立面素描說明她有耐心、比例感與構造觀察能力；骨骼素描則說明她能面對複雜結構細緻描繪。這正好對應官網列出的自由手繪、繪畫與雕塑媒材。

生態行動型學生的個人來源更強：廚餘處理系統來自家裡倒廚餘的日常觀察，海洋污染項目來自他作為帆船運動者和教練的親身經驗，客家建築研究來自父輩家鄉與家族記憶。招生官看到的不是一個可以被替換的「環保主題」，而是一個學生長期觀察某個問題、願意為它投入行動的證據。

作品集要怎麼展現「過程證據」？

康乃爾官網要求作品集包含手繪、草圖、發展中的作品與多種媒材，背後的邏輯很明確：建築教育不只看最終效果，而是看學生如何推導。四份作品集都保留了大量過程資訊：

  • 計算設計型學生的大學夏校項目，有平面、剖面、軸測、模型細節與最終模型；
  • 遊戲敘事型學生的項目，經常展示靈感來源、手繪、模型迭代與數位延伸；
  • 生態行動型學生的項目，不只有模型，還有現場照片、實驗對比、構造方法和社區實施過程；
  • 繪畫與陶瓷型學生後段的繪畫、陶瓷與素描，呈現從身體情緒、畫面構圖到結構觀察的視覺訓練過程。

放進康乃爾的 15–20 張裡，「每個項目最多 2 張」的限制意味著：一張交代完成品，另一張就要精選最能說明推導過程的畫面，而不是把所有草圖都塞進去。

多媒材能力怎麼證明？參數化要服務於觀察

官網特別列出自由手繪、繪畫、構成圖、設計、雕塑、攝影、木工與其他工藝，意思是康乃爾想看到的是視覺與空間素養的廣度，而不是某一個軟體的熟練度。四份作品集幾乎都包含實體模型、手繪、材料實驗、數位建模或計算設計：

  • 計算設計型學生的「無限擴張」，從真菌生長觀察進入 Grasshopper 與 Kangaroo 物理模擬；
  • 遊戲敘事型學生把實體模型延伸到 Unity 遊戲空間；
  • 生態行動型學生用 Rhino、3D 列印、陶瓷與真實生態材料研究人工珊瑚礁；
  • 繪畫與陶瓷型學生以油畫、針管筆、麥克筆、鉛筆素描與陶瓷證明二維造型與結構觀察能力。

重點不是「會不會參數化」，而是參數化有沒有服務於一個觀察問題。「無限擴張」的計算設計不是孤立炫技，而是從生物生長形態中擷取曲線、生成結構、模擬膜狀屋頂，再優化為多孔結構——技術是思考的結果，而不是作品集的噱頭。

遊戲敘事型學生的優勢在跨媒介想像力：他沒有把遊戲和動漫當作廉價靈感，而是進一步抽取其中的空間組織、敘事路徑、邊界、層級和運動體驗。這和康乃爾官網描述的「在類比與數位表現之間流動」、後期鼓勵跨學科探索非常契合。

作品集的價值方向要多具體？

優秀作品集最怕「空」——不是畫面空，而是價值空。很多學生會寫「我希望透過建築改善世界」，但作品裡看不到具體改善什麼、為什麼改善、怎麼改善。這四份作品集的價值方向都很明確：關注身體、審美壓力與結構素描；關注身體經驗、女性處境、自然生長與空間感知；關注人、自然、虛擬文化與空間敘事的關係；以及持續圍繞廚餘、海洋污染、鄉土建築、珊瑚生態與社區教育展開。

生態行動型學生的線索特別穩定：家庭廚餘、村莊系統、海洋垃圾、珊瑚生態、人工礁體、地方建築記憶。這種真實問題意識，正好回應康乃爾影片面試的第二題——描述一件創作項目的設計過程與影響。他不需要用抽象語言證明 impact，因為作品裡的實施照片、合作方、實驗模擬與生態教育本身就是 impact。

作品集是不是「越像建築」越好？

不是。康乃爾建築本科並不要求你在高中階段就做出完美的建築方案；相反地，如果作品集過度成熟、過度模板化、過度像被訓練出來的「標準建築圖」，反而可能失去個人性。如果只用一個詞總結四位學生的共同點，我會選「轉譯」：

  • 把身體、審美壓力與結構觀察，轉譯為繪畫、陶瓷與素描語言；
  • 把運動、電影、生物與宗教空間，轉譯為模型系統；
  • 把遊戲、動漫、生態與虛擬敘事，轉譯為空間路徑；
  • 把家庭生活、海洋經驗與鄉土記憶，轉譯為真實系統與生態模型。

以我 12,000+ 小時設計教學與設計諮詢的經驗來看，這種轉譯能力正是建築教育最核心的能力之一：建築不是簡單畫房子，而是把人的行為、社會結構、材料性能、環境條件和文化記憶重新組織成空間。

準備康乃爾建築本科作品集，該先回答哪三個問題？

很多學生會問一個看似正確、實際很危險的問題：「康乃爾喜歡什麼風格？」從這四份作品集看，康乃爾沒有單一風格——材料感強的作品、計算設計、遊戲敘事、生態行動、文化研究都可以。真正關鍵的是：你有沒有一個能持續發展的個人問題？能不能把它變成觀察、草圖、模型、實驗、圖紙和最終表達？與其先學軟體或模仿某份錄取作品集，不如先回答：

  1. 我長期觀察什麼？一個來自生活、興趣、場地或社會經驗的真實問題。
  2. 我如何把它變成空間？草圖、模型、材料、結構、路徑、光影、尺度、場景。
  3. 這個項目對我或他人有什麼影響？個人成長、社區回應、生態意識、文化記憶、真實實施或公眾教育。

三個問題回答清楚，作品集就會從「作品堆疊」變成「個人系統」。最後再照官網規格剪裁：15–20 張、每個項目最多 2 張、說明交代意圖與過程、標註尺寸媒材與完成情境、不使用 AI 生成圖像，並準備一段 3 分鐘以內、不剪輯的影片面試。
body.en:
This year, four portfolios in completely different styles were all admitted to the Cornell University Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch). Many parents and students, the moment they hear "Cornell undergraduate architecture," react the same way: does the portfolio have to look like professional architecture? Does it need lots of architectural drawings, and impressive renderings? The answer these four portfolios give is the opposite.

They do have models, drawings, sketches, material experiments, and digital modeling. What actually makes them work is not that they "look like an architecture portfolio." Each student translated everyday experience, a way of observing, a system of interests, and a set of value judgments into space. They are not proving that they are already architects. They are proving that they already have the way of thinking it takes to become one.

Rechecked in October 2026: degree structure, portfolio rules, deadlines, and video-interview prompts are updated from the Cornell AAP website. The four students' work is individual cases; before you submit, take the latest notice on the official site as the authority.

What are the official requirements for a Cornell B.Arch portfolio?

ProjectOfficial details
Degree structureA five-year professional degree (B.Arch.), NAAB-accredited, and also listed as a STEM project
Curriculum focusDesign is emphasized, and the curriculum also covers theory, history, technology, representation, and structure. Students communicate ideas through models and drawings, moving between analog and digital representation. The first three years are the core curriculum; the final four semesters encourage work across disciplines
Required materialsPortfolio + video interview, accepted only by upload through Cornell AAP SlideRoom
DeadlinesEarly Decision, first-year applicants: November 1; Regular Decision, first-year applicants: January 2; late submissions are not accepted. Fall 2027 does not accept transfer applications from other institutions
Number of images15–20 images, at most 2 per project
ContentWork that shows the applicant's skills and point of view as a future architecture student: freehand drawing (sketches and finished works), plus painting, ruler-and-compass compositional drawings, design work, sculpture, video, photography, woodworking, and other crafts
Video interviewFilmed continuously, unedited, no more than 3 minutes in total, answering three prompts: How do you express creativity? Describe the design process and impact of one art, design, architecture, or social-action project; why do you want to study architecture?
OriginalityWork may not be outsourced to a third party, and this includes AI-generated images. Team work must credit the collaborators and your own role

The above is from the Cornell AAP undergraduate architecture admissions page and the Cornell AAP Department of Architecture undergraduate project page. The admissions page also lists qualities the college values, such as Expressive Designers, Creative Thinkers, Spatial Changemakers, Cultural Innovators, Rigorous Makers, Empathic Individuals, and Broad Thinkers. It looks at how a student observes, translates, makes, and expresses. A "finished piece of architecture" is not the only thing it looks at.

What do the four portfolios answer in common? Build your own worldview first

The four portfolios could not look more different, and they share one trait: there is a clear "why" behind every project. They are not models made in order to make models, and they are not software shown in order to show software. They start from personal experience, a social issue, an observation of materials, or a cultural memory, and step by step become a spatial system.

The four students are strong in different ways, which shows that Cornell does not admit only one kind of "standard architecture student":

  • Painting and ceramics: oil paint, technical pen, marker, pencil drawing, and ceramics, used to work through the body, aesthetic pressure, and structural observation.
  • Computational design: starting from experiences such as the flight path of a golf ball, the movement of a pet, anxiety about the body in the film "The Substance," and fungal growth, then turning them into model systems and parametric structures.
  • Game narrative: starting from a prison-break series, a Unity escape game, vertical greening, and the castles and temples in games, then extracting spatial organization, narrative paths, and the experience of movement.
  • Ecological action: organized around food waste, ocean pollution, Hakka architecture, coral ecology, and community education, forming one long line of observation and action.

Why not parachute in a concept? The topic has to be about you

The most common problem when students make an architecture portfolio is a topic that is huge and has nothing to do with them. They open with "the future city," "an ecological community," or "sustainable architecture." The concept sounds correct, but the work shows no personal observation, and no reason this student had to make it.

These four portfolios avoid that pitfall. Most of the projects come from real experience: one person starts from anxiety about the body and about beauty, one from the spatial arc of a golf swing, one from sailing and ocean pollution, one from game space and architecture in anime, and one from a family's rural memory and Hakka architecture.

For the painting-and-ceramics student, what most deserves a place in the portfolio is the painting, ceramics, and drawing in the later part, more than the models in the first half. She turns unrealistic standards of beauty into two groups of body images, red and blue. Red points to the pressure that external judgment brings; blue points to self-doubt and anxiety about eating. The architectural elevation sketches show patience, a sense of proportion, and an ability to observe construction. The skeletal drawings show that she can describe a complex structure in detail. That lines up with the freehand drawing, painting, and sculptural media listed on the official site.

The ecological-action student's personal sources are even stronger. The food-waste system comes from watching kitchen scraps being thrown out at home. The ocean-pollution project comes from his own experience as a sailor and a coach. The Hakka architecture research comes from the hometown of his parents' generation and from family memory. What an admissions officer sees is evidence that a student has observed a question for a long time and is willing to act on it. An interchangeable "environmental theme" would not show that.

How does a portfolio show "evidence of process"?

Cornell's site asks the portfolio to include hand drawing, sketches, work in progress, and multiple media. The logic is clear: architectural education looks at how a student develops the work, and the final effect is only part of that reading. All four portfolios keep a large amount of process information:

  • The computational-design student's university summer-school project includes plans, sections, axonometrics, model details, and a final model;
  • The game-narrative student's projects often show the source of the idea, hand drawings, iterations of the model, and a digital extension;
  • The ecological-action student's projects include site photographs, comparisons between experiments, construction methods, and the process of carrying the work out in a community, along with the models;
  • The painting, ceramics, and drawings in the later part of the painting-and-ceramics student's portfolio show a course of visual training, from bodily emotion and the composition of an image to structural observation.

Inside Cornell's 15–20 images, the limit of "at most 2 images per project" means one image presents the finished piece, and the other has to be a carefully chosen frame that best explains how the work was developed. There is no room to pack in every sketch.

How do you prove ability across media? Parametric work has to serve an observation

The site specifically lists freehand drawing, painting, compositional drawings, design, sculpture, photography, woodworking, and other crafts. What Cornell wants to see is breadth of visual and spatial literacy, which reaches wider than fluency in any one piece of software. Almost all four portfolios include physical models, hand drawing, material experiments, digital modeling, or computational design:

  • Unlimited Expansion, by the computational-design student, moves from observing fungal growth into Grasshopper and Kangaroo physics simulation;
  • The game-narrative student extends physical models into Unity game space;
  • The ecological-action student uses Rhino, 3D printing, ceramics, and real ecological materials to study artificial coral reefs;
  • The painting-and-ceramics student uses oil paint, technical pen, marker, pencil drawing, and ceramics to show two-dimensional form and structural observation.

The point is whether the parametric work serves an observed question. Being able to "do parametric design" is not, on its own, the point. The computational design in Unlimited Expansion does a specific job: it extracts curves from forms of biological growth, generates a structure, simulates a membrane roof, and then optimizes that into a porous structure. The technique is the result of thinking. It is not there as a gimmick.

The game-narrative student's strength is imagination across media. He treats games and anime as material to extract from — spatial organization, narrative paths, boundaries, hierarchy, and the experience of movement — which is a step past using them as cheap inspiration. That fits Cornell's description of "moving between analog and digital representation," and the later encouragement of exploration across disciplines.

How specific does a portfolio's direction of values need to be?

What a strong portfolio has most to fear is being "empty": empty of values, while the image itself may be full. Many students write "I hope to improve the world through architecture," but the work never shows what would be improved, why, or how. The direction of values in these four portfolios is specific: attention to the body, aesthetic pressure, and structural drawing; attention to bodily experience, the circumstances women face, natural growth, and spatial perception; attention to the relationship among people, nature, virtual culture, and spatial narrative; and a sustained line through food waste, ocean pollution, vernacular architecture, coral ecology, and community education.

The ecological-action student's thread is especially steady: household food waste, a village system, ocean trash, coral ecology, artificial reefs, and the memory of local architecture. That sense of a real problem answers the second prompt in Cornell's video interview — describe the design process and impact of one creative project. He does not need abstract language to prove impact. The photographs of the work being carried out, the partners, the experimental simulations, and the ecological education are themselves the impact.

Is a portfolio better the more it "looks like architecture"?

No. Cornell undergraduate architecture does not ask you to produce a perfect architectural scheme in high school. A portfolio that is overly finished, overly templated, and overly like a trained set of "standard architectural drawings" can lose what is personal about it. If I had one word for what the four students share, I would choose "translation":

  • translating the body, aesthetic pressure, and structural observation into the language of painting, ceramics, and drawing;
  • translating movement, film, biology, and religious space into model systems;
  • translating games, anime, ecology, and virtual narrative into spatial paths;
  • translating family life, experience of the ocean, and vernacular memory into real systems and ecological models.

From my 12,000+ hours of design teaching and design consulting, this ability to translate is one of the core abilities of an architectural education. Architecture is a matter of reorganizing human behavior, social structure, material performance, environmental conditions, and cultural memory into space, which is a larger task than simply drawing houses.

Preparing a Cornell undergraduate architecture portfolio, which three questions should you answer first?

Many students ask a question that sounds right and is in fact risky: "What style does Cornell like?" From these four portfolios, Cornell has no single style. Work with a strong sense of material, computational design, game narrative, ecological action, and cultural research can all belong. What matters is whether you have a personal question you can keep developing, and whether you can turn it into observation, sketches, models, experiments, drawings, and a final expression. Learning a piece of software, or copying a portfolio that was admitted, can wait until you have answered these:

  1. What have I been observing over a long time? A real question from life, an interest, a site, or social experience.
  2. How do I turn it into space? Sketches, models, materials, structure, paths, light and shadow, scale, scenes.
  3. What impact does this project have on me or on other people? Personal growth, a response from a community, ecological awareness, cultural memory, a real implementation, or public education.

Once those three answers are clear, the portfolio changes from "a stack of work" into "a personal system." Then edit it to the official specification: 15–20 images, at most 2 per project, text that sets out intention and process, dimensions, media, and the circumstances of completion noted, no AI-generated images, and an unedited video interview of no more than 3 minutes.

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾建築本科作品集一定要很像建築作品嗎？
q.en: Does a Cornell undergraduate architecture portfolio have to look like architecture?

a.zh-Hant: 不用。康乃爾 AAP 官網要求作品展現申請者作為未來建築學生的技能與觀點，列出自由手繪、繪畫、構成圖、設計、雕塑、影片、攝影、木工與其他工藝。本文四份錄取作品集分別以繪畫陶瓷、計算設計、遊戲敘事與生態行動為主，共同點是把個人經驗轉譯成空間。
a.en: No. The Cornell AAP site asks for work that shows an applicant's skills and point of view as a future architecture student, and it lists freehand drawing, painting, compositional drawings, design, sculpture, video, photography, woodworking, and other crafts. The four admitted portfolios in this article center on painting and ceramics, computational design, game narrative, and ecological action. What they share is translating personal experience into space.

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾 B.Arch 作品集要放幾張、什麼時候截止？

a.zh-Hant: 15–20 張、每個項目最多 2 張，只接受經 Cornell AAP SlideRoom 上傳；Early Decision 新生 11 月 1 日、Regular Decision 新生 1 月 2 日截止，逾期不收。Fall 2027 不接受外校轉學申請。
a.en: 15–20 images, at most 2 per project, accepted only by upload through Cornell AAP SlideRoom. Early Decision for first-year applicants is November 1, and Regular Decision for first-year applicants is January 2. Late submissions are not accepted. Fall 2027 does not accept transfer applications from other institutions.

q.zh-Hant: 康乃爾 B.Arch 影片面試問什麼？
q.en: What does the Cornell B.Arch video interview ask?

a.zh-Hant: 一段連續拍攝、不剪輯、總長不超過 3 分鐘的影片，回答三題：如何表達創造力？描述一件藝術、設計、建築或社會行動項目的設計過程與影響？為什麼想讀建築？
a.en: One video, filmed continuously and left unedited, with a total length of no more than 3 minutes, answering three questions: How do you express creativity? What was the design process, and what was the impact, of one art, design, architecture, or social-action project? Why do you want to study architecture?

q.zh-Hant: 作品集裡可以放參數化或 Grasshopper 作品嗎？
q.en: Can a portfolio include parametric or Grasshopper work?

a.zh-Hant: 可以，但要服務於一個觀察問題。例如「無限擴張」從真菌生長擷取曲線、生成結構與多孔屋頂，技術是思考的結果；同時須遵守官網規定，不可使用 AI 生成圖像或外包。
a.en: Yes, if it serves an observed question. Unlimited Expansion, for example, extracts curves from fungal growth and then generates a structure and a porous roof. The technique is the result of thinking. The site's rules still apply: no AI-generated images, and no outsourcing.

q.zh-Hant: 準備康乃爾建築作品集應該先做什麼？

a.zh-Hant: 先回答三個問題：我長期觀察什麼？我如何把它變成空間？這個項目對我或他人有什麼影響？再照官網規格剪裁成 15–20 張、每項目最多 2 張，並準備影片面試。
a.en: Answer three questions first: What have I been observing over a long time? How do I turn it into space? What impact does this project have on me or on other people? Then edit to the official specification — 15–20 images, at most 2 per project — and prepare the video interview.

posts.abstract_en: Four very different high-school portfolios were all admitted to the five-year Bachelor of Architecture at Cornell University's College of Architecture, Art, and Planning (AAP): one built on painting, ceramics and structural drawing; one on computational design (a Grasshopper/Kangaroo tensile roof grown from fungal patterns, a golf-ball trajectory stick model); one on game and film narrative (an escape maze later rebuilt as a game level); and one on ecological action (kitchen-waste composting, marine pollution, a Hakka house section model and 3D-printed artificial coral reefs). Their common thread is translation of personal experience into spatial systems, with visible process evidence and a concrete value direction. Facts were checked against Cornell AAP pages in October 2026: NAAB-accredited, STEM-designated B.Arch; portfolio of 15-20 slides with no more than two per project via Cornell AAP SlideRoom, due November 1 (Early Decision) or January 2 (Regular Decision); an unedited video interview of up to three minutes answering three prompts; no outsourcing or AI-generated images.

title.zh-Hant: 錄取卡內基美隆建築本科的作品集：她把橘子、身體、植物與記憶都搭成了空間（2026 年 10 月官方查核）
title.en: A Carnegie Mellon architecture portfolio: how one admitted student built oranges, the body, plants and memory into space (checked October 2026)

summary.zh-Hant: 一份錄取卡內基美隆（CMU）建築本科的作品集，如何對應官網列出的好奇心、空間推理、綜合能力與「動手製作的慾望」？拆解橘子涼亭、生長的支架、灰姑娘等作品，並對照 CMU 官網：10 件作品、經 SlideRoom 提交，ED 11 月 2 日、RD 1 月 8 日截止。
summary.en: How does a portfolio admitted to Carnegie Mellon (CMU) undergraduate architecture meet the curiosity, spatial reasoning, ability to synthesize, and "desire to make" named on the official site? It unpacks the orange pavilion, A Scaffold of Growth, Cinderella, and other works, set against the CMU site: 10 works, submitted through SlideRoom, with Early Decision due November 2 and Regular Decision due January 8.

tldr.zh-Hant: CMU 建築學院本科（B.Arch 五年制 NAAB 認證；B.A. 四年制）申請＝Common App＋SlideRoom 作品集：兩份表單、10 件不同創作、一段簡短影片，可附一件作品的過程記錄；JPG 與影片、不收 PDF、一頁最多 3 張圖。ED 作品集 11 月 2 日、RD 1 月 8 日截止。官網要看好奇心、批判思考、空間推理、綜合能力與動手製作的慾望，且整體編排與單件作品同樣重要。這份錄取作品集用大量手作模型與材料實驗，把橘子、身體、植物與記憶轉譯成空間。
tldr.en: Applying to the CMU School of Architecture as an undergraduate (a five-year NAAB-accredited B.Arch; a four-year B.A.) means the Common App plus a SlideRoom portfolio: two forms, 10 different creative works, and a short video, with the option to attach a process record for one work. JPG and video are accepted, PDF is not, and a page holds at most 3 images. The Early Decision portfolio is due November 2 and the Regular Decision portfolio January 8. The site looks for curiosity, critical thinking, spatial reasoning, the ability to synthesize, and a desire to make by hand, and the overall arrangement matters as much as any single work. This admitted portfolio uses many handmade models and material experiments to translate oranges, the body, plants, and memory into space.

body.zh-Hant:
有些作品集看起來很完整，卻讓人覺得它主要停留在螢幕裡：圖很順、效果也不錯，就是少了一種「這個學生真的動手試過」的痕跡。這份錄取卡內基美隆大學（Carnegie Mellon University，CMU）建築學院本科的作品集不一樣——你能看到木、線、纖維、壓克力、樹脂、黏土、植物、金屬絲被一點點組織起來。它不只是展示結果，而是展示一個學生如何和材料反覆溝通。

這點很 CMU。CMU 建築學院在本科招生頁上明確寫出，作品集要看到申請者 desire to make and build things——不是只會想，而是真的願意把複雜的東西做出來。

2026 年 10 月重新查核：學制、作品集規定、截止日與作品集面談日期，均依 CMU 建築學院官網更新；本文作品屬個人案例，送件前請再以官網最新公告為準。

合作作品鼓勵放入，但須標註為 Collaborative、列出所有參與者，並說明自己的角色
作品集面談非必要但強烈建議：與教師進行 15 分鐘 Zoom 面談，須先送出 Common App 才能報名，名額先到先得

以上出自CMU 建築學院本科招生頁與CMU 建築學院 B.Arch 項目頁。招生頁寫得很直接：作品集要呈現好奇心、批判思考、創新、解決問題、空間推理／視覺思考、綜合能力，以及動手製作與建造的慾望；而且「作品集整體編排的品質，與任何單件作品的品質同樣重要」。

CMU 作品集要怎麼證明「好奇心」？

這份作品集最貼近 CMU 的第一點，是它的好奇心很具體，而不是停在「我對很多東西感興趣」。她會去看咖啡館怎麼把不同材料和光線拼在一起；會去想「居住」和「耕種」能不能在同一個垂直空間裡共生；會去研究二十多種水果的剖面、植物纖維、庭院、城市廣場，甚至身體裡的組織結構，再把這些內容轉譯成模型或裝置。

這種轉譯能力，比單純做得漂不漂亮更重要：它說明她不是在套公式，而是在主動建立自己的設計語言。

為什麼「不是就建築談建築」反而加分？

這不是一本純藝術集，也不是一本純建築集。裡面有空間模型，也有材料實驗、裝置、產品、城市設計、手繪與拼貼，甚至有把身體經驗轉成空間裝置的項目。CMU 招生頁要求選件時「展現多種媒材、二維與三維的關係，以及多樣的主題，同時突出你最強的作品」，這份作品集正好對上。

例如「會呼吸的植物架」不是單純做一個花架，而是從天然纖維與植物出發，做出既有材料實驗、又有空間意味的作品；「生長的支架」則把膝關節韌帶重建手術與 MRI 影像，轉成一個帶有骨架、纏繞與生長感的空間模型。

CMU 說的「空間推理」在作品集裡長什麼樣？

很多學生會畫也會做，卻未必能把二維和三維的關係處理清楚。這份作品集最明顯的例子，是她在大學夏校項目中做的「從圖案到體量」練習：不是把圖案直接複製成立體，而是先分析圖案內部的秩序和關係，再一步步推成體量。

後面的橘子涼亭、灰姑娘，以及建築拼貼和針管筆建築畫，也都能看出她不是在「描一個形」，而是在處理空間裡的層次、穿插、包裹、支撐和節奏。橘子涼亭先研究了二十多種水果的剖面，選定橘子，再把果肉的瓣形化為果園中竹編涼亭的屋頂——從觀察到結構，每一步都看得見。

手作在 CMU 作品集裡有多重要？

CMU 在本科招生頁特別寫出 desire to make and build things，建築學院的使命頁也說明，核心能力的教學建立在「透過繪圖與製作（手工與數位）學習」之上。這本作品集裡有大量需要長時間搭建和推敲的作品：灰姑娘那種藍白透明材料與螺旋上升的空間關係、生長的支架裡的纏繞、支撐與懸掛、永恆花園裡裝置與小尺度人物場景的結合，都不是快速拼出來的東西。它們讓招生官直接感受到：這個學生願意花時間做、肯吃苦，也有處理複雜關係的耐心。

作品集怎麼講出一個完整的個人方向？

CMU 要求學生「仔細策展與編排作品集，講出一個關於你自己、你的能力與熱情、以及你投入建築學習的決心與動機的動人故事」。這份作品集跨了很多媒介，卻不亂：裡面一直有幾條穩定的線索——自然與生命、脆弱與生長、空間與情感、結構與包裹、身體經驗。

它不是每個項目都在展示「我會一個新技能」，而是每個項目都在從不同角度回答「我到底想透過空間表達什麼」。這讓整本作品集不顯得散，反而讓人看見一個完整的學生。

偏藝術裝置的作品集適合申請 CMU 嗎？

這本作品集有些項目更偏藝術裝置，和傳統意義上的建築項目仍有邊界；放到特別強調「建築像不像建築」的學校，未必會被同樣理解。但放在 CMU，這些「不那麼標準」的部分反而成了優勢：官網的 B.Arch 介紹寫明，前三年是高度結構化的基礎課程與設計課，第四、五年則依個人興趣選擇方向，學生可以在永續與計算、都市設計與建築性能等交叉領域打造自己的專長。

以我 12,000+ 小時設計教學與設計諮詢的經驗來看，這份作品集被 CMU 錄取，是因為它非常清楚地讓學校看見三件事：這個學生有真正的好奇心、有跨媒介的空間轉譯能力，也有把想法做出來的執行力——而這三件事，正是 CMU 招生頁列出最看重的能力。

準備 CMU 建築本科作品集的檢查清單

  1. 10 件不同作品：每件都要有自己的觀察起點，避免同一技能重複出現。
  2. 一頁一張圖：需要合併時一頁最多 3 張，JPG 格式，不交 PDF；少放技術製圖。
  3. 媒材與維度要有廣度：手繪、模型、材料實驗、裝置、數位作品都可以，重點是二維與三維之間的關係。
  4. 善用過程記錄：官網允許為其中一件作品附上過程記錄，選最能說明推導邏輯的那件。
  5. 整體敘事：編排順序本身就是作品，讓 10 件作品串成一條個人主線。
  6. 時間點：ED 作品集 11 月 2 日、RD 1 月 8 日（美東 23:59）；送出 Common App 後盡早報名作品集面談。
body.en:
Some portfolios look complete and still feel as if they mostly stayed on a screen. The drawings are smooth and the effects are fine, and what is missing is the trace that "this student really tried it by hand." This portfolio, admitted to the undergraduate degree in the School of Architecture at Carnegie Mellon University (CMU), is different. You can see wood, thread, fiber, acrylic, resin, clay, plants, and metal wire being organized a little at a time. It shows the result and, more than that, how a student communicates with materials again and again.

This is very CMU. On its undergraduate admissions page, the CMU School of Architecture states plainly that a portfolio should show an applicant's desire to make and build things — a real willingness to make complicated things, which goes further than only being able to think.

Rechecked in October 2026: degree structure, portfolio rules, deadlines, and portfolio-interview dates are updated from the CMU School of Architecture website. The work in this article is an individual case; before you submit, take the latest notice on the official site as the authority.

What are the official requirements for a CMU undergraduate architecture portfolio?

ProjectOfficial details
DegreeBachelor of Architecture (B.Arch): a five-year, NAAB-accredited professional degree. Bachelor of Arts in Architecture (B.A.): a four-year pre-professional degree. The application materials for the two are identical. Students are not separated by degree at admission, and they choose by the end of the second year at the latest
Application processTwo steps: first apply to the university with the Common Application and select College of Fine Arts / School of Architecture, then submit the Architecture Portfolio through SlideRoom. Only the portfolio on SlideRoom is reviewed. Physical portfolios are not accepted
DeadlinesEarly Decision: both the Common App and the portfolio on November 2 (the portfolio until 23:59 US Eastern), with decisions on December 15. Regular Decision / transfer: the Common App on January 4, the portfolio on January 8 (23:59 US Eastern), with decisions by April 1
Portfolio contentsFill in two forms, upload 10 different creative works, and record a short video responding to the prompts. You may choose to attach a process record for one of the works
FormatJPG images and video are accepted; PDF is not. One image per page is preferred. If images are combined, at most 3 images per page. A short account of the work's background in the Description field is recommended. Technical drawings are discouraged
Collaborative workIncluding it is encouraged, but it must be marked Collaborative, with every participant listed and your own role explained
Portfolio interviewNot required, but strongly recommended: a 15-minute Zoom interview with a faculty member. The Common App has to be submitted before you can sign up. Places are first come, first served

The above is from the CMU School of Architecture undergraduate admissions page and the CMU School of Architecture B.Arch project page. The admissions page is direct: a portfolio should present curiosity, critical thinking, innovation, problem-solving, spatial reasoning / visual thinking, the ability to synthesize, and a desire to make and build; and "the quality of the portfolio's overall arrangement is as important as the quality of any single work."

How does a CMU portfolio prove "curiosity"?

What comes closest to CMU's first point is that the curiosity here is concrete, and it goes further than "I am interested in lots of things." She looks at how cafés piece different materials and light together. She asks whether "living" and "farming" can coexist in the same vertical space. She studies the sections of more than 20 kinds of fruit, plant fibers, courtyards, city squares, even the tissue structures inside the body, and then translates that material into models or installations.

This ability to translate matters more than whether something is simply made to look beautiful. It shows that she is actively building a design language of her own, which is a further step than applying a formula.

Why does "not talking about architecture only as architecture" count in your favor?

This is not a pure art portfolio, and it is not a pure architecture portfolio. It contains spatial models, and also material experiments, installations, products, urban design, hand drawing, and collage, including projects that turn bodily experience into spatial installations. When it comes to choosing work, the CMU admissions page asks you to "show a range of media, the relationship between two and three dimensions, and a variety of themes, while featuring your strongest work." This portfolio meets that.

A Plant Stand That Breathes, for example, does more than make a flower stand. It starts from natural fiber and plants and makes a work that is a material experiment and also spatially meaningful. A Scaffold of Growth turns ligament-reconstruction surgery of the knee, and MRI images, into a spatial model with a sense of skeleton, winding, and growth.

What does the "spatial reasoning" CMU describes look like in a portfolio?

Many students can draw and can make, and still leave the relationship between two and three dimensions unclear. The clearest example in this portfolio is a "from pattern to volume" exercise she did in a university summer-school project. She analyzes the order and the relationships inside the pattern first, then pushes it step by step into volume, which is a different move from copying the pattern straight into a solid.

The orange pavilion and Cinderella that follow, along with the architectural collages and the technical-pen architectural drawings, also show that she is working with layers, interlocking, wrapping, support, and rhythm in space, which is a different task from "tracing a shape." The orange pavilion begins with sections of more than 20 kinds of fruit, settles on the orange, and turns the segments of the flesh into the roof of a bamboo-woven pavilion in an orchard. From observation to structure, every step is visible.

How important is making by hand in a CMU portfolio?

On the undergraduate admissions page, CMU specifically names a desire to make and build things, and the School of Architecture's mission page also explains that teaching of the core abilities is built on "learning through drawing and making (by hand and digitally)." This portfolio contains a great deal of work that takes a long time to build and to refine: the relationship, in Cinderella, between transparent blue-and-white material and a spiraling ascent; the winding, support, and suspension in A Scaffold of Growth; the joining of an installation and a small-scale figure scene in The Garden of Eternity. None of these is something assembled quickly. They let an admissions officer feel directly that this student is willing to spend time making, willing to take on hard work, and patient with complicated relationships.

How does a portfolio tell a complete personal direction?

CMU asks students to "curate and arrange the portfolio with care, and tell a moving story about yourself, your abilities and passions, and the resolve and motivation you bring to studying architecture." This portfolio crosses many media and stays coherent. A few stable threads run through it: nature and life, fragility and growth, space and emotion, structure and wrapping, bodily experience.

Each project answers, from a different angle, "what do I actually want to express through space?" That is a different job from every project showing "I can do a new skill." The whole portfolio holds together, and you can see one complete student.

Is a portfolio that leans toward art installation suitable for applying to CMU?

Some projects in this portfolio lean further toward art installation, and a boundary remains with architectural projects in the traditional sense. At a school that particularly stresses "whether the architecture looks like architecture," they would not necessarily be understood in the same way. At CMU, these "less standard" parts become an advantage. The B.Arch introduction on the site states that the first three years are a highly structured set of foundation courses and design courses, and that the fourth and fifth years are a direction chosen according to personal interest. Students can build their own expertise in intersecting fields such as sustainability and computation, or urban design and building performance.

From my 12,000+ hours of design teaching and design consulting, this portfolio was admitted to CMU because it lets the school see three things very clearly: this student has real curiosity, an ability to translate space across media, and the execution to make an idea. Those three things are exactly the abilities the CMU admissions page lists as what it weighs most.

A checklist for preparing a CMU undergraduate architecture portfolio

  1. 10 different works: each one needs its own observation to start from, so the same skill does not appear again.
  2. One image per page: when images need to be combined, at most 3 per page, in JPG, with no PDF. Include few technical drawings.
  3. Breadth of media and dimension: hand drawing, models, material experiments, installations, and digital work can all belong. What matters is the relationship between two and three dimensions.
  4. Use the process record well: the site allows a process record for one of the works. Choose the one that best explains the logic of how it was developed.
  5. An overall narrative: the order itself is part of the work. Let the 10 works form one personal line.
  6. Timing: the ED portfolio is due November 2 and the RD portfolio January 8 (23:59 US Eastern). After the Common App is submitted, sign up for the portfolio interview as early as you can.

q.zh-Hant: CMU 建築本科作品集要交幾件作品？
q.en: How many works does a CMU undergraduate architecture portfolio require?

a.zh-Hant: 依 CMU 建築學院官網，Architecture Portfolio 需在 SlideRoom 填寫兩份表單、上傳 10 件不同的創作作品，並錄一段回應題目的簡短影片；可選擇為其中一件作品附上過程記錄。接受 JPG 與影片，不收 PDF。
a.en: According to the CMU School of Architecture website, the Architecture Portfolio requires two forms filled in on SlideRoom, 10 different creative works uploaded, and a short video responding to the prompts. You may choose to attach a process record for one of the works. JPG and video are accepted; PDF is not.

q.zh-Hant: CMU 建築本科作品集什麼時候截止？
q.en: When is the deadline for a CMU undergraduate architecture portfolio?

a.zh-Hant: Early Decision：Common App 與作品集皆 11 月 2 日（作品集至美東 23:59），12 月 15 日公布結果；Regular Decision 與轉學：Common App 1 月 4 日、作品集 1 月 8 日（美東 23:59），最晚 4 月 1 日公布。
a.en: Early Decision: both the Common App and the portfolio are due November 2 (the portfolio until 23:59 US Eastern), with decisions released December 15. Regular Decision and transfer: the Common App is due January 4 and the portfolio January 8 (23:59 US Eastern), with decisions released by April 1.

q.zh-Hant: CMU 的 B.Arch 和 B.A. 要分開申請嗎？
q.en: Do CMU's B.Arch and B.A. require separate applications?

a.zh-Hant: 不用。兩個學位的申請材料完全相同，錄取時不分學位；學生最晚在第二年結束前選擇五年制、NAAB 認證的 B.Arch，或四年制的 B.A. in Architecture。
a.en: No. The application materials for the two degrees are identical, and admission does not separate them by degree. By the end of the second year at the latest, students choose the five-year, NAAB-accredited B.Arch or the four-year B.A. in Architecture.

q.zh-Hant: CMU 建築作品集最看重什麼？
q.en: What does a CMU architecture portfolio weigh most heavily?

a.zh-Hant: 官網列出好奇心、批判思考、創新、解決問題、空間推理／視覺思考、綜合能力，以及動手製作與建造的慾望；並強調作品集整體編排的品質與單件作品同樣重要，要講出關於自己、能力與熱情的故事。
a.en: The site lists curiosity, critical thinking, innovation, problem-solving, spatial reasoning / visual thinking, the ability to synthesize, and a desire to make and build. It also stresses that the quality of the portfolio's overall arrangement matters as much as any single work, and that the portfolio should tell a story about you, your abilities, and your passions.

q.zh-Hant: CMU 作品集面談一定要參加嗎？
q.en: Do you have to attend the CMU portfolio interview?

a.zh-Hant: 不是必要，但官網強烈建議。這是與教師進行的 15 分鐘 Zoom 面談，須先送出 Common App 才能報名，名額有限、先到先得。
a.en: It is not required, but the site strongly recommends it. It is a 15-minute Zoom interview with a faculty member. You must submit the Common App before you can sign up. Places are limited and filled first come, first served.

posts.abstract_en: An admitted portfolio for Carnegie Mellon University's School of Architecture undergraduate program, read against what CMU says it looks for: curiosity, critical thinking, innovation, problem-solving, spatial reasoning and visual thinking, ability to synthesize, and the desire to make and build things. The student's projects - a composite cafe, a living-and-farming tower, a fibre-cement plant stand, a clay-and-wire viewing tower inspired by knee-ligament reconstruction, a paper-and-resin fairy-tale tower, a mourning garden and a bamboo pavilion derived from mandarin segments - are hand-built, cross-media and tied together by themes of nature, growth, the body and memory. Facts checked on CMU pages in October 2026: five-year NAAB-accredited B.Arch and four-year B.A., same application, degree chosen by the end of year two; Common App plus SlideRoom portfolio of two forms, ten creative works and a short video; JPG/video only, no PDF; Early Decision deadline November 2, Regular Decision portfolio January 8; optional but strongly recommended 15-minute portfolio review interview.

title.zh-Hant: 加州藝術學院 CCA 2027 年停辦、校園轉給范德堡：藝術與建築申請者該怎麼選校？（2026 年 10 月官方查核）
title.en: CCA closes in 2027 and its campus goes to Vanderbilt: what art, design and architecture applicants should do (checked October 2026)

summary.zh-Hant: 加州藝術學院（CCA）將在 2026–27 學年結束時關閉，舊金山校園由范德堡大學接手，並成立 Huang 藝術、建築與設計學院。CCA 已不收新生；建築系 B.Arch 與 M.Arch 已獲 NAAB 核准轉移至范德堡。本文整理官方資訊與 2027 秋季選校建議。
summary.en: California College of the Arts (CCA) will close at the end of the 2026–27 academic year. Vanderbilt University is taking over the San Francisco campus and will establish the Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design. CCA is no longer admitting new students, and NAAB has approved transferring the architecture B.Arch and M.Arch to Vanderbilt. This post gathers the official information and school-selection advice for fall 2027.

tldr.zh-Hant: CCA 已於 2026 年 1 月 13 日宣布，將在 2026–27 學年結束時關閉，目前不接受任何申請。在讀生可在 CCA 讀到 2027 年春季，之後可走 ArtCenter、CalArts、CSU East Bay、Pratt、SF State、SVA、University of Redlands LA 等 teach-out 銜接（須 2027 春季仍在 CCA 註冊）。CCA 學生不會自動轉入范德堡；唯一例外是建築：NAAB 已核准把 CCA 的 B.Arch 與 M.Arch 轉移到范德堡並給予四年持續認證。范德堡舊金山校區預計 2027 年秋季開學、約 1,000 名學生，旗艦學院為 Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design，但科系、截止日與作品集要求截至 2026 年 10 月尚未公布。
tldr.en: On January 13, 2026, CCA announced that it will close at the end of the 2026–27 academic year and that it is not accepting any applications. Continuing students may study at CCA through spring 2027, then use teach-out pathways with ArtCenter, CalArts, CSU East Bay, Pratt, SF State, SVA, and University of Redlands Los Angeles, provided they are still enrolled at CCA in spring 2027. CCA students do not transfer automatically to Vanderbilt. The only exception is architecture: NAAB has approved transferring CCA’s B.Arch and M.Arch to Vanderbilt with four years of continuing accreditation. Vanderbilt’s San Francisco campus is expected to open in fall 2027 with about 1,000 students. Its flagship is the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design, but as of October 2026 the programmes, deadlines, and portfolio requirements had not been published.

body.zh-Hant:
2026 年 1 月 13 日，創校於 1907 年、位於舊金山的加州藝術學院（California College of the Arts，CCA）宣布與范德堡大學（Vanderbilt University）達成協議：CCA 會逐步結束營運，在 2026–27 學年結束時關閉，舊金山校園之後由范德堡接手，並在同一地點開辦包含藝術、建築與設計的大學部與研究所課程。

這篇文章不談八卦，只回答準備申請藝術、設計、建築的學生和家長最在意的幾件事：CCA 現在還能申請嗎？已經在讀的學生怎麼辦？范德堡舊金山校區到底會開什麼？以及這件事對選校有什麼啟示。以下資訊皆於 2026 年 10 月重新對照 CCA 與范德堡官網。

文首封面是 CCA 現在的舊金山校園，也就是未來的范德堡舊金山校區（Vanderbilt University–San Francisco）預定地。圖片來源：Vanderbilt University 官網

CCA 現在還能申請嗎？

不能。CCA 招生頁目前明確寫著：學校不再接受、也不再審查任何申請，不會再招收新的入學班級。換句話說，2027 年秋季入學的申請季，CCA 已經不在選項裡。如果你的選校清單還列著 CCA，請直接刪除，並把時間放在下面提到的替代方案上。

已經在 CCA 就讀的學生怎麼辦？

依 CCA 官方公告，學校會持續授課到 2026–27 學年結束，預計能在這段時間內完成學業的學生，可以照原計畫拿到 CCA 學位。需要更多時間的學生，CCA 已和多所學校簽訂正式的 teach-out（銜接完成學業）協議。依 CCA 官方說明（2026 年 10 月 12 日更新），合作學校包括：

  • ArtCenter College of Design（ArtCenter）
  • California Institute of the Arts（CalArts）
  • California State University, East Bay
  • Pratt Institute
  • San Francisco State University
  • School of Visual Arts（SVA）
  • University of Redlands, Los Angeles（原 Woodbury University）

要注意兩個條件：第一，想保留正式銜接資格，必須在 2027 年春季學期仍在 CCA 註冊；第二，這些協議是在 CCA 關閉後才生效，而且每個科系對應的合作學校不同，要按自己的主修逐一查。

另一個常見誤會是「范德堡接手校園，所以學生會自動轉成范德堡學生」。CCA 官方 FAQ 說得很清楚：范德堡在 2027 年秋季開辦的是一個新機構，有自己的課程、畢業要求與招生流程，CCA 學生不會自動轉入，想讀必須另外申請。

建築系學生有什麼不同？

建築是唯一的例外，也是這次最值得建築申請者注意的更新。美國建築認證委員會（NAAB）已核准把 CCA 經認證的 B.Arch（建築學士）與 M.Arch（建築碩士）轉移到范德堡大學，並給予兩個學位四年的持續認證。

在其餘學校與監管核准完成的前提下，范德堡打算讓 2026–27 學年仍在 CCA 就讀、而且預計畢業時間超過 CCA 關閉日的 B.Arch 與 M.Arch 學生，可以在范德堡舊金山校區（Vanderbilt University–San Francisco）繼續完成學位；資格會依學生在 CCA 的學業表現而定。對建築生來說，這代表 NAAB 認證不會因為學校關閉而中斷，這是考照路徑上最關鍵的一點。

范德堡舊金山校區會開什麼課？什麼時候能申請？

依范德堡官網，舊金山校區預計在 2027 年秋季（2027–28 學年）開始招收學生，前提是取得必要的監管核准；規模預計約 1,000 名大學部與研究生。2026 年 7 月，范德堡進一步宣布以黃仁勳與黃柏薇（Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang）家族 7,500 萬美元的配對捐款為基礎，成立 Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design，作為舊金山校區的旗艦學院，目前捐款帶動的總投入已超過 1 億美元。

官網描述的方向是：以先進科技結合藝術與建築的基礎訓練，透過工作室實作與設計實驗室培養技術與視覺能力，再加上創新與工程的商業、技術素養。大學部課程強調密集的工作室實作，以及學徒制、實習等體驗式學習；研究所則是以工作室為核心、研究導向並連結職涯。

但請注意：截至 2026 年 10 月，具體科系清單、申請截止日與作品集要求都還沒有公布，學院院長也仍在全國公開招聘中。官網目前只說明，大學部申請者會透過既有的申請平台直接申請舊金山校區，並在申請時選擇該校區預計開設的科系，整體仍屬於范德堡的大學部招生框架；更多細節「即將公布」。

2027 秋季申請者該怎麼調整選校清單？

根據 12,000+ 小時設計教學與設計諮詢的經驗，我會建議這樣處理：

  1. 原本把 CCA 當主要目標的學生：把預算與志趣相近的學校補進清單。CCA 的強項在於設計、建築、藝術並存於同一所獨立藝術學院，可以優先比較同樣類型的院校，例如官方 teach-out 名單中的 ArtCenter、CalArts、Pratt、SVA，再依主修檢查課程是否對口。
  2. 對范德堡舊金山有興趣的學生：可以列入觀察名單，但不要把它當成唯一的保底或主力。科系、截止日、作品集規格都還沒公布，作品集請先照一般藝術／建築本科的標準準備，等官方公布後再微調。
  3. 建築申請者：B.Arch 與 M.Arch 已取得 NAAB 持續認證，是新校區目前最明確的項目。若你以考取美國建築師執照為目標，可以持續追蹤這兩個學位的招生公告。
  4. 所有申請者：把「學校財務與體質」納入選校考量。CCA 校長在公告中直說，依賴學費的營運模式已無法持續。選擇小型獨立藝術學院時，可以留意招生規模的變化、是否隸屬於綜合大學，以及學校公開的發展規劃。

CCA 的資源會消失嗎？

不會完全消失。依雙方公告，范德堡計畫成立 CCA Institute at Vanderbilt，納入 CCA 的瓦蒂斯當代藝術中心（Wattis Institute for Contemporary Arts）、保存 CCA 的檔案資料，並作為校友連結的平台；范德堡也會支持紀念 CCA 歷史的展覽與活動。對已畢業的 CCA 校友而言，學位與校友網絡仍然有延續的管道。

結論：一所學校關閉，選校邏輯要跟著更新

CCA 停辦提醒我們，選校不只是看排名與作品風格，也要看學校能不能陪你走完四到五年。對藝術與設計生而言，2027 秋季的最佳做法是：把 CCA 從清單移除、用定位相近的學校補位，並把范德堡舊金山與它的 Huang 藝術建築設計學院列為值得追蹤的新選項——等科系與作品集要求正式公布，再決定要不要投入。
body.en:
On January 13, 2026, California College of the Arts (CCA), founded in 1907 and based in San Francisco, announced an agreement with Vanderbilt University: CCA will wind down and close at the end of the 2026–27 academic year. Vanderbilt will then take over the San Francisco campus and, on the same site, offer undergraduate and graduate programmes in art, architecture, and design.

This article is not about gossip. It answers the questions that matter most to students and parents preparing applications in art, design, and architecture: Can you still apply to CCA? What happens to students who are already enrolled? What will Vanderbilt’s San Francisco campus actually offer? And what does this change about how you build a school list? Everything below was checked again against the CCA and Vanderbilt websites in October 2026.

The cover image is CCA’s current San Francisco campus, the planned site of Vanderbilt University–San Francisco. Image source: Vanderbilt University

Can you still apply to CCA?

No. CCA’s admissions page currently states, in plain terms, that the school no longer accepts or reviews any applications and will not admit another entering class. In other words, for the fall 2027 application season, CCA is no longer an option. If CCA is still on your list, take it off and put that time into the alternatives below.

What happens to students who are already at CCA?

According to CCA’s official announcement, the school will keep teaching through the end of the 2026–27 academic year. Students who can finish in that time may graduate with a CCA degree as planned. For students who need longer, CCA has signed formal teach-out agreements with several schools. As of CCA’s official update on October 12, 2026, the partner schools are:

  • ArtCenter College of Design (ArtCenter)
  • California Institute of the Arts (CalArts)
  • California State University, East Bay
  • Pratt Institute
  • San Francisco State University
  • School of Visual Arts (SVA)
  • University of Redlands, Los Angeles (formerly Woodbury University)

Two conditions matter. First, to keep a formal teach-out place you must still be enrolled at CCA in the spring 2027 term. Second, the agreements take effect only after CCA closes, and the partner school differs by major, so you have to check the match for your own programme.

A common misunderstanding is that, because Vanderbilt is taking over the campus, students will automatically become Vanderbilt students. CCA’s official FAQ is clear: what Vanderbilt opens in fall 2027 is a new institution, with its own curriculum, graduation requirements, and admissions process. CCA students will not transfer automatically. If you want to study there, you have to apply.

What is different for architecture students?

Architecture is the only exception, and it is the update architecture applicants should pay the most attention to. The National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB) has approved transferring CCA’s accredited B.Arch (Bachelor of Architecture) and M.Arch (Master of Architecture) to Vanderbilt University, with four years of continuing accreditation for both degrees.

Once the remaining institutional and regulatory approvals are in place, Vanderbilt intends to let B.Arch and M.Arch students who are still enrolled at CCA in 2026–27, and whose expected graduation falls after CCA’s closing date, finish their degrees at Vanderbilt University–San Francisco. Eligibility will depend on a student’s academic record at CCA. For architecture students, this means NAAB accreditation does not stop because the school is closing. That is the point that matters most on the path to licensure.

What will Vanderbilt’s San Francisco campus teach, and when can you apply?

According to Vanderbilt’s website, the San Francisco campus expects to begin enrolling students in fall 2027 (the 2027–28 academic year), provided it receives the necessary regulatory approvals, at a scale of about 1,000 undergraduate and graduate students. In July 2026 Vanderbilt further announced the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design as the flagship college of the San Francisco campus, founded on a $75 million matching gift from the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang family. The gift has already brought the total commitment to more than $100 million.

The direction described on the official site is to combine advanced technology with foundational training in art and architecture, to build technical and visual skill through studio work and design labs, and to add the business and technical literacy of innovation and engineering. The undergraduate curriculum emphasizes intensive studio practice and experiential learning such as apprenticeships and internships. Graduate study is studio-centred, research-driven, and tied to professional practice.

One caution: as of October 2026, the specific list of programmes, application deadlines, and portfolio requirements have not been published, and the college is still running a national search for a dean. The site currently says only that undergraduate applicants will apply directly to the San Francisco campus through the existing application platform and, in the application, choose a programme the campus expects to offer. The whole process still sits inside Vanderbilt’s undergraduate admissions framework. Further detail is “coming soon.”

How should fall 2027 applicants adjust their school lists?

From 12,000+ hours of design teaching and design consultation, this is how I would handle it:

  1. If CCA was a primary target: add schools that are close in cost and in what you want to study. CCA’s strength was housing design, architecture, and art in one independent art college. Start with schools of a similar kind on the official teach-out list—ArtCenter, CalArts, Pratt, and SVA—then check, major by major, whether the curriculum actually matches.
  2. If you are interested in Vanderbilt San Francisco: put it on a watch list, but do not treat it as your only safety or your only first choice. Programmes, deadlines, and portfolio specifications have not been published. Prepare the portfolio to the usual standard for an undergraduate art or architecture application, and adjust once the official requirements are out.
  3. If you are applying in architecture: the B.Arch and M.Arch already have NAAB continuing accreditation, and they are the most clearly defined offerings the new campus has announced so far. If your goal is to qualify for an architect’s license in the United States, keep following the admissions announcements for these two degrees.
  4. For every applicant: include a school’s finances and institutional health in the decision. CCA’s president said directly in the announcement that a tuition-dependent operating model was no longer sustainable. When you look at a small independent art college, pay attention to whether enrollment is changing, whether the school belongs to a larger university, and what development plans it has published.

Will CCA’s resources disappear?

Not entirely. Under the announcements from both sides, Vanderbilt plans to establish the CCA Institute at Vanderbilt, which will include CCA’s Wattis Institute for Contemporary Arts, preserve CCA’s archives, and serve as a platform for alumni. Vanderbilt will also support exhibitions and events that mark CCA’s history. For CCA alumni who have already graduated, the degree and the alumni network still have a way to continue.

Conclusion: when a school closes, the logic of choosing a school has to change with it

CCA’s closure is a reminder that choosing a school is not only about rankings and the look of the work. It is also about whether the school can stay with you for four or five years. For art and design students, the best move for fall 2027 is to take CCA off the list, replace it with schools in a similar position, and keep Vanderbilt San Francisco and its Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design on the list of new options worth watching—then decide whether to commit once the programmes and portfolio requirements are officially published.

q.zh-Hant: CCA 加州藝術學院還能申請 2027 秋季入學嗎？
q.en: Can you still apply to California College of the Arts (CCA) for fall 2027?

a.zh-Hant: 不能。CCA 招生頁說明學校不再接受或審查任何申請，也不會再招收新的入學班級；學校將在 2026–27 學年結束時關閉。
a.en: No. CCA’s admissions page states that the school no longer accepts or reviews any applications and will not admit another entering class. The school will close at the end of the 2026–27 academic year.

q.zh-Hant: CCA 在讀生會自動變成范德堡學生嗎？
q.en: Will current CCA students automatically become Vanderbilt students?

a.zh-Hant: 不會。范德堡在舊金山開辦的是新機構，有自己的課程、畢業要求與招生流程，CCA 學生須另外申請。例外是建築：NAAB 已核准 CCA 的 B.Arch 與 M.Arch 轉移到范德堡，符合資格的建築生預計可在范德堡舊金山校區完成學位（仍待其餘核准）。
a.en: No. What Vanderbilt is opening in San Francisco is a new institution, with its own curriculum, graduation requirements, and admissions process. CCA students must apply separately. The exception is architecture: NAAB has approved transferring CCA’s B.Arch and M.Arch to Vanderbilt, and eligible architecture students are expected to be able to finish their degrees at the Vanderbilt San Francisco campus (still subject to the remaining approvals).

q.zh-Hant: CCA 的 teach-out 合作學校有哪些？
q.en: Which schools are CCA’s teach-out partners?

a.zh-Hant: 依 CCA 官方 2026 年 10 月 12 日更新：ArtCenter、CalArts、CSU East Bay、Pratt Institute、SF State、SVA、University of Redlands Los Angeles（原 Woodbury University）。學生須在 2027 春季仍在 CCA 註冊才保有正式銜接資格，各科系對應學校不同。
a.en: According to CCA’s official update of October 12, 2026: ArtCenter, CalArts, CSU East Bay, Pratt Institute, SF State, SVA, and University of Redlands Los Angeles (formerly Woodbury University). Students must still be enrolled at CCA in spring 2027 to keep a formal teach-out place, and the partner school differs by major.

q.zh-Hant: 范德堡舊金山校區什麼時候開學？可以申請哪些科系？
q.en: When does Vanderbilt’s San Francisco campus open, and which programmes can you apply for?

a.zh-Hant: 范德堡預計 2027 年秋季開放學生入學（待監管核准），約 1,000 名大學部與研究生，旗艦學院為 Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design。截至 2026 年 10 月，具體科系、截止日與作品集要求尚未公布；大學部將透過既有申請平台直接申請舊金山校區並選擇科系。
a.en: Vanderbilt expects to enroll students in fall 2027 (subject to regulatory approval): about 1,000 undergraduates and graduate students. The flagship college is the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design. As of October 2026, the specific programmes, deadlines, and portfolio requirements had not been published. Undergraduates will apply directly to the San Francisco campus through the existing application platform and choose a programme at that campus.
